## Update — 28 Oct 2026 (360): Thor charged to 100 % — charge limit fixed so it can't give up

**What happened (Thor, 27 Oct, read from its logs and Voltcap's charge log):** plugged in at 1 % at 19:41. At 20:09
Android's own app backup ran on Voltcap and ended it; at 20:09:52 AYN's root service (pservice) crashed too. Voltcap
came back at 20:10, looked for the root service once, didn't find it, and kept that answer for the whole run: the charge
limit took the Thor for a handheld with no charge switch and switched itself off. It charged to 100 % by 21:22,
unplugged at 21:35 and ran down to 88 % overnight. Since 08:24 it's plugged in again and held at 88 %.

**Fixed (on main, not released yet):**
- The root service is looked up again when it's missing or has gone away (at most every 5 s), and a call that hits a
  dead service looks it up and tries once more.
- The charge limit no longer settles on "no switch" on an AYN handheld while its root service is out of reach; it tries
  again on the next battery change and keeps its service running.
- Calls to AYN's service go one at a time (its crash was inside its request handling; Voltcap's charge limit, tuner and
  stick lights could call it at the same time). Not proven to be the cause.
- Checked on the Thor: after two restarts of Voltcap (installs) the stop stays set and the battery stays at 88 %.

## Update — 27 Oct 2026 (354): permanent rule — no text cut short with "…"

- **New permanent rule** (CLAUDE.md #11, QA rule R18): Voltcap never shortens text with "..." / "…". Text wraps, uses its
  space better, shrinks to a size that stays readable, or slides along slowly so all of it can be read. Only where a hard
  limit can't be changed is it shortened, and then the full text is still reachable (focus, scrolling, a detail view).
  Ellipses that belong to the text itself stay.
- **New shared piece `FullText`** (`ui\FitText.kt`): wraps → shrinks readably → slides; used instead of "…".
- **Fixed now:** the 10 category-screen looks and Customize consoles (13 places).
- **QA:** `static_checks.py` TRUNCATE lists every remaining "…" cut: **585 places** left in older screens. They're fixed
  as each screen is worked on, and the count is reported until it's zero. New code adds none.
- Compiled (release build). Not checked on the Thor: its battery ran out.

## Update — 27 Oct 2026 (350, pass 2): Classic much smoother — the colour glide rebuilt the whole home screen every frame

Second QA pass on the Thor (Classic). Details: `tools\qa\REPORT.md` (pass 2), `defects.json` D17, D20–D25.
- **Smoother navigation, measured on the Thor with the same scenarios as the first baseline.**
  - Janky frames: 7.4 % → 1.6 % while moving, 5.9 % → 1.7 % with rapid input.
  - p90 frame time: 19 → 12 ms. p99: 26 → 19 ms.
  - Video hitches in the recorded run: 24 → 2.
  - Cause: the theme colours glide for 600 ms after each game change, and everything that read them in composition was
    rebuilt on every frame of it — the home screen ~110×/s, the game cards ~1000×/s. Now one rebuild per button press.
    The glide itself is unchanged.
  - How: the colours are read while drawing through the new `ShelfTheme.live`.
  - Files: `ui\theme\ShelfColors.kt`, `ui\theme\Theme.kt`, `ui\GameCard.kt`, `ui\LauncherScreen.kt`, `ui\EdgeBump.kt`,
    `ui\StatusLooks.kt`, `ui\LivingLibrary.kt`, `ui\TileHome.kt`, `ui\FocusEffects.kt` (softGlowLive, pulseBorderLive),
    and AccentIcon in GameCard.
- **Empty frame before the category slide** (`ui\GameDock.kt`): gone. Checked frame by frame on a 120 fps recording.
- **Tile home "Middle"** (`ui\LauncherScreen.kt`, `ui\TileHome.kt`): the tiles now sit in the middle of the screen.
- **Template pictures** (`ui\ResImages.kt` new; CoverCases, RealMedia, PhysicalMedia, StyleCardboardBox, TvRoomHome,
  FramesScene): case, cartridge and box frames are decoded once and shared, not again in every card.
- **Start-up** (`data\SecureStore.kt`): an already-open account store no longer waits for another one being opened.
  Still open: the first frame waits ~0.3 s for 3 account stores (D24).
- **QA system tested against injected faults** (test builds only, `ui\QaFault.kt`). Recordings capture every frame
  (1391/1391). These were all caught:
  - single-frame flashes (11/11, no false alarms);
  - injected stalls (6/6);
  - wrong focus moves (2/2);
  - a re-introduced category-switch flash (2/2).
- **New QA tools**:
  - `ui\QaInval.kt` names the state that makes a part rebuild.
  - Device scripts `rc.sh`, `churn.sh`, `tcold.sh`, and `vqa.sh memtest`.
  - Static rule THEME-COMPOSE (R10).
  - The churn observer that made the app crawl during testing (D21) is now opt-in only.
- **Not done yet**: other layouts, R1 / Settings / dialogs walked with the controller on the device, game launch and
  return, second screen, the calm-idle redraws (D18).

Toni's brief "VoltCap — Complete Autonomous App QA, Visual Inspection & Optimization System". First pass on the Thor
(Classic layout); everything is in `tools\qa\` (README = how to run, RULES = bug patterns, defects.json, REPORT.md).

  120 fps recordings, frame stats, Perfetto, memory, a whole `suite`), `tools\frames.py` (finds 1–3-frame flashes, blank

  neo-retro's aluminium LED rail, the bartop's plywood). New proportions from the real machines: classic upright 0.66 ×
  0.87 × 1.87 m (vertical front with coin door, deck ~1 m, screen ~22° in a recess, angled speaker panel, marquee box,
  slanting back); candy 0.73 × 0.86 × 1.50 m one rounded shell (seated deck at 0.75 m, knee recess, screen ~31°, lit
  header, rounded top); neo-retro 0.78 × 0.90 × 1.72 m (lower body leaning forward, near-upright screen, speaker
  header); bartop on a wooden game table (0.80 m). Each its own side treatment: full side art on the upright and
  bartop, a framed art panel on the neo, the candy's two-tone stripe.

  glows), faces darker towards the floor, fine edge highlights, layered contact shadows, brushed coin doors and kick
  plate, speaker grilles, the glass recessed in a bezel with its top in shadow and a soft reflection, a printed control

## Update — 26 Oct 2026 (344): seven console-inspired layouts — Blades, Bubble home, Pocket camera, Panel dashboard, Game magazine, Rental shop, Terminal

Toni's brief ("8 new console & ES-DE inspired layouts", with the concept board). Original names, drawings and sounds only
(no console names, logos, avatars or third-party theme assets). The Dreamcast one was skipped (Toni: "skip if it's too
same"): Airy home (1999) already is the light, bubbly, VMU-display layout. Each layout is a style home with its own keys,
its own game window (WinScenesConsole.kt), status bar look, R1 rules, presets, preset drawing, option icon and Layout
options; all keep Endless, L2 / R2, X favourite, Y achievements, Start = quick menu, Select = sort & filter, touch, and
come back where you were after a game (StyleRestore).
- **Blades (2005)** (`ui\StyleBlades.kt`): five overlapping blades with curved leading edges — Spotlight, Games, Systems,
  Media, Settings; ◀ ▶ slide the next one open (the stack glides, the content cross-slides), ▲ ▼ its list. Games: the
  category list with a lit bar, the game in your game look, console, play time, achievements and their badges. Systems:
  consoles with logos, counts, console pictures (A opens its games, B back). Spotlight: last played, achievements,
  statistics, search, a gamer card. Window: one more blade sliding in (the "guide"). Options: colour (green, silver, blue,
  orange, theme), start blade, badges, moving light, sounds.
- **Bubble home (2011)** (`ui\StyleBubbles.kt`): glossy game bubbles in staggered rows (5 / 4 / 5, 4 across on
  narrower screens), pages running downwards with dots, the one you're on swelling and bobbing, its name in a pill at the
  top. A unfolds the game's **LiveArea**: layered art, its bubble and name, a big Start, round Achievements / Details /
  Options buttons, screenshots (shown once loaded), achievements with badges and facts; ◀ ▶ (on Start) the next game's
  page, ▼ the round buttons; the page's corner is curled — B, a tap or a drag on it peels the page back. Folders: B on the
  bubbles shows your consoles as folder bubbles. Options: open on the bubbles or straight into the LiveArea, wallpaper
  (sky, sunset, mint, night, the game's art), folders, floating, sounds. Distinct from Airy home (round, glossy, paged).
- **Pocket camera (1998)** (`ui\StylePocketCamera.kt`, `ui\DitherArt.kt`): four shades of chunky pixels — the game as a
  dithered photo (Bayer, levels stretched) in a thick-framed viewfinder with "POCKET CAMERA" and its photo number, name,
  year, console, pixel icons for achievements / time; the album (4 before, 4 after) either side. ◀ ▶ games, ▲ ▼ the photo
  (cover / screenshot / artwork), shutter or develop transitions. Window: the camera menu with a ► cursor. Palettes:
  classic green, pocket grey, sepia, blue, red, backlit.
- **Panel dashboard (2008)** (`ui\StylePanels.kt`): channels of angled panels — Spotlight, My games, Systems, Media,
  Settings — the one you're on big at the front, the rest receding to the right, turned away; the channels above / below
  smaller and dimmed; your profile (RA picture, name, points) on the left on wide screens. Game panels: the game's art
  softened behind your game look. Window: a detail panel swinging round to face you. Colours: green, silver, graphite, theme.
- **Game magazine** (`ui\StyleMagazine.kt`): each category an issue open on a desk, each game a spread — art page with
  headline, kicker and a "product shot" in your look; story page with a drop cap, screenshots, VERDICT burst (critics'
  score or time played), ACHIEVEMENTS and THE STATS boxes, running foot and page numbers. ◀ ▶ turn the page (it lifts at
  the spine and turns over), ▲ the CONTENTS page (A turns to a game). Window: a torn-out page with a PLAY burst and
  callouts. Styles: bold 90s ("PRESS START"), glossy 2000s ("LEVEL UP"), 80s computer mag ("HIGH SCORE").
- **Rental shop** (`ui\StyleRentalShop.kt`): a 90s store wall under a buzzing "GAME RENTALS" neon, the console's backlit
  section sign, shelves of real 3D cases (Case3D, each at its real shape, standing on the board; or your game look), the

  SEARCH / SORT / SETTINGS .EXE), the category as a directory listing (8.3 names, console as extension, play time), reverse

    command line naming the key you're on. Closing runs it back and the disc lands in its place on the orbit (its

## Update — 26 Oct 2026 (330, phase 2 of 5): layout-made game windows, Cardboard box (top-down storage boxes), Storage boxes, File select, PS2IODB save icons

- **Game windows made by their layouts** (`ui\WinScenes.kt`, Toni: "each popup a natural extension of its layout, not
  a recoloured generic window"). GameWindow keeps everything that makes the window work (opening out of the game's place
  and going back into it, the inspected piece, pages, Play's focus, the banner / motion / classic-window overrides) and
  hands the layout a `WinSceneCtx` with the game and every action — Play first, Details / Full details / Back, Options,
  Achievements, Save sync, Manual, Inspect, Performance, the save and performance lines, and the details / options /
  achievements / performance pages in the layout's colours. Windows without a piece now go back into their game's place
  when closed (they used to vanish). Settings › Game window › "<layout>'s window": Built into the layout (default) /
  Standard window.
  - **Cardboard box:** the case pulled out of the box is the centrepiece (the window's piece, turning from its spine to
    its front as it comes forward — `InspectMotion.fromSpine`), with a typed **insert sheet** taped beside it: facts on
    dotted lines, a few lines of story, the actions as rubber stamps (lit one stamped red), round sticker tools.
  - **File select:** the file block turns over (its front turns away) and its **back grows out into the window** in the
    block's own colour — console tab, stars, cover window, outlined name, time and story on an inset panel, fat buttons
    (lit one yellow, bouncing). Closing turns it back into the block.
  - **Storage boxes:** a **stored-entry record** — the sprite big on a stand (hopping), name plate, console tag, tabs
    Info / Details / Achievements / Options (L1 / R1 or tap), facts in pixel-framed cells, a menu with a ▶ pointer.
  - **Memory card:** the browser's **info screen** — the save icon big and turning (its own animation playing), the
    save's title in yellow top right with the facts, the choices as words along the bottom over the grey screen.
  - **Case flow:** the case out on the left and its **media** beside it — video / backdrop big, a strip of screenshot
    slides (◀ ▶ / tap shows one big), facts as glass chips, glossy pills with their reflections.
  - File select, Storage boxes and Memory card open out of the file / icon itself (their piece only via Inspect).
- **Cardboard box rebuilt** (`ui\StyleCardboardBox.kt`) after Toni's corrections ("looking down into a real cardboard
  storage box… two rows of tightly packed cases, spines up… multiple boxes when one fills up… not a shelf"):
  - Built to measure and drawn through a camera (`BoxCam`): a box two DVD-lengths deep and 420 mm across, 250 mm walls,
    5 mm board, its four flaps folded out, seen from 95 cm above (Camera angle moves it toward the front). The insides of
    all four walls, the floor, the cases' ends between the rows and the cut edge of the walls show as they would.
  - Cardboard: generated kraft / white materials (`tools\box\gen_cardboard.py` → `res\drawable-nodpi\box_*.webp`:
    fibres, mottling, fluted walls, flutes in the cut edge), each surface lit by how it faces the light (upper left),
    darker where walls meet the floor, flap creases, contact shadows along the rows. Wear and tape optional (off).
  - Each case at its real length and thickness, spine up; as many as physically fit across the back row, then the
    front row, then **Box 2, Box 3…** — the label shows "BOX n OF m" with ◀ ▶; ◀ ▶ past a box's side goes into the next
    box (at once, or after a knock), swipe changes box (one per swipe), Endless goes round from the last box.
  - The case you're on is lit and comes up a little (the one before goes back down first); A slides it straight up out
    of its slot, then turns it toward its cover, then its window opens; B reverses all of it into the same slot. Y turns
    it to its cover in place. Its case pictures are got ready while you rest on it (no plain slab mid-flight).
  - Layout options: case size (fewer / more to a row), spacing, packing (neat / messy), camera angle, how far it comes
    out, speed, box label (printed / marker / none), past a box's side, cardboard (brown / white / dark), wear and tape.
    Presets: Cardboard box, White archive box, Rummaged box. R1: the look, game size, badges and achievement chip tiles
    hidden there (the box always shows cases by their spines).
- **File select:** each block is labelled with the game's **console** (PlayStation 2, Nintendo 64…) instead of
  FILE A / B / C / D.
- **Storage boxes:** the icons are **pixel sprites** (the achievement icon or the cover's middle brought down to 32 px,
  colours stepped, stepped corners, a dark outline, drawn with hard pixel edges), standing in soft slots on the
  wallpaper; the one you're on hops in two steps; picked up, it rises to the pointer. Pixel-framed box, header and preview.
- **PS2 save icons from PS2IODB** (`data\Ps2IconDb.kt`, `res\raw\ps2iodb_index.tsv`): PS2 games with no save on this
  device show the game's real memory-card icon, downloaded once and cached; its animation plays on the one you're on
  (`Ps2Icons.Anim`). Memory card layout and the Save Vault's PS2 style; Layout options › Icons from PS2IODB.
- **Logos as 3D badges** (`ui\LogoSlab.kt`) for games without a save icon. Fixed: they never loaded (blank icons —
  Toni: "the games that don't have the icons are shown empty").
- **Freeze fixed:** File select's window froze the Thor (Android 13's turned-text cache) — text in turned layers is now
  drawn flat first (`flatTextFor3d`) in File select, Cardboard box and Memory card.

## Update — 26 Oct 2026 (330, phase 1 of 5): Pocket classic's game window, Memory card (2000), Case flow

The retro layout expansion runs in five phases, each built, checked on the AYN Thor and pushed (Toni: push each phase;
original names; layout-styled dialogs opt-in). Tracking matrices: `docs\compat\LAYOUTS_330.md`.

- **Pocket classic (from PR #12):** A on the game panel opens the game's window (Game window off: it starts the game, as
  everywhere). The window is the pocket menu's own: a pale paper screen with faint pinstripes, a sharp grey frame,
  monospace capitals — START / GAME INFO / BACK — and the picture and the lit button in Layout options › Accent colour.
  The whole window works as on every layout (details, achievements, options, saves, Inspect, performance).
- **Game window colours keep a layout's own look where the colours are the look** (`WinLook.keepsPalette`): with "The
  game's colours" (the default) or "Theme colours" the paper of Pocket classic and the grey of Memory card stay; the
  game's / theme's colour lights the accent only. Other layouts unchanged.
- **New layout: Memory card (2000)** (`ui\StyleMemoryCard.kt`): the games as small save icons floating in loose rows on
  a neutral grey screen lit from above — the category as the card's name top left with how many games are on it, the game
  you're on top right in yellow with its console, time played and achievements, blue arrows for more rows, button hints.
  The icon you're on lifts and brightens with a soft light behind it and turns. PS2 games with a save on this device's
  memory cards show **their save's own 3D icon and two-line title** (read only, never changed — the Save Vault's reader);
  others their clear logo (your pick first), an app's icon, a small disc printed with the cover (disc consoles) or a little
  box of it, else a plain memory-card symbol — never called a save icon. ◀ ▶ ▲ ▼ through the icons (rows scroll), A the
  window, L2 / R2 the next card, Endless goes round; tap to pick, tap again to open, drag to scroll. Layout options: icon
  size, spacing, loose / straight rows, depth, the icon you're on (turns / sways / lifts), background (grey, grey-blue,
  your theme), save icons, title, hints, floating. Its window: smoky grey-blue glass. Presets "Memory card" and "Memory
  card, grey-blue". (The Save Vault's PS2 memory-card style from update 239 already is the optional vault presentation.)
- **New layout: Case flow** (`ui\StyleCaseFlow.kt`): real 3D cases (the game's front, real spine, its back when turned)
  on a curved carousel on a dark stage — the one you're on facing you, the others turned toward it along the curve,
  smaller and darker further out, with reflections; each console's case at its real size. Moving glides the whole row
  (nothing pops in or out; Endless glides on from the last case to the first). A brings the case forward and its window
  grows out of it (Inspect there turns it round); B sets it back. Layout options: fronts or spines either side, curve,
  spacing, case size, the side cases' turn, camera height, speed, reflections, stage, name. R1 › Case for every game
  works here. Presets "Case flow" and "Case flow, spines".
- **R1 on the new layouts:** the look, game size, console badges and achievement chip tiles are hidden there (they'd
  change nothing); Endless, Music player, Sort, Categories etc. stay. Memory card's card name follows R1 › Categories.
- **Fixed while checking:** Case flow's category name sat over the round shortcuts' ☰ in the top-left corner (found by
  the R1 tile walk — the tile changed nothing): it's at the top in the middle there.
- **Checked on the Thor:** every option of both new layouts rendered (35 shots); recordings of moving, scrolling,
  categories and opening / closing the window (no flashes, the piece flies back to its place); R1 tile walk of both
  layouts in the Cover and Case looks (every tile shown changed the screen); Pocket classic's window on both screens with
  D-pad and B; Mr Bean's real PS2 save icon. Unit tests (`Layouts330Test`).
- **Not tested:** the Retroid Pocket Classic / Flip 2 (not connected), other screen sizes, Memory card's Sways / Lifts

## Update — 26 Oct 2026 (329): every R1 tile pressed in every layout × look on the Thor, fixes, Dark Channel grid

- **R1 tile walk (test hooks only, `ui/TileCheck.kt`):** `--es voltcap_test_tilewalk <tiles|all>` /
  `--es voltcap_test_tilewalk_all "LAYOUTS|LOOKS|TILES"` press every R1 tile the panel shows for the layout / look on
  screen (through the panel, like an L1 shortcut), close it and compare both screens before / after (PixelCopy); a tile
  that changed nothing gets its next value too. A control (panel opened and closed, nothing pressed) runs first.
  Everything is a preview and put back after each tile; the home screen is held still (`HomeIdle.holdForTest`), a fake
  song "plays" so the music player shows, presses don't count for "most used" tiles. The whole walk runs inside Voltcap
  (adb's background shells died) and writes `<external files>/tilecheck/results.log`; it stops itself below 20 % battery
  or above 45 °C. Second pass: 480 × 270 pictures and a 0.04 % line, so small changes (the corner ☰, an achievement chip)
  count.
- **First pass: 33 layouts × 8 looks, 3,754 tile presses** (25 Oct 16:00–23:38). 2,739 changed the screen; the 1,015 that
  didn't were sorted into real dead tiles (fixed or hidden below), things that change only somewhere else (the Categories
  screen's corners, Green Core's games page, a tiny ☰ under the old line) and content (a game without achievements or
  real disc scans).
- **Fixed / hidden where the tile did nothing** (`R1TileRules.kt`, `QuickSettings.kt`, …):
  - **Gaps on Twin showcase** changed Twin desk's gap; it now changes the showcase's own (from 4 dp — closer looked the
    same; the showcase's Layout options list too).
  - **Magnifier on the two-screen layouts** (Twin desk / icons / showcase, Pocket classic / ribbon): their lower half
    owns the second screen, so the page never showed. Greyed there, saying to open the normal second screen first.
  - **Music player on style homes without Voltcap's status bar** (Hero tiles, Channel grid, Spotlight's Home menu, the
    Pocket layouts, Twin showcase): "in the status bar" drew nothing, so the tap switched an invisible player. There the

  - **Categories on Twin desk / Twin showcase:** "All categories" looked the same as "Current only" (every category shows

## Update — 25 Oct 2026 (328): device walk of every layout × look, a game that came back on the wrong screen, sampling while asleep

- **Device walk on the AYN Thor (the rest of the 326 audit).** All 33 home layouts × 8 game looks (264 combinations) shown
  with the test hooks (nothing saved), the R1 panel opened and closed with B in each, both screens captured: no crash, no
  freeze, R1 closed every time. What the panel showed was logged per combination and compared with the automated matrix:
  every difference comes from a switch set differently on the Thor (cartridge packs downloaded, header off, Twin full top,
  Spines on Shelf off, Case stacks carousel on) — none was a wrong rule. Screenshots of every layout looked through (no
  clipping, no broken cards / cases / discs / spines). After the walk a restart brought your own layout and look back
  (Case stacks + Case).
- **Twin desk during a game:** the in-game second screen (Game + info) stayed live — pages, the Widgets page (Now playing,
  System, clock, battery), timer counting; back home, Twin desk's lower half came straight back.
- **Fixed — a game brought back from the background could open on the lower screen.** Starting a game that is still open
  (Running games / Quick resume) brought it forward without saying which screen. With Game + info Voltcap opens the info
  page on the second screen first, so that screen had the focus — and Android opened the game there. Found with WWE All
  Stars: its launcher came up on the lower screen, started its game window again and the old one closed with a crash;
  Voltcap's info page then stayed on the lower screen with no game. New launches always passed the game's screen; now
  resuming does too (`QuickResume.resume`, `RunningGames.resume`, `LauncherViewModel.startGameNow`). Possibly one of the
  "second screen randomly stops" reports.
- **Fixed — performance readings kept running with the screen off.** Measured asleep during a game: Voltcap read the CPU /
  GPU / FPS files every second (≈3 % of one core, a 35 MB + 59 MB garbage collection every ~2 min). The overlay paused
  itself when the screen went off, the in-game tuner (AutoTDP) didn't. The sampler now skips every reading while the
  device is asleep, whoever holds it (`data/perf/PerfSampler.kt`). The freeze watchdog no longer reads every thread's CPU
  time every 5 s while asleep either (`data/crash/FreezeWatchdog.kt`; a freeze still writes its report).
- **Longer play and memory:** 7 min of WWE All Stars with Twin desk: second screen live throughout, Voltcap steady at
  306–342 MB. Leak check — all 33 layouts walked 5 times from a fresh start: memory rose to 0.9–1.5 GB, but the native
  memory in use went back down after garbage collections (705 → 172 MB), so no leak; pictures are freed late and the
  allocator keeps freed pages. Count-limited picture caches that ignore Android's trims are noted as a follow-up (would
  lower the peak on smaller handhelds). Hours of play not tested.
- R1: the "Drawn media" rule (tile removed in 325) is out of the list of tiles with a rule; a test now also fails when a
  rule names a tile that isn't built (`R1TileRules.kt`, `R1Compat326Test.kt`). The matrix CSV lost that column.
- **Fixed — a test preview could be saved as your settings.** During an adb walk (test hooks, "nothing saved"), turning
  the in-game second screen's page saved the whole previewed appearance: Twin desk became your saved layout. While a
  preview is on, every appearance change now stays a preview (`LauncherViewModel.setAppearance`). Your layout was put
  back to Case stacks with the Case look (checked: restart → Case stacks; the same page turn during a preview no longer
  saves anything). Only reachable with the test-hooks file (adb), never in normal use.
- Test hooks: with the hooks file present the R1 panel logs its tiles per layout / look (`QuickSettings.kt`,
  `TestHooks.enabled`) — that is how the walk was compared. Nothing changes without the file.

## Update — 25 Oct 2026 (327): Switch games really start in Eden and Eden Duo from Voltcap

- **Eden Duo installed on the Thor** (v1.3.2.2 from its GitHub release, `dev.igawa6.edenduo`) for testing. Voltcap found
  it at once: **Game settings › Emulator** lists citron, Eden and Eden Duo for every Switch game.
- **Found while testing: Voltcap could not start a Switch game in any Eden build** (Eden, Eden Duo — and this was so
  before 326). Eden opened and closed again ("No game found in arguments or intent"); Eden Duo crashed. Voltcap hands
  games over as a *Shared file link*, and Eden's file code only reads games through the *folder it was given* (a storage
  link). Now Eden's family (every build with yuzu's `org.yuzu.yuzu_emu` screen: Eden, Eden Duo, Eden Nightly / Legacy,
  yuzu) gets a storage link through the game's own folder — the Switch games folder you give Eden. If you gave Eden a
  folder higher up (or keep games in sub-folders), set it under Settings › Emulators › Switch › Folder given to the
  emulator. Eden Duo's screen swap (game on the lower screen) works with this kind of link too.
  Checked on the Thor: Mario Golf Super Rush started from Voltcap in Eden and ran (59.9 FPS), the in-game second screen
  on the lower screen, Voltcap's own lower screen out of the way; back home, all back. (`EmulatorCatalog.profileFor`,
  `LaunchProfiles.treeAtGameFolder`, `GameLauncher.explicitAttempts`.)
- Voltcap's file provider now also answers the document questions emulators ask a link (`data/RomShareProvider.kt`,
  in the manifest in place of Android's FileProvider, same authority) — Eden logged an error for every shared link.
- Game settings › Display now updates at once when this game's emulator changes (Eden Duo → "Emulator uses both
  screens").
- **Eden Duo itself can't run a game yet on the Thor:** it's a fresh install without your keys / firmware and without a
  games folder. Its own first-start setup (Eden Duo › settings: keys, firmware, add the Switch ROMs folder) is needed —
  not done by Claude (your keys are yours to copy). Then a Switch game set to Eden Duo starts like Mario Golf did in Eden.
- Donkey Kong Country Returns HD doesn't start in Eden even from adb (the file itself, not Voltcap).
- Test side effects: Mario Golf Super Rush and Donkey Kong Country Returns HD were started once and are in Continue
  playing now; both games' emulator choice was set back to Console's emulator. Switch has no console emulator set yet
  (Settings › Emulators › Switch).
- **Copy** (already in place and pushed): `src_copy\data\EmulatorCatalog.kt`, `src_copy\data\LaunchProfiles.kt`,
  `src_copy\data\GameLauncher.kt`, `src_copy\data\RomShareProvider.kt` (new), `src_copy\ui\GameProfileDialog.kt`,

## Update — 25 Oct 2026 (326): second screen no longer freezes during games, Eden Duo, R1 compatibility audit

- **Before anything else — `src_copy` was 111 files behind.** PRs #9–#11 (0.6.40 / 0.6.41) changed `app/src` directly on
  GitHub, so `src_copy` and three `project_copy` files (SUMMARY.md, packs/v1/carts_CREDITS.txt, tools/release/release.ps1)
  were older than the project. The next robocopy would have put the old versions back. They were refreshed from
  `main` (ebcc767) first; `git status` showed no code change after the robocopy, so they match exactly.
  **If you edit on GitHub again, refresh `src_copy` before the next robocopy** (or tell Claude to).

- **Second screen "stops working" during games — root cause found on the Thor (adb).** Voltcap's second-screen window is
  an Android Presentation: a window above every app on its display. It stayed up while a game covered Voltcap, but its
  drawing is paused while Voltcap is in the background — so the lower screen showed a **frozen picture** (clock stuck at
  13:24 at 13:26, video stopped, taps doing nothing), and it sat over the live in-game second screen Voltcap opens for
  the game (pages, widgets, music, volume, timer). The same happened whenever another app or one of Voltcap's own
  windows covered the home ("sometimes inside Voltcap"). Now the window steps aside while Voltcap is in the background
  and comes back (the same window, nothing rebuilt) when Voltcap is in front again. Checked on the Thor: in-game timer
  0:11 → 1:25 → 1:52, clock moving, a tap changes the page; back home the home's second screen is back and live; sleep /
  wake the same. (`ui/SecondScreen.kt`)
- **The window comes back when Android closes it itself** (the display's size / density changing, the screen going for a
  moment): the home believed it was still up (Twin layouts kept their lower half "on" an empty screen) until Voltcap was
  restarted. It's rebuilt now (at most 5 times in 30 s, only while Voltcap is in front, never over a game's own screen).
  Not reproducible on the Thor's firmware (a density change didn't make Android close it) — not tested on the device.
- **In-game second screen stayed black-and-white:** the home's dimming kept running behind it and its grey shared with the
  in-game screen, which nothing woke. It waits while Voltcap is in the background now (`SecondDim.hold`). Thor: still in
  colour after 1:40 of play.
- Behaviour change: with Settings › Screens layout **"Game, leave the other screen"** the lower screen shows what's under
  Voltcap's window (the Thor's own launcher) during a game, instead of the frozen Voltcap picture. **"Game + info"** (the
  default) is the one with Voltcap's live pages during play.

- **Eden Duo** (github.com/igawa6/eden-duo, package `dev.igawa6.edenduo` — read from its `duo.gradle`; its dev builds
  `dev.igawa6.edenduo.dev`):
  - Recognised as a Switch emulator (picker suggestion, emulator list) and launched directly: its `EmulationActivity`
    with the game as the intent's data (its `EmulationFragment` reads a content link ending in .nsp / .xci…).
  - **Per game:** new in **Game settings › Emulator**: *Console's emulator* or any installed Switch emulator for this game
    only (e.g. Fire Emblem: Three Houses on Eden Duo for its companion, the rest on Eden). An emulator that's later
    uninstalled is kept in the game's settings; the console's is used meanwhile. Globally as before: Settings ›
    Emulators › Switch. New installs pick Eden Duo › Eden › Citron as the Switch default (existing setups untouched).
  - Its companion keeps the lower screen: on a built-in second screen a game in Eden Duo gets **"Emulator uses both
    screens"** unless you set a layout for it (Settings › Screens), and Voltcap's own window steps aside (above).
  - Eden Duo's screen swap needs a lasting file grant; with the default "Shared file link" it keeps the game on the main
    screen. Not tested on the device — **Eden Duo isn't installed on the Thor**.

- **R1 compatibility audit** (rules in `ui/R1TileRules.kt`, the one place that decides every tile):
  - **Outline** (325) was shown on every layout; the style homes draw their own focus ring, so it switched nothing there.

  and back each carry the shade in their own light (as the shells with a sides' picture already did), so an opaque

## Update — 23 Oct 2026 (320): manuals downloaded ahead, or only previewed

- **Manuals: download all ahead, or preview only** (Toni: "the manual downloads only when I press it on the case — can
  they all be downloaded ahead if I choose so, and if not just a preview, viewed that time without downloading").
  Settings › (Manuals card) › **Manuals on this device**: *Preview only — nothing kept* (default) — a manual is fetched
  into a temporary file only to read it and deleted when its reader closes (`ManualLinks.previewDir` / `dropPreview`,
  `ArtFiles.downloadManual(into = …)`); *Download all ahead* — every manual found is downloaded in the background, 20 s
  after start and when it's picked (`downloadManualsAhead`, quiet `findAllManuals`), and one opened is kept. Manuals
  already on the device open from there either way; the case's booklet shows a manual's first page only when it's kept.
- **Copy:** `data/Features.kt`, `data/ArtFiles.kt`, `data/ManualLinks.kt`, `LauncherViewModel.kt`, `ui/LauncherScreen.kt`,
  `ui/SettingsDialog.kt`.
- **Not compiled here** (GitHub's build check runs); not tried on a device.

## Update — 23 Oct 2026 (319): GBA spines across the whole box side; box sides in the cover's colours

- **GBA (and any cardboard box) spine too thin** (Toni: "not as wide as the cardboard"): a spine scan narrower than the
  box's side was fitted inside it whole — a thin strip on plain card. It's stretched across the side now, its whole height
  kept (`boxSideSpine`, Case3D.kt); a scan far wider than the side is still fitted inside, N64 as before.
- **Box sides in the cover's colours** (Toni: the printed sides on or off; off → the cover's colours, per side): Settings ›
  Game look › Box sides — "Fill missing sides" is the printed sides on; with "Authentic only" or "Plain cardboard" a new
  row, **Sides in the cover's colours: Right side / Top / Bottom** (all on by default, `Features.boxSideColors`), gives
  each side with no picture of its own the colour of the cover's edge that meets it (`BoxSides.edgeColor` / `colored`);
  a side switched off stays plain card.
- **Second screen dock: one-colour icon pack, no plate** (Toni: "an icon pack in one colour so it follows the theme's
  colours", "remove the square look with the blur behind"): each app is its symbol in the theme's accent — the app's own
  monochrome icon (Android 13+) where it ships one, else its adaptive icon's foreground in the accent's shades, else its
  whole icon in them (`AppIconCache.loadMono`, `MonoAppIcon`); Voltcap's shortcuts their symbol alone. No rounded plate,
  no blurred copy behind (the empty "+" slot keeps its faint plate). Settings › Screens › App dock › **Icons in the
  theme's colour** (on; `Features.secondDockMono`) — off: the apps' own colour icons, still without the plate.
- **…and everywhere** (Toni: "the icons always used for everything"): with that switch on, every app icon in Voltcap —
  app drawer, shortcuts, notifications, apps in the library and on the home layouts — is its one-colour symbol in the
  accent, all the very same colour (an icon without its own monochrome version keeps its drawing as see-through parts)
  (`rememberAppIcon` returns it, tinted once per icon and colour; `AppIconArt` drops the banner and the blurred
  copy behind it).
- **Still covers for games scraped before update 317** (Toni: "I don't see the still art on the discs and cartridges"):
  the still cover was only looked up on a fresh scrape. `LauncherViewModel.backfillStillCovers()` (20 s after start)
  looks up the first still cover of every game whose cover is animated and has none yet (40 a pass, a game tried once
  a week; `SteamGridDbRepository.fetchStillGrid`), keeps it with the art and the cartridges / discs wear it at once.
  A cover you picked yourself (Artwork & details) that's animated still has no still one beside it.
- **A tap on the inspected case / disc often did nothing** (Toni: "touching the case doesn't open it, it's realised after
  some time"; dragging fine): a finger that moved a few pixels made the touch a drag and the tap was lost. A touch under
  0.4 s that moved under 28 dp now counts as the tap (`inspectTap`, both Inspect views, MediaInspectView.kt).
- **Copy:** `ui/MediaInspectView.kt`, `ui/Case3D.kt`, `ui/BoxSides.kt`, `ui/SettingsDialog.kt`, `data/Features.kt`, `ui/AppIcons.kt`,
  `data/SteamGridDbRepository.kt`, `LauncherViewModel.kt`, `ui/LauncherScreen.kt`,
  `ui/SecondDockShortcuts.kt`, `ui/SecondScreenHome.kt`, `ui/ScreenLayoutsUi.kt`.
- **Not compiled here**; GitHub's build check runs on the PR. Not tried on a device.

## Update — 23 Oct 2026 (318): Stats' recaps get the covers of games no longer on the device ahead

- **Covers fetched before they're needed** (Toni: "Stats don't show pictures of games that aren't on the device — scrape
  them before"): `LauncherViewModel.prefetchStatsArt()` looks up the covers of every game in the play history that isn't
  in the library — played on another device, or here and since removed — most played first, 20 s after start and each
  time Stats opens; kept in the Save Vault art store the recaps read. A game whose cover wasn't found is tried again after
  a week. Removed games are searched by their file's name, the console guessed from its folder (`data.goneGame`, shared
  with `YearRecapDialog`).
- **Game window (picture on top, buttons under) cut off at the bottom** (Toni's screenshot: the "Saves" / performance
  line half off the window, no way to scroll): the room it saves under the picture is a guess, and a fact line that wraps
  pushed the line out. The window now scrolls when it still doesn't fit (`GameWindow.kt`, Arrange.STACK); the D-pad's
  focus scrolls to what it lands on.
- **Freeze opening a game's window** (crash report 2026-10-22 19:36, Flip 2, "Input dispatching timed out"): the
  RetroAchievements login was read on the main thread, and its first decryption through the Keystore took over 5 s.
  `RaCredentialsStore` now decrypts each account once and keeps it in memory (forgotten on save / clear / a backup
  restore), and the view model reads it off the main thread at start (`warm()`). The other two freezes in those reports
  (19:17, 20:16) were the GPU stalls the carousel work in 314–317 removed; the 21:10 crash was the charge-limit start
  fixed in 317.
- **Spines cut at their ends on DS, Game Boy, Game Boy Color cases** (Toni's Inspect screenshots: Assassin's Creed II
  Discovery's "NINTENDO DS", Astérix's "GAME BOY", Dr. Mario's title cut at the top): a spine scan a little narrower than
  the case's side was zoomed to fill it, cutting its top and bottom. `spineWhole` (Case3D.kt) keeps the whole height —
  widens a narrower scan to the side (up to 1/0.7×), fits a far narrower one inside whole, cuts only a scan wider than
  the side (in the middle, as before). Keep cases and cardboard boxes; N64 and your own cuts unchanged.
- **Copy:** `ui/Case3D.kt`, `LauncherViewModel.kt`, `data/OtherDevices.kt`, `data/RaCredentialsStore.kt`, `data/Backup.kt`,
  `ui/YearRecapDialog.kt`, `ui/LauncherScreen.kt`, `ui/HubScreens.kt`, `ui/GameWindow.kt`.
- **Not compiled here** (no Android SDK); not tried on a device.

## Update — 22 Oct 2026 (317): Cartridge carousel GPU memory and redraws, first-launch charge-limit crash

**Status:** Same branch / [PR #6](https://github.com/dzepdzep/Voltcap/pull/6), not merged; CI is the compile check, not
tested on a handheld.

- **Found (`voltcap-mem6.zip`, Flip 2):** still 1,011 GPU render targets / 1,233 MB, identical to mem5 — the GPU's
  ceiling, not a slow leak (new buffers simply fail past it). Android keeps one buffer per offscreen layer for every
  node in the drawn tree, even off the screen or behind something; a game is only left out when the carousel doesn't
  draw it. The "far off the screen" check (update 314) counted a game as on it up to the slot's width + height *and* a
  whole screen's width past each edge — further than "To the edge" builds games (~15 a side on the Flip 2, ×3 in Box
  flow), so nothing was ever left out. Cases and discs (plain canvas drawing) barely noticed; each turned cartridge
  holds up to 6–7 layers (user: "the cases and cds don't lag").
- **Changed:** `Carousel.kt` — a game is left out once it is past the edge by more than a tenth of the carousel's width
  (`CarouselViewport.CULL_MARGIN`), its reach half the slot's width + its height (still room for a turned piece's sides,
  its media and lean). `SolidPiece.kt` — the generic path (drawn templates, cartridge photos, pack pictures): the face's
  light set on the face's own layer, so the turned face is a plain layer, not a second offscreen buffer (the outline made
  from the face only uses its shape — SrcIn / DstOut — so it looks the same). *(Reverted below.)*
- **Crash (`voltcap-crash-20261022-2110331`, 0.6.35):** `ForegroundServiceDidNotStartInTimeException` for
  `ChargeLimitService` — six minutes after start, the main thread skipping 50–110 frames at a time (the GPU memory
  above), so the service didn't reach `startForeground` within Android's 10 s. `ChargeLimitService`: with Voltcap in
  front a plain `startService` (no deadline; `startForegroundService` only when Android refuses from the background); a
  new status while it runs only updates the notification (each new label used to start it again, each with a new 10 s
  deadline); `stop` never stops it while a start is on its way — it stops itself once in the foreground (`wanted`).
- **Measured after the above (user, Flip 2):** render targets 1,011 → 363 (479 MB); still sluggish. gfxinfo: GPU 3 ms
  (p50) / 9 ms (p90), frames 28 ms / 300 ms — CPU-bound. **Perfetto (`voltcap-trace5.zip`, Case stacks, scrolling the
  drawn console cartridges):** ~6 fps; the main thread waits on the RenderThread (113 ms/frame), which re-draws ~400
  offscreen pictures every frame (`flush layers` 125 ms, 2,026 rect fills): ~75 turned pieces, all on the generic path
  (face, outline, sides, smear — PhysicalMedia's drawn templates have no single front picture), plus each game's shade.
- **Changed (`SolidPiece.kt`, `PieceShot`):** a piece without its front's picture takes one of its own — its content
  drawn once into a node-sized picture (`GraphicsLayer.toImageBitmap`, 120 ms after the content last changed) — and is
  turned from it like the shells (sides' picture, plain layers, nothing offscreen per frame). The content sits in a layer
  of its own whose drawing bumps `PieceShot.version` only when it changes (a label coming in), which takes the picture
  again; content that keeps changing gives up on it (`off`) and is drawn as before. The face-light change above is
  reverted (the picture must be unlit).
- **Measured (user):** 16 fps (frames 61 ms p50 / 65 ms p90, GPU 6 ms) — better, still sluggish. **Perfetto
  (`voltcap-trace6.zip`):** still ~460 offscreen redraws a frame; the process had taken ~737 front pictures — each
  recomposition (every carousel step) gave the piece a new content-layer modifier, which drew the content again, counted
  as new content, retook the picture, and after 40 retakes gave up (`off`). Now remembered once per piece (`shotMark`).
  The idle hop of the drawn templates, cartridge photos and pack pictures moved round the solid piece (as the drawn
  shells' already was), so their picture never holds them mid-hop (`PhysicalMedia.kt`, `CustomCarts.kt`).
- **Measured (user, 317c):** worse — frames 350 ms, the Flip 2's fan loud. A loop: a piece drawn from its picture
  leaves its content out of the screen's drawing; drawn again for the next picture, the content drew itself anew, which
  counted as a change and asked for another picture (and its sides' picture again, on the CPU) — over and over. Now its
  own drawing for the picture doesn't count (`PieceShot.quiet`), and a piece takes at most 10 pictures (the last stays).
- **Measured (user, 317d):** frames 5 ms (p50) / 250 ms (p90), 34 % janky, 323 MB render targets, fan quieter; still
  sluggish. **Perfetto (`voltcap-trace7.zip`):** ~226 offscreen redraws a frame — CarouselArt's darkening buffer for each
  game aside (~67 a frame, ~32 ms), pieces coming back on the screen taking their picture again (`copyImageInto` /
  `setSurface` ~28 ms a frame, up to 86 ms), and the sides' pictures thrown out of the GPU's cache and uploaded again (~28
  a frame).
- **Changed:** `PieceTurn.shadeOf` / `shadeTaken` — a piece drawn from its pictures takes the carousel's shade on itself
  (its lights × (1 − shade), its back a black SrcAtop), and `CarouselArt` then leaves out its darkening buffer (read again
  while drawing, so never both). `PieceShots` — the pieces' pictures kept by what they show (`solidPiece(shotKey)`: drawn
  templates, cartridge photos), 96 at most. `sideArtOf` returns a GPU (HARDWARE) bitmap on API 26+. `SolidLight` in 40
  steps (the shade slides through it). Known difference: a console badge on a cartridge aside isn't darkened with it.
- **Measured (user, 317e):** frames 32 ms (p50) / 250 ms (p90), 264 MB render targets; still janky. "Games each side"
  didn't change how many show (open question — which view the R1 Carousel tile names). **Perfetto (`voltcap-trace8.zip`):**
  ~158 offscreen redraws a frame (from ~460); the pictures taken of the screen (`copyImageInto` + `setSurface`) ~42 ms a
  frame while new games come in.
- **Changed:** `rememberTemplateCartFront` / `templateCartFront` (`RealMedia.kt`) — a template cartridge's front made as
  one picture on `Dispatchers.Default` (paper window, art laid as TemplateMedia lays it, cut by the shell's mask, the shell
  over it; GPU bitmap; kept in `DerivedArt`), handed to its solid piece as `faceArt` (`PhysicalMedia.kt`): no picture of
  the screen taken for them any more (PieceShot stays for cartridge photos and pack pictures).
- **Games each side in Box flow / Spine wall / pull-out stack (user: "doesn't work with those"):** `Carousel.reach` took
  three times the number (pull-out: + 8 behind the pulled-out case) — slim and packed, every choice from 2 up reached the
  screen's edges. Now the number picked is how many show each side (pull-out: + the 8 hidden); To the edge keeps ×3.
- **Screen recording (`voltcap-flash.mp4`):** the "flashing" is the stacks jumping — ~70 distinct frames in 10 s while
  stepping — not a drawing fault (no brightness flicker, no label changes found).
- **317h reverted:** with it every frame took 250–400 ms (UI thread slow on each, bitmap uploads on most) and the fans
  ran hard on the Flip 2 — a repeat somewhere in the photo / disc-shell front path. Back to 317g.
- **Animated covers off on cartridges and discs (Toni):** `mediaArtModel` (every cartridge / disc printed picture) asks
  for the still first frame (`styleArtRequest(still)`, own memory key), as do the pack sticker (`rememberPackLabel`) and
  a disc photo's trimmed request — whatever Animated artwork is set to. A playing label redrew its turned piece each frame.

  later; `adb shell cmd package compile -m speed-profile -f com.shelf.launcher` (or installing with the build's `.dm`)
  compiles it at once — why the update 316-era `.dm` helped the cases.
- **GameCube spines (Toni: Budokai 2, Melee, Pikmin):** a keep case's spine scan more than 1.8× as wide (for its height)
  as the side is left out (`SPINE_TOO_WIDE`, `Case3D.kt` spineFit2) — its middle cut to the side was a blurred slice of

  that frame neither CarouselArt nor the piece darkened it. Now set once and kept; a piece without its pictures darkens

## Update — 22 Oct 2026 (316): Smoother 3D cases — their pictures made away from the screen's thread

**Status:** Same branch / [PR #6](https://github.com/dzepdzep/Voltcap/pull/6), not merged; CI is the compile check, not
tested on a handheld.

- **Found:** `Case3D` (the 3D cases in every carousel, Case stacks, the shelf and the game window) cut, fitted and
  framed its pictures inside `remember` on the screen's thread the first time each case was drawn: the front
  (`fillCrop` / `fitFace` / `jewelFront` / `framed` with the template band), its own spine (`singleSpine(orientSpine)`,
  which reads the scan's pixels, then `boxSideSpine` — reads every pixel to find the flaps — or `fillCrop`), the console
  spine with the title (600 px, text and logo) for games without one, and the back (`fitBack`). Several full-size
  picture copies per new case on the screen's thread: scrolling a big carousel of cases stuttered as they came in.
- **Changed:** `rememberDerived` (Case3D.kt): the result already in `DerivedArt` at once (`DerivedArt.peek`), else made on
  `Dispatchers.Default` while the case shows its usual stand-ins (the front in the game's colour, the dark spine strip
  `SpineCache.WAITING`) — the same stand-ins it already showed while its pictures loaded. `rememberConsoleSpine` does the
  same for the console spine (`DerivedArt.peekNamed`). The face is remembered as an alias (`DerivedArt.alias`, not
  counted twice in the 48 MB cache); `framed` is now cached too (it was made again on every key change). Same pictures,
  same rules (update 308 / 311 / 312 spine fitting untouched).
- **Flip 2 ANR again (`voltcap-crash-20261022-193624_11.zip`):** 0.6.34 — again published from `main` *without* PR #6
  (main = 313 + two version bumps). Froze as Inspect opened over Case stacks (421 kgsl allocation failures, 3–7 MB each,
  8 s frames). With PR #6 the games behind the inspect view faded one by one, so every turned cartridge would have
  needed its whole-piece buffer again at once: the carousel's games now fade as **one group** (`Carousel.kt`, a Box
  1.5× wide / 1.6× tall round the carousel so the games past its sides and their reflections aren't cut), each piece
  stays opaque inside it (no buffer of its own). Overlapping cases no longer show through each other while dimmed.
- **Perfetto trace from the Flip 2 (user, 0.6.35 fix build, scrolling cartridges in Case stacks, 8 s):** 53 frames in 8 s
  (~6–7 fps), ~150 ms each; RenderThread "flush layers" 75 ms/frame, ~287 offscreen render passes and ~566 clears per frame
  for ~47 turned pieces (≈6 passes each — the old generic solid-piece path), GPU itself 6–11 ms; 374 MB of render targets.
  Cause: the **Custom / Clear 3D cartridges** draw your pack's shapes through `PackCart` → `AuthenticPackCart` (update 307),
  which wasn't on update 314's picture-built path, and made its 640 px front and read the pack picture's plastic
  (`CustomPieceTones.load`, a file decode) on the screen's thread for each new piece. Fixed: `AuthenticPackCart` front from
  cache at once else on `Dispatchers.Default` (previous kept, a place changing game draws at once), plastic via
  `rememberCustomPieceTone`, and `solidPiece(faceArt = PieceFace(front, look.aspect, frame))` — `PieceFace.frame` +
  `pieceFrameRect` (the front stretched to its frame in the shape's box, rounded as Compose rounds Dp). `PackCart` /
  `CustomCart` take `solid` / `motionSeed` and apply them themselves (the two-picture Vita / HuCard shapes and the disc
  shells keep the old order and path). Tests for `pieceFrameRect`.
- **Second trace (after the pack fix):** 82 frames / 8 s (was 53), 123 GPU passes a frame (was 287), flush layers 33 ms
  (was 75) — but prepareTree 39 ms (was 10): the covers (480×426) were **uploaded to the GPU 5,461 times in 8 s** (2.2 s),
  because **567 render targets / 754 MB** stood in the GPU cache and threw them out every frame. Only ~25 pieces show:
  the rest were the games far off the screen that update 314 stopped *drawing* but that still *held* their GPU pictures
  (~45 a side with To the edge). Now a game far off the screen (`culled`) keeps nothing composed inside its slot — its
  layers are released — and is built again a whole carousel width before it can show.
- **Third trace (with that):** worse — **1,019 render targets / 1,243 MB**, median frame 101 ms, GPU stalls: rebuilding
  the games coming back made new GPU pictures faster than the old ones were let go. **Reverted** (culled games stay
  composed, not drawn). Instead the turned pieces drawn from a picture need **no offscreen picture at all** while drawn
  opaque: `sideArtOf` makes the sides' picture once per front off the screen's thread (`rememberDerived`: the outline at
  alpha × 4 − 24 in the plastic's tone under the sheen — what the offscreen sides drew; `sideAlpha` / `sideRowRgb`,
  tested), and the sides and the face are plain layers (`edgeLeaf` / `litLeaf`, their light drawn in, recorded as the
  turn changes). The smear is gone for them: each of its copies is drawn at its own place, the same places in the same
  order. Difference: the sheen spans the piece's picture rather than the whole slot (a landscape cartridge's sides
  shade over the cartridge, not the empty slot above and below it).
- **Flip 2 ANR on the fix build (`voltcap-crash-20261022-2016011.zip`, 0.6.35, Case stacks, after 88 s):** 500 kgsl
  failures at ~0.8 MB (slot-sized layers) and ~3.2 MB (whole-piece buffers). Compose keeps every GraphicsLayer a node
  makes alive — and its GPU picture — until it's let go, drawn or not, so the games built off the screen still held
  theirs. Now: `PieceTurn.activeOf` (the carousel's `!culled`, read while composing) — a piece not shown keeps no
  solid-piece layers at all; `shadeOf` is 0 while culled, so `CarouselArt` lets go of its darkening layer; and the picture
  path no longer records the offscreen `edge` / `lit` it doesn't draw, nor `solid` until a see-through face or the back
  needs it.
- **Memory snapshot after 2 min of scrolling (fix build):** still **1,011 render targets / 1,233 MB**, native heap 560 MB
  — the culling change didn't touch it. Cause found in `solidPiece`: it took ~10 new GraphicsLayers (`obtainGraphicsLayer`)
  every time its drawing cache was rebuilt, and it was rebuilt at every carousel step for the pieces whose slot recomposed
  (a new `PieceTurn` each recomposition, a new `PieceFace` each recomposition of CartShellArt / AuthenticPackCart); the
  layers let go kept their GPU pictures for a long time, so they piled up while scrolling until the GPU ran out. Now the
  layers are `rememberGraphicsLayer()`s kept for the piece's life (re-recorded on a rebuild), the carousel hands each slot
  one remembered `PieceTurn` (latest turn / opacity through `rememberUpdatedState`), and the `PieceFace`s are remembered.
- **Not changed yet:** N64 spines that "still don't apply correctly on some games" (user) — waiting for which games and
  how they look (see the chat for the likely causes).

**Changed:** `ui/Case3D.kt`, `SUMMARY.md`.

## Update — 22 Oct 2026 (314): Smooth scrolling through 3D cartridges in the carousel

**Status:** Branch `claude/laughing-franklin-xci4p0`, PR to `main` (not merged). Edited in `app/src/main/java/...` and
`app/src/test/...` directly (this cloud checkout has no `src_copy/`): **pull the branch; don't robocopy an older
`src_copy` over these files.** No Android SDK in the cloud workspace — GitHub Actions on the PR is the compile check;
not checked on a handheld.

- **What caused the lag (found before changing anything):**
  1. *Off-screen pieces drawn every frame.* "To the edge" (on by default) builds ~15 games each side on the Thor
     (`ceil(12 × screenWidthDp / 600)`), three times that in Box flow / Spine wall; only ~5–7 a side are on screen. Every
     turned 3D cartridge (and 3D case) out of sight still drew all its offscreen pictures each frame.
  2. *Each turned cartridge redrew 5–6 offscreen pictures per frame* (`solidPiece`: face, solid outline, sides, lit face,
     smear, whole). Its sides draw the same layer up to ~130 times a frame (32 slices × 4 smear copies), and Android's
     renderer re-walks and fully re-damages everything under a layer drawn more than once in a frame — so nothing was
     ever reused, and the RenderThread walked the face's layers ~130 times per piece per frame.
  3. *Main-thread stutter:* `CartShellArt` drew each ~640 px shell front (outline, label, text, glitter) synchronously in
     composition as each cartridge came into the carousel, and again when its cover arrived (shared 24-entry cache).
- **Fixes (no models, sizes, art, animations or settings changed):**
  - `Carousel.kt`: `CarouselViewport` (the carousel's box on screen) + per-game `culled` (derivedStateOf, flips only when
    a game crosses a line a quarter screen past the edge, slot width + height of slack). A culled game isn't drawn and its
    turn / yaw / shade lambdas return the last drawn values, so nothing of it is re-recorded while away. It stays composed
    (its art keeps loading ahead).
  - `SolidPiece.kt`: `solidPiece(faceArt = PieceFace(bitmap, aspect))` — when the content is exactly one picture (a drawn
    shell's front), the turned face, outline and sides are made once from the picture as leaf layers (no layer inside),
    so drawing the sides many times never re-damages them; only smear + whole are drawn per frame, and nothing when the
    turn hasn't changed. Without `faceArt` (pack / template / photo cartridges, Save Vault card) it is exactly as before.
  - `CartShellArt` (`CartShells.kt`): applies the solid piece and motion itself (motion now round the solid piece, so a
    hop lifts the turned piece whole); front from cache at once (`CartShells.cachedFrontFor`, `CustomCarts.authenticFront(peek)`),
    else drawn on `Dispatchers.Default` keeping the previous front while the cover arrives; a place switching to another
    game still draws synchronously (never shows the old game's piece). `PhysicalMedia.kt` passes `solid` / `motionSeed`.
  - **"To the edge" showed only 2 games each side (user, Flip 2, every look).** Tucked behind spaced its far games
    0.42 middle-game widths apart (update 129's bigger games × 0.62), against 0.27 with 5 each side — so on the Flip 2
    only ~3 centres fitted (the third cut by the edge). `Carousel.EDGE_STEP` 0.4: as close as 5 each side's, games kept
    at their bigger size; ~5 a side on the Flip 2, more on wider screens. The other views' spacing is unchanged.
  - Off-screen check measured against the carousel's own box (cull only past a whole box width beyond either edge),
    not window coordinates, which can go stale during a page slide.
  - PR #5's Stacks-only cap of 5 games each side is not wanted (user) — not carried over; PR #5 closed.
  - **Video previews (carried over from `fix/video-preview-background-priority-313`, the one part `main`'s update 313
    lacked):** a background picture picked for the game itself (Artwork & details) is never covered by its gameplay clip
    either — `allowsFullscreenGameplayVideo(style, pickedBackground)`, both the home and Hero carousel clips. Test added
    to `BackgroundVideoPolicy313Test`. With this, every fix branch's wanted change is in this PR or already in `main`.
  - `PieceFit.kt` (new): `pieceArtRect` (CartShellArt's exact pixel placement, so flat ↔ turned never shifts) and
    `carouselOffScreen`.
- **Tests:** `app/src/test/.../CarouselPerf314Test.kt` (11 tests: placement rounding for wide / tall / mismatched
  pictures, on / near / far off screen, unknown sizes, "To the edge" shows at least as many as 5 each side) — passed locally with Kotlin 2.2.10 + JUnit 4.13.2. The rest
  needs the PR's CI (assembleDebug + unit tests). **Not tested:** frame times, memory and visuals on AYN Thor / Retroid
  Pocket Classic (no device access) — see the PR for the `dumpsys gfxinfo` steps.

**Changed:** `ui/Carousel.kt`, `ui/SolidPiece.kt`, `ui/CartShells.kt`, `ui/CustomCarts.kt`, `ui/PhysicalMedia.kt`,
`ui/PieceFit.kt` (new), `ui/BackgroundVideoPolicy.kt`, `ui/LauncherScreen.kt`, `BackgroundVideoPolicy313Test.kt`, `app/src/test/java/com/shelf/launcher/ui/CarouselPerf314Test.kt` (new), `SUMMARY.md`.

## Update — 22 Oct 2026 (313): Respect selected home background over gameplay previews

**Status:** Changes saved on branch `fix/background-video-respect-selection-313`, [draft PR #4](https://github.com/dzepdzep/Voltcap/pull/4); not yet merged or published. The existing v0.6.32 release is untouched. Code level review complete, CI and handheld checks pending.

- **Root cause:** `LauncherScreen.HomeLayer` draws `VideoCrossfade` *after* the user's chosen background. Its old `backdropClip` excludes only Black and some layouts, so a gameplay video can cover a wallpaper or animated scene once the selected game rests for two seconds. The Hero carousel path also had no background-choice guard.
- **Fix:** New pure helper `allowsFullscreenGameplayVideo` in `ui/BackgroundVideoPolicy.kt` permits fullscreen gameplay previews only when the effective background is **Game art** or **Blurred art**. The wallpaper, animated scene (including per-game theme override) and Black backgrounds are respected in both regular home and Hero carousel. Existing `VideoCrossfade` fades, looping, sounds and preview fetching are left alone.
- **Unchanged:** The global video-preview on/off toggle, sound preference, any video in the Gaming room monitor, the video/details pages, selected wallpaper playback (including GIF / video wallpaper), saved preferences, home layouts, physical-media artwork, and other transitions. Updated the Video previews settings subtitle to explain the behavior.
- **Tests:** Added `BackgroundVideoPolicy313Test.kt` verifying both allowed, three excluded and all enum modes; GitHub Actions source compilation with isolated compile-only Discord stub must pass before merge. Signed APK and real-device visual test are separate.
- **Separate crash report:** User reports VoltCap crashing while showing cartridges in a 3D carousel. Code paths inspected in `Carousel.kt`, `SolidPiece.kt`, `PhysicalMedia.kt`, `MediaInspectView.kt`; no stack trace or repro log available, and GitHub cannot reach the user's local USB ADB server. **Not diagnosed / not fixed.** Collect `adb logcat -b crash -d` immediately after reproducing, and address in a *separate* minimal patch. Do not switch off 3D effects or remove features without evidence.
- **Separate installation log:** `:app:installDebug` compiled Kotlin but failed with ADB `No connected devices`, unrelated to the background preference or crash. The user must authorize USB debugging / confirm `adb devices` before trying to install.

**Changed:** `ui/LauncherScreen.kt`, `ui/BackgroundVideoPolicy.kt`, `ui/SettingsDialog.kt`, `app/src/test/java/com/shelf/launcher/ui/BackgroundVideoPolicy313Test.kt`, `SUMMARY.md`.

## Update — 22 Oct 2026 (311): Investigate N64 Shelf vs Inspect mismatch, release safety

- **Tarzan real-spine exception (user's follow-up):** Some N64 games, such as Tarzan, already display their genuine artwork spine; Super Mario 64 and Superman show generated dark title spines in Inspect. Do **not** force one common N64 spine, or treat every N64 title as having a missing scan. Resolve each game independently, prioritize a usable game's own `Spine` scan when Matching spines and R1 Spine override are off, and preserve its real proportions. A real scan might be absent, delayed, incompatible, or intentionally overridden; user screenshots alone do not prove which for each title.
- **Update 311 source verification:** GitHub Actions `Verify Android update 310` succeeded on exact commit `53a90c62f95ee6674af6481644b7f2168b563dd2` (runs <https://github.com/dzepdzep/Voltcap/actions/runs/39774297334> and <https://github.com/dzepdzep/Voltcap/actions/runs/39774289193>) with the CI-only Discord stub, Gradle debug assemble and JVM unit tests. This is NOT a real release build, and no Flip 2 / Thor device check happened in this session.
- **Publishing access audit, 22 Oct 2026:** Latest published signed release remains `v0.6.30` on GitHub. No signed v0.6.31 APK or DM profile files from Claude's local PC are present in this chat, its Library, or the GitHub releases; this session cannot see the PC's USB ADB server or the local APK output. Available GitHub connector has no create-release/upload-asset action. Never re-label v0.6.30 or upload the stubbed CI debug build as 0.6.31. Only the original production-signed APK that was *actually built from the final merged revision* can be released.


**Status:** Changes on `fix/dual-screen-controls-310`, draft PR #1. **No device access from this ChatGPT GitHub connection**: user has the Flip 2 physically connected with USB/ADB enabled, but the connected GitHub tool cannot reach that PC's local ADB server. Do not claim a Flip 2 test or release; last public APK is still v0.6.30.

- **Verified main first:** Main is still Claude's update 309. Checked `ShelfHome.kt`, `MediaInspectView.kt`, `Case3D.kt`, `CaseCatalog.kt`, `MediaCovers.kt`, `BoxTexture.kt`, and release script before editing. No main or published APK was changed.
- **Confirmed a mismatched precedence rule:** `ShelfHome.kt`'s `SpineBody` uses `Features.spinesOwn` ("Matching spines") to suppress per-game real spine scans and pick the console-wide/custom spine. The inspected 3D case's `Case3D` did *not* honor that setting, so N64 cardboard-game spines could suddenly change to scanned spines only in Inspect. Updated `Case3D.kt` to follow the shelf's matching-spine precedence and to skip waiting for unused scans when matching/for-all is selected.
- **Screenshot diagnosis (4 screenshots supplied):** Super Mario 64 is correct on the shelf but Inspect shows an extra triangular/duplicated N64 corner on the box front; when rotated, it shows a generic dark title spine. Superman's front is much closer, but its inspected left spine is also the generated dark title spine. Other individual games differ. This gives concrete visual evidence of a *per-game artwork selection and fitting mismatch*; no new APK has been visually tested.
- **Inspect front source fix:** `MediaInspectView.kt`'s `InspectCase` now detects when `InspectPiece.front` is the game's original `BoxTexture.front` scan and passes `realFront=true` to `Case3D`. Previously `Case3D` assumed the already-selected scan was ordinary cover art and might composite the N64 console frame over the already-complete retail box front. Reuses the existing scan system; non-scanned covers still keep the template.
- **Keep a valid spine scan:** `Case3D.kt`'s `boxSideSpine` no longer drops the real cardboard-spine bitmap entirely when its width/height differs by over 30% from the measured case side (the update-308 rule). It now fits the existing scan inside the 3D side with its original proportions and fills spare space from the scan's border colour. It does not invent a missing scan; the generated spine is still a fallback if no scan exists. An unusual source (e.g., a box's top-edge print) still needs on-device visual judgment.
- **Not yet resolved:** N64 front-cover mismatch seen by the user on Flip 2. The shelf and 3D Inspect use different rendering paths (e.g. `PulledOutCase` / `CoverCase` versus `InspectCase` / `Case3D`), and Inspect may select a boxed-front scan where shelf uses a framed cover; the *specific* visual cause cannot be established without screen capture. Compare the *same N64 game* on shelf and Inspect with identical settings before modifying artwork transforms. Check real N64 region orientation, spine scan vs long top edge, crop/fold flaps, and whether any image source is incorrectly chosen. Preserve correct shelf appearance and other systems.
- **Release script:** `tools/release/release.ps1` now preserves `versionCode=37` when `versionName=0.6.31` has already been staged, instead of silently incrementing it to 38; for a genuinely new version the old increment behavior is retained.
- **Build verification:** CI-only compilation from update 310 passed at <https://github.com/dzepdzep/Voltcap/actions/runs/39770672317>. Update 311 still needs its own completed CI source compile, followed by a *real* local build with the genuine Discord SDK and signing key, and device tests. CI stub artifacts are never releasable.

**Changed:** `app/src/main/java/com/shelf/launcher/ui/MediaInspectView.kt`, `app/src/main/java/com/shelf/launcher/ui/Case3D.kt`, `tools/release/release.ps1`, `SUMMARY.md`. No changes to Discord production functionality or N64 artwork assets.

## Update — 22 Oct 2026 (310): Dual-screen dashboard access, shared category picker and gliding-category stability

**Status:** Source changes prepared on branch `fix/dual-screen-controls-310` and opened as [draft PR #1](https://github.com/dzepdzep/Voltcap/pull/1) for review. **Not merged into main, compiled and unit-tested in CI-only stub mode, not installed, not device-tested, not released.** Last published release remains **0.6.30**. Claude's original update 309 and all earlier work remain on `main`.

- **Checked Claude's work first.** Verified latest `main` commit `555df82` (update 309) and existing code for all five two-screen layouts. Twin Icons already has Mixed / Dark / Light themes; its implementation was left unchanged. Twin Desk, Twin Icons and both Pocket layouts already had native buttons to open the regular second-screen dashboard. Twin Showcase was missing this access. No duplicate dashboard subsystem was built.
- **Regular second-screen pages from dual layouts.** Added a saved **Open normal second screen** switch (on by default) in shared twin layout options. Existing native shortcuts honor it. Twin Showcase gets a compact **Second screen** button on the lower screen. Pocket Classic gets a fallback button when its optional bottom toolbar is hidden. The normal second-screen page and dock are reused; the existing back button returns to the dual-layout lower screen. No second-screen pages, widgets, media mixer or game data were duplicated.
- **Option for categories on dual-screen layouts.** Added **Additional category bar** (off by default) for Twin Desk, Twin Icons, Twin Showcase, Pocket Classic and Pocket Ribbon. It uses the current category stops and follows the existing **Categories: All / Current only / Off** setting. **Current only** shows the current label; tap it to expand the selectable category pills and tap **Done** to collapse again. **All** shows the selectable pills immediately. **Off** shows no shared bar. Each original layout's own built-in category navigation remains usable rather than being replaced.
- **Hidden/current category case.** Fixed Twin Showcase's built-in category pill tap when the current stop is `-1` (a saved category that is now hidden); it uses the existing Pocket category-step helper, as other Pocket category navigation does.
- **Flashing/jitter candidate.** `GlidingChipRow` previously restarted its scroll animation whenever a chip remeasured, potentially repeatedly on dual-screen presentation changes. The animation now starts on changes to the selected category or viewport/count and waits for the selected chip to be measured instead of restarting on every layout pass. This is a code-level fix for a plausible cause, **not yet a visual confirmation** that the reported flashing is gone.
- **Native category bar setting.** Twin Desk stops drawing its permanent native category label when Categories is set to **Off**. The shared category expansion state resets when a new home layout is selected.
- **User's video reviewed (5.42 seconds).** On the AYN Thor, Green Core's top screen stays visible while the standard category pills repeatedly appear and disappear. This is whole-bar visibility flicker, not a proven scroll-animation glitch. `LauncherScreen` now determines category-title fallback using the actual Green Core page (and stable title rules for several dual-screen layouts), instead of relying on the global native-title count that can include a different screen. **This still needs a fresh device video after installing the build.**
- **Build verification:** Added `.github/workflows/verify-update-310.yml` to test/debug-build on GitHub Actions without release signing, saving test results and a **debug-only** artifact. The initial run failed because the setup-android action requested an obsolete SDK `tools` package; the workflow now uses the hosted runner's SDK. CI reached Gradle but is blocked by the absent local Discord SDK AAR.
- **Version staged:** `app/build.gradle.kts` has `versionCode = 37`, `versionName = "0.6.31"`. No APK was published, no tag was created, and the existing v0.6.30 release is unchanged.
- **CI-only compile workaround and successful test (no Discord removed from real builds).** `app/build.gradle.kts` has a guarded `-PvoltcapCiWithoutDiscord=true` mode that works **only** on GitHub Actions. It excludes the proprietary AAR and CMake bridge for the check, supplying one isolated Java API stub at `app/src/ciDiscordStubs/java/com/discord/socialsdk/DiscordSocialSdkInit.java`. The PR workflow runs `:app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebug` but **does not upload or publish the stubbed APK**. On 22 Oct 2026, <https://github.com/dzepdzep/Voltcap/actions/runs/39770672317> finished **successfully**, including the Gradle build and JVM tests. This verifies Kotlin/Compose builds without the proprietary dependency but does **not** validate the production Discord SDK, signed release, or on-device category flashing.
- **CI blocker confirmed:** On the corrected Android runner, the build reaches Gradle but fails in `processDebugNavigationResources`: the required `app/libs/discord/lib/release/discord_partner_sdk.aar` is missing from the public GitHub checkout. This is the Discord Social SDK archive referenced by `app/build.gradle.kts`, not a Kotlin error from this update. It must be available from the exact authorized local SDK installation or an approved private CI source. Do not publish a debug-signed substitute. The CI workflow now detects the missing archive before downloading Android tools.
- **Prior update preserved.** Update 309's Twin Icons `Colours`: Mixed (dark top / light bottom, default), Dark (both dark) and Light (both light) remain unchanged. Update 308 and earlier changes remain as Claude committed them.

**Files changed on branch:** `app/build.gradle.kts`; `.github/workflows/verify-update-310.yml`; `app/src/ciDiscordStubs/java/com/discord/socialsdk/DiscordSocialSdkInit.java`; `app/src/main/java/com/shelf/launcher/data/Features.kt`; `ui/TwinScreens.kt`, `TwinDesk.kt`, `TwinIcons.kt`, `TwinShowcase.kt`, `PocketShared.kt`, `PocketSettings.kt`, `HomeChrome.kt`, `LauncherScreen.kt`; `SUMMARY.md`.

Check RP handheld/one-screen fallbacks where available. Verify that no category flashing remains; if it persists, capture a screen recording and diagnose the real rendering cause. Then set versionCode 37 / versionName 0.6.31, build the compatible signed APK and publish a GitHub release. Do not publish an unverified or differently signed build.

## Update — 21 Oct 2026 (302): case backs from TheGamesDB, unused picture copies cleaned up — after release 0.6.27

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`. **Copied, built (assembleRelease, no errors), unit tests run (all pass) and installed on the AYN Thor.** Committed and pushed by Claude. **Not published.** The Cover Project and MobyGames are left out, as you decided.

- **TheGamesDB backs.** TheGamesDB already sent each game's back cover (`boxart`, side `back`); Voltcap ignored it. Now, with your own TheGamesDB key, a case with **no back scan of its own** (no ScreenScraper back, no full case scan, no pick of yours) asks TheGamesDB for its back **once its back is actually looked at** (turned round in the game window / a case look, or Inspect) — not for every game in the library, so the key's allowance isn't used up. Found backs are kept per game on the device (`TgdbBacks`, prefs `tgdb_backs2`) and go into the game's real-media list as "Back of the box" (so the case, Inspect and Artwork & details all see it, and you can still pick another). TheGamesDB doesn't say which region a back is from.
- **Failures aren't "no back":** a failed look-up (no network, HTTP 429) is not remembered as "none", and TheGamesDB is left alone for an hour after one. A game with no back on TheGamesDB is asked again after two weeks.
- **Cleanup:** copies of your uploaded pictures (`files/user_art`, Update 301) that no pick uses any more are removed at start (in the background; anything copied in the last hour is kept), with the cuts kept for them.
- Device / repo leftovers from this session removed (screenshots, test picture, the test snapshot file, logcat buffer back to 256 KB).

Files touched:
- `src_copy\data\TgdbBacks.kt` (new), `src_copy\data\TheGamesDbApi.kt` (`fetchBack`, failures surfaced), `src_copy\data\PhysicalOverrides.kt` (TheGamesDB back filled in before your picks), `src_copy\data\UserArt.kt` (`cleanup`), `src_copy\data\FullScanCuts.kt` (`dropMissingFiles`)
