## Update — 21 Oct 2026 (300): cartridge accuracy — ROM headers pick the Game Boy Color / DSi card, Japanese Gold & Silver, Disk System disks, white Nintendo Power carts, DS card thickness — after release 0.6.26

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`. **Copied, built (assembleRelease, no errors), unit tests run (all pass) and installed on the AYN Thor.** Committed and pushed by Claude. **Not published.** The full audit (system, variant, region, before, change, source, VERIFIED / ESTIMATED / CONFLICTING / UNCONFIRMED) is `docs\physical_media\CARTRIDGE_AUDIT_300.md` (also in the project as `CARTRIDGE_AUDIT_300.md`).

- **Game Boy / Color from the ROM header (new `data/RomHeaders.kt`).** Byte 0x0143 (Pan Docs): 80h → the black dual-mode Game Pak, C0h → the clear Color-only one, anything else → the grey Game Boy one. Only trusted when the header checksum matches; read on a background thread, 0x240 bytes, from plain files, content addresses and .zip (the first ROM inside); .7z stays unknown. Kept with the file's size and date (a changed file is read again; an unreadable one is retried once per run). The "(GB Compatible)" file-name tag is now only the fallback. Your picks, console styles and verified editions still come first; console, emulator, launch, saves untouched. On the Thor: header read confirmed (Pokémon Picross (Proto) → 80h). On Toni's library 6 untagged GBC files are 80h (e.g. The Smurfs' Nightmare (USA), South Park (Proto)); Pokémon Yellow is 80h on the GB list but keeps its own yellow edition.

- **DS: white DSi-exclusive card from the header** (unit code 03h; Game Verifying / Wikipedia). DSiWare (title-ID category 00030004 — Cave Story, Dragon Quest Wars, Game & Watch… on Toni's Thor) were never on a card and keep the standard one. `dsi_white` (existing material) is used for the first time. No DSi-only retail card is in the library, so the white card itself wasn't seen on the device.
- **DS card 3.64 mm thick** (Game Verifying), was 3.8.
- **Pocket Monsters Kin / Gin (Japan): verified and automatic** — dark-blue front / dark-grey back, Gin the opposite (Game Verifying's DMG guide). Western Gold / Silver, Crystal unchanged.
- **NTR-031 infrared cards: Korea added** (Game Verifying lists Korean releases).

- **Famicom Disk System (.fds, also .fds.zip):** drawn as the FDS disk, not an NES / Famicom cartridge. The scanner still files them under NES (emulator and launch unchanged).
- **Nintendo Power GB Memory and SF Memory: white** (MarioWiki, Bulbapedia — text sources); were dark grey / grey placeholders.
- **Zipped ROM names** ("… [patched].gbc.zip"): the ROM's own ending is dropped too, so the edition matches (Pokémon Silver [patched] had no edition).

Added / changed:
- **Volume Mixer widget** (`builtin:VOLUME_MIXER`): media volume (Android's own, follows the volume keys), each app's volume where the mixer works (AppMixer), mute / unmute, a key that opens the full mixer on the main screen. Compact = media only; Normal = + the app playing; Expanded = up to six apps. Added from Settings › Second screen tools, or from the board itself (Edit › Add).

- **Editor:** tap a widget (or reach it with the controller) to pick it; its tools appear above the board (always in view on the small lower screen): ◀ ▶ move, size (Compact / Normal / Expanded — only the sizes another app's widget allows: its resize mode and min/max height), ↺ back to its default size, ✕ remove. - **Thor top/bottom-screen volume — investigated, not shown:** `Settings.System secondary_screen_volume_level` (0–15, default 7; the Thor has 4) is watched by AYN's `com.odin.settings`, which turns it into `persist.sys.audio.value` (a gain table) and re-applies the music volume. Checked: changing the setting changes the property (then put back to 4). Writing it needs the system shell or root (a non-public System setting); `…_for_headphones` is declared but nothing uses it. Whether it actually changes one screen's loudness can only be judged by ear — not confirmed, so no control is shown yet. Retroid Pocket Duo: not available here, nothing documented found — not shown.

- **Your cartridge pack (Custom cartridges):** each pack shape gets the connector end of the real cartridge it's drawn after — Game Boy, N64, SNES, GBA, NES, Famicom, Genesis, Game Gear, DS, 3DS, Switch, Atari 2600 — fitted to the shell in the picture (the pack's pictures have a clear margin of 1.5–5 % round the shell, measured; the same for every console and both finishes). ## Update — 20 Oct 2026 (275): cartridge bottoms in 3D — the opening, its walls, the board and the gold contacts at their real count, for 54 cartridges — after release 0.6.19

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`. **Copied, built, installed (with the start-up profile) and checked on the Retroid Pocket Flip 2**, committed and pushed by Claude (Toni's OK). **Published as Voltcap 0.6.20.**

- **Before:** the turned cartridge's bottom was a flat face with a picture on it (a dark strip, a green line), so from below or at an angle it was plain plastic.
- **Now** each connector end is real geometry seen through a hole: the opening with its inner walls and ceiling at depth (and up the back where the real shell is cut away: Game Boy family, DS / 3DS / Switch cards), the board inside as a solid slab (bevelled where the real one is), each gold finger at the published count and pitch, plus ribs, dust plates, doors, notches and second boards where the real cartridge has them. Flat-shaded, lit from the upper left, drawn far to near; the front, back, labels, colours, sway and turn are unchanged.
- **Which ones:** 54 drawn shells, and cartridge photos / templates of the same console (they get their console's numbers, stretched to fit). 13 stay plain on purpose (disks, flat-pad cards like HuCard / Sega Card / Lynx / MMC, the Virtual Boy's cap, and four with no description of their connector end).
- **How sure:** contact counts and pitches are published (NESdev, SNESdev, ConsoleMods, replica KiCad footprints, patents); opening sizes, depths and board recess are estimates (no photo of a real bottom could be opened). Full table with sources: `CARTRIDGES.md` › Bottoms.
- **Checked on the Flip 2:** 22 shells, each from below-front, straight under and below-behind, before and after (`Claude outputs\hold274A\cart_bottoms_1…6.jpg`); the other 32 in PC previews only (`sheet0…8.png`). Fixed on the way: the DS / 3DS pocket lines up with the drawn back's connector window. Frame times turning under a Mega Drive cartridge: p50 14 → 12 ms, p95 19 → 17 ms, p99 22 → 24 ms (no measurable cost; nothing is drawn unless the bottom or back opening shows).

Files (`src_copy\`): `ui\CartUnderside.kt`, `ui\MediaInspectView.kt`; `CARTRIDGES.md` (Bottoms section).

## Update — 20 Oct 2026 (274): Inspect / Wobble, a piece sways when left alone, Inspect… in every game's menu, Save Vault Inspect returns and sways, the three wide-capsule looks, Stats round shortcut, play time from Recents, popup fixes — after release 0.6.19

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`. **Copied, built, installed (with the start-up profile) and checked on the Retroid Pocket Flip 2**, committed and pushed by Claude. **Published as Voltcap 0.6.20.**

- **Couldn't find the inspect view:** it only came up when the look draws cartridges, discs or cases. Every game's menu (START) now has **Inspect…**, which brings its cartridge / card / disc (else its case) out in the game window whatever the look. Checked on the Flip 2: Donkey Konga 2's disc came out with the Covers look.
- **Inspect or Wobble** (Settings › Game look › Covers, cases & discs › More look options › In the game window), asked once after this update: *Inspect* = turn it by hand; *Wobble* = no turning by hand, it just sways like the pieces on the home rows. Back / outside leaves the question for next time; only a pick counts.
- **Left alone it goes back to its animation:** after the 2-second turn back (on by default, as before) the piece sways gently ±24° ("Sway when left alone", on). Any touch, the stick, Y or a tap stops it where it is (no jump).
- **Save Vault:** tap the save's object in its details to Inspect it ("Tap to inspect" under it). In Inspect, left alone for the hold it turns back to face you (and its own size, in the middle), then sways. Checked on the Flip 2 with Pokémon Silver's card: dragged, it came back after ~3 s and swayed. Nothing about the save is touched.
- **Wide capsules, three looks under Covers › Cover style:** *Wide capsules* (every game wide, the ones beside too), *Wide · first game only* (a fixed capsule, no animation, the others covers), *Wide · when you're on it* (cover → wide capsule animation). "Wide capsules" is gone from Art (it was the same look twice) and the separate "The game you're on" choice is folded into these.
- **Stats round shortcut** (bar chart, next to Achievements): opens Play stats; hide it like the others in Settings › Home › Round shortcuts.
- **Play time (Silver showed 3 h, played on the RP Classic):** Voltcap is the home screen, so Home pressed mid-game ended the session and going back to the game from Recents was never counted. Now any game still open from an earlier launch gets the time it was really on screen while Voltcap was away (Android's usage record, Usage access needed). Measured sessions are no longer cut to 8 h (that stays only for the wall-clock fallback). Time already lost can't be recovered.
- **After an in-app update Voltcap opens itself again** (it left the Flip 2 on the Retroid launcher until Home was pressed): only as the home app, with the screen on.
- **Popups:** the Game look choices' text was cut with "…" — now shown in full, cards as tall as the tallest; R1 tile names no longer break mid-word ("Achievement / s") or end in "…"; the game window beside an inspected piece had its "Saves / Performance" line squeezed to two empty slivers — room made; Save Vault's save list rows ran into each other — taller; Save Vault details' buttons centred and a little lower; the battery-saver note's buttons centred.
- **Two-line names:** the name under a card switched between two heights when it started scrolling (one frame or two), nudging the row; both now sit in the same fixed-height box. Recorded on the Flip 2 in the Grid and the Voltcap row: no vertical movement of the row (within 0.4 px).
- Testing hook (adb only, with `voltcap_test_hooks`): `--es voltcap_test_inspect "Game|shellId|yaw|pitch"`.

## Update — 20 Oct 2026 (271): Charging log for the RP Classic heat (#99) — read-only; list of what's left (`Claude outputs\LEFT_TO_DO.md`) — after release 0.6.18

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`. **Copied, built, installed (with the start-up profile) and checked on the Retroid Pocket Flip 2**, committed and pushed by Claude. **Published as Voltcap 0.6.19.**

**Charging log (new, read-only — it never changes a charging setting).** While the handheld charges, Voltcap notes once a minute (and at plug / unplug): time, battery %, charger (charger / USB), charging status, battery temperature, chip temperature (through the vendor root service), voltage, current, screen on / off, and Voltcap or another app in front. It's kept 7 days in `Android/data/com.shelf.launcher/files/charge_log.csv` (readable over USB, so the RP Classic can be charged on the 65 W charger away from the PC and read later). Diagnostics › Device › Charging log shows the hottest moment ("Hottest: battery 25.7 °C at 10-20 07:52 (charger, screen on) · chip up to 45 °C · 0.1 h logged"). Checked on the Flip 2: rows every minute, Diagnostics line shown, no crash. Not checked: the plug / unplug rows (the Flip 2 stayed plugged in).
Limit: it writes only while Voltcap's process lives (it's the home app, so usually; Android may pause it in deep sleep — the minutes before and after show that).

**What's left:** `Claude outputs\LEFT_TO_DO.md` (also in the project as `claude/LEFT_TO_DO.md`): the open roadmap items, devices without the newest builds, open questions, known rough spots, ideas.

Files (`src_copy\`): `data\ChargeLog.kt` (new), `MainActivity.kt`, `ui\DiagnosticsContent.kt`.

Every switch was put back as it was (Xbox, L2 / R2 Both, Mode Standard, Fan Smart).

- **R1 › Device › L2 / R2 (new):** Both → Analog → Digital, Android's L2/R2 mode (`trigger_input_mode` 2 / 0 / 1). Hold: Android's Handheld Settings. AYN and Retroid.

Retroid's firmware turns the fan Off whenever Mode goes to Standard (its own tile does it too); Voltcap's Mode tile puts your fan setting back. Fan on Retroid: Quiet / Smart / Off (no Sport there).
- **A game's own button layout** (per-game profile) used the old AYN-only writes and missed the gamepad property: it now uses the same switch as the R1 Controller tile, so it works on Retroid too.
- Diagnostics › Device said "Vendor root service: Available (AYN)" on the Flip 2: it names the maker now.
- Settings search checked: all 617 entries lead to a page and group that exist.

## Update — 20 Oct 2026 (268): R1 Controller tile — the handheld's own Xbox / Retro controller style, the same switch as Android's (Retroid too) — after release 0.6.18

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`. **Copied, built, installed (with the start-up profile) and checked on the Retroid Pocket Flip 2** (the Odin 2 Portal was unplugged), committed and pushed by Claude. **Published as Voltcap 0.6.19.**

**R1 › Device › Controller (Xbox / Retro).** Press: switches the built-in controller between Xbox and Retro layout. Hold: opens Android's Handheld Settings (Input › Controller style). It writes exactly what Android's own Controller style does — read off the Flip 2 by switching Android's Quick Settings tile and comparing before / after: `temp_abxy_layout_mode` (0 Xbox / 1 Retro), `flip_button_layout` (1 / 0) and `persist.sys.gamepad.type` (1 / 0; before, Voltcap's old Buttons tile didn't set this one). Checked both ways on the Flip 2: Voltcap's tile → Android's tile shows Retro; Android's tile → Voltcap's tile follows. Android's third choice, Disconnect (2 / 0 / no_create 1 / prop 2), shows as "Disconnected"; a press brings the controller back as Xbox (checked: the "Xbox Wireless Controller" input device is back). The tile now shows on every handheld whose firmware has the switch (found by its setting, with the vendor's root service) — before, AYN only.
Also Settings › Controls › Button legend: "Handheld's controller style" — Xbox / Retro / Handheld Settings, the same switch.
The Flip 2 was left on Xbox, as it was.

## Update — 19 Oct 2026 (265): Metacritic scores filled in from RAWG on their own (no file needed); Settings tidied — duplicates gone, music switches under Audio, crash reports and Restart under Diagnostics — after release 0.6.16

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`. **Copied, built, installed (with the start-up profile) and checked on the Odin 2 Portal and the Flip 2**, committed and pushed by Claude. **Published as Voltcap 0.6.17.**

**Metacritic sort without a file.** A bundled Metacritic file was left out on purpose (the scores are licensed, the data set has no licence). Instead: when a category is sorted by Metacritic or Critic score and a free RAWG key is connected (Settings › Accounts), Voltcap looks up the missing scores on RAWG by itself, one game every ~1 s in the background, and doesn't ask again for 30 days for a game RAWG doesn't know. The Sort window shows the progress ("Looking up missing scores on RAWG: 7 / 62…") or how to connect RAWG. Loading your own scores file still works as before.

**Settings, simpler.**
- Audio › Background music now holds "Pause music when closed" and "Also pause when locking" (were under Device).
- Diagnostics now holds Restart Voltcap and the crash reports (were at the end of Device › This device); "This device" starts folded with a one-line summary.
- Duplicates removed: "Lights off with the screensaver" (stays in Theme › Controller lights), Overlay/Performance notification switches (stay in Device › Notifications), "Video previews" in Home › Extras (stays in Audio), the second "Use the second screen" switch on Screens (the fold is now just "Home app").
- Clearer names: "Only the game you're on spins", "Only the cover you're on animates", Spacing "Roomy / Tight".
- Pointers fixed: lyrics → Home › Music player, sounds → Audio, scraping → Accounts, RomM permissions → Settings › Permissions; Diagnostics has its own icon.
- Settings search: 24 entries for pages that no longer exist removed; new ones for Permissions, Allow everything, Restart Voltcap, In-game Quick menu, Spacing.

## Update — 19 Oct 2026 (254): the tuner's "stock" clocks survive a Voltcap restart (#96 / #104); RP Classic GBC frame check; Pokémon Silver copies compared (#101)

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`. **Copied, built, installed on the Thor and the RP Classic** by Claude, committed and pushed by Claude.

**Copy `src_copy`**, changed (1): `src_copy\device\tune\Tuner.kt`. **Files to delete:** none.

- **Found on the RP Classic (#96, with your OK to change tiers for the test — put back to Stock afterwards):** its clocks sat at exactly Voltcap's Balanced caps — little 1.29 GHz, big 1.65 GHz, GPU 605 MHz — with the power tile on **Stock**, and **Max didn't lift them either**. Cause: the tuner reads the "stock" clocks when Voltcap starts. When Voltcap restarted while its own Balanced caps were on the chip (an app update, Android ending the process), it read those caps as the device's own, and from then on Stock and Max put back… the caps. The AYN handhelds rewrite their clocks every 10 s, so it didn't show there; the RP Classic never does (up 14 days).
- **Fix:** the stock clocks are kept on disk with the boot they were read in, plus whether Voltcap's own limits are on the chip. A Voltcap starting again in the same boot with its limits still on takes the kept stock instead of its own caps (written by hand as JSON, so an app update reads it right). Checked on the Thor: Voltcap force-stopped and started again with your Balanced + Underclock Light on — caps re-applied as before, no crash.
- **The RP Classic itself needs one restart** to get its real stock clocks back (nothing Voltcap can write goes above what it thinks stock is) — question 38.
- **GBC frame pacing on the RP Classic:** Mr. Driller (a GBC cartridge without a save battery — no save file was made, checked) in RetroArch / Gambatte, GL driver, at those caps: 35 s, 2110 frames, **100 % at 16.7 ms, none late**. The GBC stutter from #96 didn't show; I'll measure again after the restart and with your Pokémon setup only if you want (it needs a game with a save).
- **#101 Pokémon Silver (read-only):** every copy compared by in-game play time — the current save (44 h 27 min) is the furthest; you have two Silver ROMs that show the same name (one `[patched]`, empty save, started 17 Oct 18:03). Report: `Claude outputs\evidence\101_silver_progress_2026-10-19.md`, question 36.

## Update — 19 Oct 2026 (248): disc data side read from the image itself (#89 finding 11), case sizes in your case region (#89 finding 15)

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`. **Copied, unit-tested and built** by Claude, committed and pushed by Claude.

**Copy `src_copy`**, changed (2): `src_copy\ui\DiscUnderside.kt`, `src_copy\ui\PhysicalMedia.kt`. **Copy `project_copy`** (new): `project_copy\app\src\test\java\com\shelf\launcher\ui\DiscImagesTest.kt` (11 tests). **Files to delete:** none.

1. **Disc underside (the disc's data side when you turn it over)**: a PS2 game's disc was a CD-ROM (blue) whenever its image was under 900 MB, and every .img / .mds / .mdf counted as a CD. Now the image says it itself: a plain image (.iso, .img, .mdf, .bin) with UDF's descriptors is a DVD (PS2 DVDs always have them), raw 2352-byte frames are a CD; a .cue / .ccd / .mds is read through its data file; a CHD by its sector size (on the Thor all PS2 CHDs use 2048-byte sectors, so only ones bigger than an 80-minute CD — 737 MB — count as DVDs, smaller ones by size as before). Compressed .cso / .zso still go by size.
2. **"Cases · real sizes"**: keep cases, card cases and the plain jewel case took North America's size whatever Settings › Game look › Case region said. They take that region now (a Japanese GameCube case is smaller). With the default "from the file name, else North America" nothing changes.

Nothing looks different.

Measured with system traces (atrace; the Thor's perfetto crashes in its own ftrace reader) on Case stacks › Box flow, Game Boy Advance (357 games), 30 quick presses ▶:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| frames drawn | 93–120 | 459–512 |
| median frame | 200–300 ms | 19–25 ms |
| 90 % of frames under | 400 ms | 80–90 ms |
| textures re-uploaded per frame | ~25 (13 MB) | ~0 |

1. **Every game in a row was thrown away and built again on each step** — in most layouts. A `continue` inside the loop that places the games made the Compose compiler give each pass of the loop a group of its own, so a game's key was only looked up inside its own pass; one step moved every game one place along, and all of them (about a hundred 3D cases in Box flow) were made from scratch. The places are now picked before the loop. Fixed in the carousel and in the same pattern in Case stacks, the classic dock row, Tiles, Arcade, Card binder, Circuit, Console stack, Console homes, Cross menu, Pocket Quest, Record crate, Shelf, Twin desk and the anchored strip.
2. **3D cases at the sides drew their full 480 px pictures.** About sixty to a hundred cases (with reflections) needed more picture memory than the GPU keeps, so a dozen to fifty pictures were uploaded again every frame. A case seen small or turned (its front a tall sliver) now draws a half / quarter / eighth-size copy (across and down apart), kept in its own store — what the GPU showed there anyway. The reflection's off-screen layer is now only as deep as its fade reaches (nothing below it ever showed).
3. **Case stacks' bottom panel** (arched top and lit edge) is drawn once into its own layer: its two path masks (1862 × 287 and 1862 × 61) were rebuilt and uploaded every frame the carousel moved.
4. **Carousel**: each game's place function is kept inside its own group (a new one every step made every game rebuild).

5. **Save safety (#70 / #73 / #74).** Every save is classified (in-game file, memory-card image, folder card, folder save, title folder, export, state). Saves made of several files (3DS / Wii title folders, PSP folders) that changed on both devices become a conflict as a whole instead of mixing the two devices' halves. A loose title match or one fitting several games is no longer assigned to the first game: it goes to Other saves with "fits N games here — not assigned". The three-way rule and backups are unchanged.
6. **Faster first sync and live list (#68 / #76).** Missing files download 4 at a time (still checked and backed up by the sync); the vault shows a quick local list first, then the full one, and refreshes after each folder that received files and when a sync started elsewhere finishes. Full matrix: `SAVE_DETECTION_MATRIX.md`.
7. **Presets (#110).** All 73 presets audited (`PRESET_AUDIT.md`). Four that looked like another preset now differ in what their layout really draws: "Cross menu · square tiles", "Hub on your theme", "Live tiles on art", "Rounded icon bar" (art behind the top). Spotlight presets set their tile shape; "TV room 3D" uses the Cartridges look; all TV room presets set "case you're on facing you". Nine previews now draw what the preset sets. Ids kept, so saved presets still work.
8. **Edit Home (#05 / #06).** Parts snap to a 2 % grid (faint grid while dragging); D-pad moves one step (two while held); **hold A + D-pad** resizes (▲▼ bigger / smaller, ◀▶ narrower / wider); toolbar "⟲ Reset layout" (undoable); Line up keeps the other axis. Hero tiles: a part dropped inside the Big picture's dashed inner area goes *inside* it (moves with it, drawn above it, focused first); "Take out of… / Put inside…" in the part's panel.
9. **Quick Settings overlay tile (#82).** Tapping Voltcap's tile in Android's pull-down while a game runs now shows / hides the overlay at once — also for games started outside Voltcap or after Android ended Voltcap's process, on the game's own screen (Thor); if Android refuses the start it opens a hidden hop and collapses the shade. The tile shows "on" only when the overlay is really on screen, otherwise why ("No trophies for this game · tap to retry").

1. **Cartridge labels (#90).** GBA label 43 × 22 mm, centred, 1 mm corners (ConsoleMods, test-fitted; was 50 wide). SNES (US) sticker 82.5 mm wide with square top corners and 3 mm bottom corners, 37 mm on the front + 7 mm over the top (ConsoleMods 82.5 × 44, 7 mm fold). NES unchanged — its 97 × 48 front window is the 97 × 55 sticker minus the 7 mm fold, so it was right. A label *scan* that includes the fold strip has it cropped off instead of being squashed. Clear Game Boy Color backs lose the grey Game Boy's power-lock notch (GBC carts don't have it). Left as they are, with reasons in the code: GBA thickness (8 vs 9 mm in sources), Super Famicom / PAL label, Genesis label.
2. **Cartridge bottoms (#92).** In the inspect view, tilting a cartridge to look underneath now shows its insertion edge — the opening, the green board and, where the pitch is published, the gold contact rows (NES 36 × 2.5 mm, Famicom 30 × 2.54 mm, SNES main block, after nesdev / ConsoleMods) — for NES, Famicom, SNES, Super Famicom, N64, Genesis / Mega Drive, Master System, Game Boy / Color / Advance, Game Gear. Opening widths from the measured backs; wall and board depths are estimates (marked in the code). Cards (DS, 3DS, Switch, HuCard) keep the plain edge.
3. **Case views (#26 / #27 / #58).** GoldenEye and every N64 / SNES game no longer show as a flat strip with "Box turned to show its spine": those consoles' template box was drawn lying on its back; they now stand as real 3D boxes of the catalog's shape (N64 181 × 127 × 32 mm) turned to show their real spine — in the Grid, carousels, Case stacks, hero carousel, tile home and the game row. A wide box scan no longer stretches a case (shape from the catalog, ±8 %), and a full unfolded box scan (back + spine + front) is cut to its front. Grid cases now get the game's real spine scan even with a picked cover. Thickness comes from the catalog when the spine scan disagrees by over 25 %; a real spine is cropped to the side, not stretched. The fallback spine is now the console's colour with the title and the console logo, sized for the real case. Consoles without a template case but with their own case scan (PS3–PS5, Xbox) draw as a scanned case in the Grid instead of a cropped flat picture.
4. **3D case bottom (#117).** The 3D case now has a bottom face, so a case in the inspect view tilts all the way round like the other pieces.
5. **Art-driven colours (#23).** Colours that follow the game / music are now kept readable: the accent is lightened or darkened (same hue) to reach 3:1 against the background and panels and 4.5:1 for text on it; light themes swap to the palette's text colour when needed; near-grey covers keep the theme's accent; small logos can't set the colour (a colour must cover 4 % of the picture). The accent fades as smoothly as the background and changes after you rest ~300 ms on a game. Your own accent is never changed. Settings › Colours follow: new **Your colours** chip (back to your Custom colours) and **Keep my accent** (backgrounds follow the art, the accent stays yours). Text on the accent now picks black or white by real contrast.
6. **Disc tiles (#32 / #57).** In the game row, round discs carry their trophy count and status on a strip under the disc instead of over its curve; the console badge stays top-left. Game look (Discs looks): **Counts under the disc** switch (on). An Android app with no art shows its whole icon on the disc instead of a blown-up one cut by the hub.

1. **Cube menu home (#93).** A new optional layout, "Cube menu" (all other layouts unchanged). A big glass cube, inspired by the GameCube menu, is the category picker: its four sides are categories (back face relabelled when there are more), top = Apps, bottom = Settings. ◀ ▶ turn it, ▲ ▼ tip it, A opens the face; L2/R2 change category. Opening a face shrinks the cube into a dock (left column or top band) and the category's games slide in as a roomy row with title, info and Play / Details / Cube buttons. On the games: ◀ ▶ games, ▲ the docked cube (turn it to switch category), ▼ the buttons, B back to the big cube. Touch: tap / drag the cube, tap a game to pick, again to open. The cube never covers games, titles or buttons; when the screen is too small it is replaced by a "◆ category" chip. Settings (Edit Home › Cube menu): cube home on/off, dock left / top / hidden, face style, Apps & Settings faces, tint (indigo / lilac / smoke / theme accent), cube size, gentle float, room backdrop, reduced motion. Presets "Cube menu" and "Cube band". The float stops when the home goes calm.
2. **PS2 browser style (#112).** Save Vault › Filters & look (and Settings › Appearance › Save Vault): **PS2 browser style**, off by default. PS2 saves then show their own PS2 save icon, read from the save's icon.sys and .ico on the memory card (card images and AetherSX2/NetherSX2 folder cards), turning in 3D over the save's own background colours on the dark-blue PS2 browser backdrop, with the save's two-line title and size. Saves without an icon show a plain memory card labelled "No save icon". Read-only: nothing is ever written to a save; icons are cached. Other consoles keep their style.
3. **N64 cartridge label (#40).** The label is now shaped like the real N64 sticker (4 mm top corners, 3 mm bottom corners, top edge curved on a 325 mm diameter, after ConsoleMods' label table). Shell size unchanged (116 × 76.6 × 18.5 mm, ConsoleMods / Wikipedia). Label size left at 57 × 63.5 mm because the sources disagree (54.5 × 62.5 / 50.8 × 60.3 / 57 × 63.5).
4. **PS1 multi-disc cases (#88).** Games with more than one disc (.m3u, "Disc 1 of N", or Disc 1 + Disc 2 files) get the thick double jewel case, 142 × 125 × 25 mm (PSX PAL DB multiway two-disc case), for North American and Japanese releases — marked Estimated, since some used a slim double case. European multi-disc games keep the 17.4 mm Full Jewel case (PSX PAL DB). A PS1 jewel case's thickness now always comes from the catalog, not from the spine scan's shape.
5. **PS2 custom cartridge labels (#34).** PS2 covers on the custom PS2 cartridge are no longer cut down to the square window (losing title and bottom): the cover's own "PlayStation 2" header is cut off, the cover is fitted without stretching and the rest of the label filled with its edge colour. The same label fit is used on every cartridge-pack shape.
6. **App cartridges (#33).** Apps and Android games now use the pack's Switch-card-sized cartridge by default, so icons and covers fit the label. A shape you picked yourself still wins; no real cartridge model is resized.
7. **iiDB (#118) — blocked.** iiSU says a free public API "will be later released"; no API or documentation exists yet (iisu.network/news/introducing-iidb, iidb.iisu.network). Not added; Voltcap does not scrape the site.

### Smoother home (#59 / #60) — found on your Thor's setup (Case stacks with the Box flow carousel, background "Art + videos", colours following the game)
1. Every frame of the colour glide (about 70 frames per game step) built a new Material colour scheme, which rebuilt the whole home screen → the scheme is now built once per colour change; Voltcap's own colours still glide.
2. The carousel rebuilt every game on each of those frames (it was keyed on the accent colour) → only the game you're on reads it now.
3. The game's art behind the home came out as a software bitmap (the sharpening step turned the GPU copy off), uploaded on the UI thread at every step → handed over as a GPU bitmap.
4. The video clip lookup (file hash, file checks, encrypted login read) ran on the UI thread at every step → it waits until you've stopped for 0.4 s and runs in the background; the clip still shows ~2 s after you stop. The clip player is released in the background.
5. The art colours start once you've stopped on a game for ~0.2 s (they only re-glided while moving).

**Measured on the Thor, same settings as yours, before → after:**
- one game every 0.6 s: frame time p50 44 → 11 ms, p90 105 → 14 ms, slow-UI-thread frames 286 → 18 (games seen before); 18 ms p50 on games not seen yet;
- holding ◀ (25 fast steps): p50 65 → 12 ms, janky frames 72 % → 19 %.
Nothing looks different once you stop on a game (colours, art and clip as before). Only stock Android switches/sliders now change colour at once instead of gliding.

### Performance in the classic details window (#81)
- "Classic details window" (Settings › … › Game window style) had no way to the game's own power settings (Options › menu › Game settings, three levels down). It now has a **Performance** button after Favourite (on handhelds Voltcap can tune), opening the same quick rows as the Banner page's Performance tab (power mode, AutoTDP, underclock, fan…, Advanced… → the full game settings).

### Switch games' boxes and cartridges (#39)
- ScreenScraper wasn't told the console for Switch and Wii U games, and big Switch files send no checksum, so it matched by name across every console: a 3DS / Wii U release with the same name was taken and its box, cartridge and label drawn on the Switch game → Switch (225) and Wii U (18) are now sent, and a match on another console is refused (covers too).

- With no scan at all, the Switch case shows the cover in the Switch case (as before).

## Update — 18 Oct 2026 (223): Nintendo 3DS saves show in the Save Vault and sync around 3DS games (#67 / #72)

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`. **Copied, built and installed** on the AYN Thor and the RP Classic by Claude, committed and pushed by Claude.

**Copy `src_copy`**, changed (3): `src_copy\data\CloudSync.kt`, `src_copy\data\MemoryCards.kt`, `src_copy\data\SaveCapsules.kt`. **Files to delete:** none.

### Found (Thor)
Citra keeps 3 game saves in `citra-emu/sdmc/Nintendo 3DS/…/title/00040000/<title id>/data/` (0011c500, 00175e00, 0015c000 — files called `main` or `savedata0–3.dat`). The Save Vault had **no Nintendo 3DS page at all**. Two causes:
1. The library calls the 3DS **"n3ds"** (ES-DE's name); the code only knew **"3ds"** — so a 3DS game had no save folder: no sync before / after it, no watcher, nothing in the vault.
2. The vault never read the Citra folder on the device; 3DS saves could only appear after a sync job had recorded them for a game played through Voltcap.

### What changed
1. "n3ds" (and any platform name with "3ds") is the 3DS for save sync (`CloudSync.kindsForPlatform`). 3DS games now get the same sync around them as PS2 / GameCube (the whole Citra folder: before a game Drive's newer saves come down — never while the emulator may run — and after it changes go up; upload-only with the new watcher while it runs).
2. Save Vault step 2d: each `title/<high>/<low>/data/` folder is one save (file count, size, newest date), matched to your game by the **title id in the ROM's header** (`MemoryCards.n3dsTitleLow`: NCSD .3ds / .cci at 0x108, NCCH .cxi at 0x118, or "[0004000000…]" in a .cia's name; read once, kept in memory). A save of a game that isn't in the library shows as "3DS save (<title id>)". Extra data (extdata) isn't a game save and isn't listed. Saves synced from another device count the same way.

### Check
- Header read checked on the Thor's ROMs: Pokémon Alpha Sapphire → 0011c500, Pokémon Moon → 00175e00 (matches the save folders).

## Update — 18 Oct 2026 (222): saves go to Drive seconds after the emulator writes them (#103), an upload never replaces a newer Drive save (#77), the game's save status says when a newer save hasn't gone up yet (#106)

You OK'd save / sync work on 18 Oct ("Keep em all coming"). All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`. **Copied, built and installed** on the AYN Thor and the RP Classic (Voltcap 0.6.9 + this) by Claude, committed and pushed by Claude.

**Copy `src_copy`**, changed (6): `src_copy\data\SaveObserver.kt` (**new**), `src_copy\data\CloudSync.kt`, `src_copy\data\DriveClient.kt`, `src_copy\data\SaveWatchWorker.kt`, `src_copy\LauncherViewModel.kt`, `src_copy\ui\GamePopupStatus.kt`. **Files to delete:** none.

### What changed
1. **Saves go up within seconds, while the game still runs (#103).** New `SaveObserver`: from the game's start until 15 min after Voltcap is back (emulators often write once more as they close) it listens to Android's file events on the game's save folders (a file closed after writing, renamed / moved into place, created) and also takes a cheap look every 15 s (60 s with the screen off; size and date only — no reading, no network), which also covers folders shared through Android's picker. A change counts once it has **settled** (same files, same size and date on two looks ≥ 4 s apart, newest write ≥ 4 s old): several writes of one save are one change; a memory card being written is never sent half-done. It then queues one **per-game upload job** (`SaveNowWorker`, WorkManager: survives Voltcap being closed or killed, waits for a connection, retries offline). Upload-only — nothing on this device is replaced while the game may run. A save made while one is uploading is sent right after by the same job. Save states stay excluded as before. The old 10-minute watcher stays as the safety net when the process dies, now first looking after 3 min.
2. **An upload never replaces a newer Drive save (#77).** Three gaps in the upload step closed (`CloudSync.push`):
   - the file is copied once into a snapshot and exactly those bytes are hashed and sent (before: hashed in one read and streamed again — an emulator writing in between sent other bytes than the hash recorded as synced);
   - right before replacing Drive's copy its md5 is read again (`DriveClient.file`); changed by another handheld since the folder was listed → nothing sent, **conflict, both kept** (before: the list could be minutes old and the newer save was replaced);
   - Drive's md5 of what arrived must match the snapshot, or it isn't marked synced.
3. **The game's save status tells the truth (#106).** Details › save line: when a save file is newer than what was last sent (size / date differ — no reading, no network) it says **"Newer save on this device · not sent yet"** (+ "· sending soon" while the watcher runs) instead of "up to date"; a game never checked by a job but with files synced before shows **"Saves up to date · <when> · from <device>"** instead of "Not checked yet"; files never sent: "Not on Google Drive yet".

### Check (device, disposable file — no real save touched)
- RP Classic: Dr. Mario (no battery save on the cartridge) started from Voltcap; a disposable 8 KB `Dr. Mario (World).srm` written into RetroArch/saves/Gambatte while it ran → upload job ran **7 s** after the write (3 s long); written again → job **8 s** after. The AYN Thor then had the file with the **same md5** (44ca00a4…) — so Drive got exactly those bytes. Details shows the green synced cloud.
- `gradlew assembleRelease`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL; installed with `adb install -r` on both; no crashes.
- **Not device-tested:** the "Drive changed meanwhile" conflict (needs two uploads within the same second), process death mid-game, SAF picker folders, offline → online.
- Test residue: the disposable `Dr. Mario (World).srm` (random bytes) is now in Drive and on both handhelds. Dr. Mario's cartridge has no save memory, so RetroArch ignores it; delete it from Drive's Voltcap › Saves › RetroArch folder and both handhelds if you want it gone (Voltcap never deletes everywhere).
- Seen: right after an update, the first Home press showed Android's own launcher once (the home app was being replaced); the next press was Voltcap.

## Update — 18 Oct 2026 (219): R1 panel tiles no longer jump under your finger, tapped category tabs open the right category (#04), Spotlight's tiles really move to the bottom (#08), failed launches no longer add play time (#01)

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`. **Copied, built and installed** on the AYN Thor and the RP Classic by Claude, committed and pushed by Claude.

### What changed
1. **R1 panel: tiles stay where they are when it opens.** The panel started with "no controller lights" and added the RGB tile a moment later (the light service even answers "none" for a while after Voltcap starts), so every tile after it moved one place — on the RP Classic a tap meant for Endless landed on Player, and one meant for Layout on Play Spotify. Lights once found are now remembered (this run, and as `lights_found` in the R1 tile settings of this device), so the tile list is right from the first frame. (`QuickSettings.kt`)
2. **Category tabs in the style looks open the category you tap (#04).** Library panel, Live tiles, Console stack, Pocket Classic / Quest and Green Core turned a tap on a tab into "press R2 N times". R2 skips empty categories and follows your own tile order (Choose a category › Reorder) while the tabs were drawn in the plain order — so a tap on e.g. "Continue playing" could open another category. Now the tabs use the same order as L2 / R2 (`styleStops` sorted by `CategoryTileOrder`) and a tap goes straight to that category (`LauncherViewModel.jumpCategory`); one step (L2 / R2, or the tab next door) works as before. In a category that isn't in the list, taps on the Pocket looks did nothing; they now count from the start of the list.
3. **A start category you hid isn't used any more (#04).** With "Continue playing" (or another special category) hidden but still set as the start category, Voltcap started inside it, outside the L2 / R2 list; it now starts in All instead.
4. **Spotlight: "Tiles sit at the bottom" works on the Home menu (#08)** — the default Spotlight look, where the R1 Spotlight tile and the option did nothing. The tiles now sit low, right above the button hints (▲ / ▼ unchanged: icons above, hints below). Spotlight options shows the choice for Home menu and Big picture, no longer for Row & menu (which keeps its tiles on top since update 125). Big picture with the tiles at the bottom and nothing above them (Title & Play hidden, no cards): ▲ now goes up to the category names instead of doing nothing.
5. **Play time: a launch that never reached the front adds nothing (#01).** With usage access, if Android's usage record shows the game's app never came to the front (a launch that failed or bounced straight back), the whole time until Voltcap was next opened used to count — up to 8 h, screen-off time included. It now counts nothing (no session). And when the game's app was no longer known (Voltcap restarted while the game ran), only the time some other app was really in front counts, not the wall clock. Existing totals are not touched. (`RunningGames.foregroundMs`)

### What changed
1. **Memory safety of downloads** (towards the Thor's OutOfMemoryError of 15 Oct during a download): guide pages (RetroAchievements guides, StrategyWiki, Fandom) and Drive files read with a size limit (Save Vault's memory cards / PSP saves from other devices, up to 16 MB) used to read the WHOLE reply first and check the size afterwards — and a Drive reply without a length was read in full. Now reading stops one byte past the limit (`bytesCapped` in DriveClient.kt): at most the limit is ever held in memory. ### What changed
1. **Crash: "Voltcap keeps stopping" right after a game** (RP Classic, 3× on 17 Oct, `ForegroundServiceDidNotStartInTimeException` in the in-game overlay). The overlay is started as a foreground service; when it was stopped again before it had shown its notification — a launch that didn't start, or Voltcap paused and resumed at once — Android killed the whole app. Now a stop that comes too early waits until the service has gone foreground and then ends it, every start goes foreground first, and a newer start still on its way is never torn down by an older one. Nothing changes in how the overlays look or when they show. (#81–86 overlay family, P1 crash.)

Nothing in it commits, pushes, publishes or deletes. Loaded after a restart of the Claude app. (#113, #114.)

### What changed (from your four recordings, checked frame by frame)
1. **The layer behind the discs** (game popup, every disc: GameCube, PS1, Xbox 360…): a tilted disc drew its "far side" as a full silver oval behind itself, a few pixels off — it showed round the disc's own rim as a second disc. Root cause: InspectDisc (update 189). Now only the disc's thin edge is drawn (rounded at its ends); the disc turns as one piece. Its spin, art and speed are unchanged.
2. **The Switch card disappearing in its case:** the card was in the tray only when the case was turned. Root cause: the open case draws its parts far-to-near by each part's middle, and a card low in the tray (the Switch's) counted as further away than the tray's middle with the case tilted towards you, so the tray was drawn over it (CaseOpen, since 189). The card (and a disc in an Xbox One / Series lid) is now always drawn right on top of what it lies in.
3. **Switch and Xbox 360 case insides** (research below): the inside of the lid showed the front cover again, as a manual. A Switch case is clear plastic with the paper insert behind it, and holds no manual; the Xbox 360's is the same in green. Without a manual, the lid's inside is now the insert's plain back under the plastic. Games with a downloaded manual still show it as a booklet. Other cases are unchanged.
4. **Covers stretched on cartridges:** a cover on a cartridge label (drawn shells like the N64, your cartridge pack, the template cartridges and the drawn shells) was stretched to the label's shape. It now keeps its own shape, as big as fits in the label; on the drawn shells the rest of the label is the colour along the cover's edge, on the pack / template cartridges the label paper. Real label scans still fill the label (they are the sticker).

### 1. Cartridges turning round like a clock's hands (home carousel)
- **Bug:** with Settings › Game look › Moving discs on (Spin, the default), the cartridge-shaped shells from your optical-system pack — the green "android apps" cartridge, and the Steam / PlayStation / Dreamcast… cartridges in the Cartridges look — turned round and round on the screen (the disc's turn, 360° every 6 s) instead of rocking.
- **Root cause (confirmed in the code and history):** update 203 (commit 5bae1a2, "cartridges stay solid when turned") changed the call for games on your pack from `mediaMotion(false, …)` to `mediaMotion(packDisc, …)`, so every game on an optical-system shell got the disc's motion (`rotationZ = 360° × t`).
- **Fix (restored from history):** those shells move as cartridges again — `mediaMotion(false, …)` as before 203 — so they follow Settings › Game look › Moving cartridges like every other cartridge: with Spin, the original rock from git, ±24° left and right over 5.2 s, reversing, never a full turn (the same numbers as before 203). They're also drawn as solid pieces at their own shape now (they were flat when the carousel turned them).
- **Not changed:** discs keep their spin, cases their motion, the carousel's own movement, memory / SD cards, your pack's normal cartridges.

### 2. Nintendo 64 cartridge (drawn shell)
- **Root cause:** there was never a correct drawn N64 shell in git. The library shell (since 195) was a flat-topped block with grip ridges along the top. The old template picture (`media_n64.png`) isn't the real shape either. Update 206 (35a0a5c) made the drawn shell the only N64 cartridge everywhere. So there was nothing to restore; it's redrawn from the straight-on photo you sent.
- **Now:** the top arched (about 6.5 mm higher in the middle), the raised middle panel between two grooves about 22.7 mm in from each side, the sides stepping in about 1.6 mm low down with the guide slots' ledge, and the label 57 × 63.5 mm with round corners, 7 mm below the top (it was 50.8 × 60.3). It's the same outline for every N64 colour (grey, black, gold, red, blue, clear, smoke). The back, thickness and sides follow the new outline. Measurements are approximate (off a photo).

### 3. Category reorder — every tile on its own
- **Bug:** Choose a category › Reorder moved a non-console tile's whole block (all the consoles, all the collections, or the group in Settings › Categories) past the next block. Android games, Other apps, Continue playing and the like couldn't be put between consoles.
- **Now:** every tile moves one place at a time, on its own, by its key ("ALL", the filter's name, "p:<console or collection>"). The order is saved in its own file (`category_tile_order`), so it survives restarts, rescans, scraping and layout changes. A new console or collection appears after the tile it follows by default. L2 / R2 go through the categories in the same order. Two consoles moved past each other still update your console order for the views that use it.
- **Controller:** Start turns Reorder on (as before). A picks up the tile, the D-pad moves it a place at a time, and A puts it down. **New: B with a tile picked up cancels** — the order goes back to how it was when you picked it up (it used to just put the tile down where it was). B again leaves Reorder. Touch is unchanged (hold, drag, release).
- **Side effect (please say if you don't want it):** moving a group in Settings › Categories, or its Reset, clears this tile order, because otherwise that page's changes wouldn't show.

### Checked
- Type-check of all sources: **0 errors**, no NON_LOCAL_RETURN. Your PC's copies of the 6 changed files were the same as my starting point.

### Where the controls are
- **Performance** sits next to Play in the game popup (A on a game). Where the buttons share a narrow row (the Grid's and the split windows), and on the TV room's set, it's a round ⚡ button at the end of the row. One press from the popup. On the store-page style (Settings › Game window › Style › Banner) it's a **PERFORMANCE** tab (L1 / R1) and a round ⚡ button in the strip.
- **The page:** *Performance · For this game*, then *Now: Balanced · PS2 default* (what it uses and where from), and the rows: **Power mode**, **AutoTDP** (Off / Efficient / Balanced / Smooth, with its wattage), **AutoTDP target** (when on), **Underclock** (With power shows what it is now), **Fan** ("Not adjustable on this handheld" where the fan can't be set), **Advanced…** (the game's settings with the whole tuner — CPU / GPU limits, governor, screen rate, buttons, what it cost), and **Use the PS2 default again** once the game has its own settings. A / a tap steps a row to its next choice. B goes back to the popup with the D-pad on Performance again.
- **Rules kept:** the tuner's own profiles (a whole profile per game; game › emulator / app › console › device). A change here always makes or changes *this game's* profile, starting from what it used — never the console's or the device's. Heat guard and the screen-off profile stay device-wide (said on the page). Not running: "Applied when this game launches." Running (the tuner is on this game): "Running now: changes apply at once · now …".
- **Shown on the popup's main page too:** a small ⚡ line with the summary, next to the save line.
- **Save sync, always in sight:** a small line under the buttons on every page (the picture, details, options, achievements, performance), and in the store page's status line. It describes this game only: *Saves up to date · 5 min ago*, *Uploading saves… / Downloading saves…*, *Changes waiting to sync*, *Waiting for the first sync*, *Save conflict · choose which to keep*, *Sync failed · Retry*, *Offline · will retry*, *Sign in to Google Drive again*, *Not checked yet*, *No save folder for this game*, *Save sync off for this game*, *Save sync is off*, *Save sync isn't set up*, *No save sync for apps*; "· syncing all games…" while a full sync runs (said as everything, not this game). "Up to date" only from this game's own record.
- An icon and short words; the ones that need you (conflict, failed, sign in) are bold, outlined and amber with a warning icon — not colour alone. A / a tap opens the game's sync (Save sync — *Sync this game*, Resolve conflict, Open Sync settings) **over the popup** — closing it comes back to the popup (it used to close it); when sync isn't set up, it opens Settings › Sync. Opening the popup or reading the line never starts a sync and never touches a conflict; nothing is fetched from the network for it.

### How Edit Home works now
- **Open it** as before (R1 › Edit home, the home Options menu, Settings). It's an edit session: nothing is kept until **Done**, and **Discard** puts back everything — what used to be saved at once included (parts taken off or added, their styles, the backing of every part, Art position).
- **Pick** a part: tap it, or L1 / R1. Only the picked one has handles (size in its bottom-left corner, ↔ ↕ stretch, red ✕ hide); the others have a faint outline. **Elements** (☰ on the toolbar, or L3) lists every part of this home screen — hidden, under another or off the screen too — with Show / Hide.
- **Adjust**: A (or ✎ Adjust, or a tap on the size handle) opens its panel — a side panel on a wide screen (on the side away from the part), a sheet on a small one (top or bottom, away from it; it folds). Groups: Position & size · Appearance · Visibility · More (backing of every part, Art position, Elements, + Add, Preview, Reset this layout). Each says what it reaches: *This layout only (…)*, *Every layout* (music player, round shortcuts) or *Shared: Voltcap row, Tile home, Grid* (header, game info, news, category bar).
- **Preview** hides every frame, handle and bar; any button or a tap goes back.
- **Done** = Start or ✓ Done. **B** goes back one step (closes the panel); at the top it leaves — with changes it asks **Save / Discard / Keep editing**. The touch Back gesture does the same.
- **Undo** = Y (or ↶ Undo): moves, sizes, stretches, styles, adding, hiding, showing, resets, Art position — one step each (held D-pad presses count as one).
- **Reset**: X resets the picked part (place, size, stretch, appearance). *Reset this layout* (panel › More) resets only this layout's parts — the other layouts, the music player and the round shortcuts keep theirs (it used to reset every layout).
- While editing, a touch beside the parts does nothing (it can't start a game or scroll the row); keys never reach the home screen.
- Home button / screen off / a call: the session stays open as it was. If Voltcap is closed in the middle, what it changed at once is put back next start.

**Controls, old → new:** A *saved and left* → opens the part's panel · B *saved and left* → back a step / Save–Discard–Keep editing · Start *+ Add* → Done · Select *✕ (saved at once)* → hide / show (undoable) · Y *reset every part on every layout* → Undo · X reset part (same) · L1 / R1 pick (same) · L2 / R2 size (same) · D-pad move (same) · L3 *Style* → Elements (shortcut; Style is in the panel) · R3 Art position (same; also in the panel). Nothing needs L3 / R3.

### Category reordering
- **Choose a category** (classic tiles): **hold a tile** — it's picked up (Reorder turns on) and the same touch drags it; near the top / bottom edge the list scrolls on. Each tile shows a drag handle while reordering. Start / the Reorder button, A pick up / put down, the D-pad and B work as before.
- **Y** (or the new **Options** button) opens the tile's options: **Reorder**, **Change picture…**, **Reset picture**. The hold no longer opens the picture picker, and X no longer resets the picture straight away.
- **Platform browser › Grid:** hold a console's card and drag it — always now (the "Drag-and-drop reorder" switch is gone; Settings says how); near the left / right edge it scrolls on. Start picks it up, ◀ ▶ move it, A puts it down. Holding a card that isn't a console opens its options. The card you're on shows a drag handle. Y opens the same options (Reorder there too).
- The rule is said on screen while reordering: consoles move among the consoles (your console order, also L2 / R2's); All, Favorites, Recent… and the consoles' and collections' blocks move as whole groups. The moved tile is followed by its key.

### Android games: disc or cartridge
- **Settings › Game look › Covers, cases & discs** (with Cases or Cartridges & discs as the main look) › **Android games**: Follow the current look (default, as before) / **Disc (Suggested)** / Cartridge.
- **One game:** its menu (Start) › **Disc or cartridge…** (the Cartridge shell row, renamed for Android games) › As the setting / Disc / Cartridge; it says what it is now and why.
- **Which wins:** a layout where every game is a disc (Disc station) → the game's own choice → a shell or cartridge pack you picked for it or for Android (stays a cartridge — never replaced without asking) → the Android games setting → the look (Discs only, "All CDs").
- One rule for every place: the cards, the closed and opened cases and what lies in them (a disc lies on the hub), the game window, the inspection view, the edge band and the launch animation (`mediaFor` decides; the game window used to ask with no look at all). The platform, category and launch settings never change. Presentation (case only / beside / half out) and the art stay their own settings.

### The category title
- **Settings › Categories › On the home screen › Category title**: Show, then dim (default: clear when you switch category, then 60 %, never gone) / Always clear / Off.
- A layout that shows the category itself (its tabs, header, caption — 20 layouts mark their label) keeps it. One that shows none right now gets one title, the Category name part, at that layout's free spot — e.g. Spotlight with its category tabs off or hidden in Edit Home, an empty category on the Voltcap row / Tile home / Grid, a custom layout without a category text. Never two.

- Hiding a layout's category tabs (navigation) no longer hides the title. Taken off in Edit Home it stays off on that layout (Elements or + Add › Taken off brings it back). On the row layouts, Settings › Categories › Category name: Off still means no name there.

### What was wrong (found on the Thor, 207 build)
- **Green back on the Ben 10 PSP cases:** ScreenScraper served a pure green #00FF00 picture (395 × 680, 2.4 KB) as "Back of the box" — its stand-in for a missing scan. 14 such files were saved on the Thor. Voltcap drew it as the back.
- **Backs from another edition:** each kind (box, back, spine) was picked World / US first on its own, whatever the game's region — the European Ben 10 got US scans (and the US green stand-in).
- **Backs late or missing:** a case without a back handed in made its back only once it had turned past 70°, so the back came in after the turn (or on a second turn); the warm-up decoded fronts and spines only.
- **DS cards:** drawn as a 28 × 28 window under a moulded ridge with a console band across it, so the cover with its printed NINTENDO DS strip read as a small box. The real card (measured off a straight Advance Wars: Dual Strike photo: 517 px = 33 mm) has a 27 × 29 mm sticker from 2.9 mm in and 1.6 mm down, plain plastic below, the lower left corner cut off. 3DS the same with its side tab.
- **Game Boy boxes (and other cardboard boxes):** the side opposite the spine was one flat colour taken from the front's edge — a plain block (Battletoads & Double Dragon's right side).
- **PS3 cases:** sized as 190 mm DVD cases (a Blu-ray case is 171.5 mm), as tall as PS2 ones.
- **Disc half out of every case:** `disc_case` was on (look memory `caseMedia=HALF`) from a preset / the Mix look.
- **Scrolling a long row of 3D cases (GBC, about 45 cases):** 94 % of frames janky, median 81 ms. Measured with simpleperf: half the screen thread was rebuilding the row — every case rebuilt on each D-pad step (each was handed the middle game's index), and again whenever any game's scans arrived (every case read the whole scans map, and the carousel's shared settings were rebuilt with each new map). Each rebuild copied pictures on the screen thread: the cover cut to the case's shape, two copies per case to average its edge colours, the turned spine, the loading front; and ran the name-cleaning regexes and the region lookup again (a regex was even compiled per name).
- **Category switch:** 89.5 % janky, median 101 ms — the same per-case work for the whole new row at once.
- **Save sync:** Voltcap was reinstalled on 13 Oct, which emptied its list of save folders (it lives in Voltcap's own data). Since then every sync only merged favourites and playtime and still said "Everything up to date", and the sync after playing had no folder to upload from. There was no way to see or pick the Google account (three on the Thor): Google chose one by itself.

### Now
- **No flat-colour stand-ins:** a picture that is one flat colour (checked on a 7 × 7 grid when decoded) counts as no picture: the next in line shows (the back cut from the full box scan, a printed back). Cases, the game window and the turned case use it.
- **One edition:** the game's own region first (its file name), and back / spine from the region its box front came from. (Already-saved scans stay until the game is looked up again — R1 › Rescan or the game's menu.)
- **Backs at once:** a scanned back is decoded with the case, and warmed ahead with the fronts and spines (not on small-memory devices, where it still waits for the turn).
- **DS / 3DS cards:** the measured sticker and cut corner; no band or ridge on any cartridge's label; a box scan used as the label has the box's printed console strip cut off (cut to the cover template's art window).
- **Cardboard boxes:** the other side carries the spine's print, with its fold lines.
- **Case sizes:** keep cases and card cases from CaseCatalog (North American size); PS3 / PS5 / Xbox One / Series 171.5 mm.
- **Case only by default:** Settings › Game look › Cases › With its media — **Case only** (default), **Case + media**, **Case + disc half out**. Media only is the Cartridges & discs look. Set once to Case only on this update.
- **Reorder categories:** on Choose a category, press **Start** or the **Reorder** button in the corner; **A** picks the tile up / puts it down, the **D-pad** moves it, **B** finishes; on the touch screen drag a tile. Consoles take your order (also used by L2 / R2 and the warm-up); All, Favorites, Recent… and the consoles' and collections' blocks move as groups.
- **Saving after scraping:** asking Save all while it runs (as a finished scrape does) makes it go round once more at the end, while there's room.
- **Faster rows and switches:** each game in a row rebuilds only when it becomes / stops being the one in the middle or its own scans change (HomeScans.of); pictures a case makes from its cover are kept (DerivedArt, up to 1/12 of the memory, held only while the cover itself is); edge colours sampled without copies; names and regions worked out once.
- **Diagnostics (debug builds):** `adb logcat -s VoltcapPerf` — every 5 s: frames, slow frames (> 33 ms), average and slowest, pictures ready / decoded, case faces kept / made; after L2 / R2: how long until the frames settled.
- **Save sync:**
  - With saves on and no save folder at all, the emulators' save folders found on the device are added (RetroArch saves, PPSSPP saves, ARMSX2 memory cards, Citra saves on the Thor), under the same names as before so they meet their Drive folders. Once only; files that differ from Drive are asked about, never overwritten.
  - With no save folders the status says "No saves synced: no save folders are set up (Settings › Sync › Save folders)" instead of "Everything up to date".
  - Settings › Sync › Google Drive shows **Account: …** (as Drive reports it) and has **Switch account** (Android's account list). Switching drops what this device knew of the old Drive (folder records, the favourites' merge base, the change feed) so the new one is read fresh, merged as a first sync.

### Check
- Type-check: 0 errors. No `NON_LOCAL_RETURN` in the compiled classes. Every change reread against your PC's copy.
- Measured on the Thor before the fixes (207 build): category switch R2 × 6 and scrolling GBC × 20 (numbers above), simpleperf call graphs; Ben 10 backs, DS card photo, Battletoads box, PS3 size, prefs, the sync settings and log (`folders: []`, "Everything up to date" since the reinstall), the emulator save folders present.

- **Save all did nothing (Settings › Metadata › Saved on this device).** The art store was at 929 MB of its 1 GB, and saving stops at 90 %. Picking a bigger size didn't start it again, and while automatic saving was already running, Save all now returned without a word.
- **Two different N64 (Game Boy, SNES…) cartridges.** The real drawn shell was only the default for anyone who had once picked Real shell; everyone else got the template pack's flat picture in some views and the drawn shell in others.
- **Labels were cropped** to the label window, cutting the edges off label scans.
- **The UMD was drawn square** (Sony: approx. 65 × 64 mm).

### Now
- **Saving art:** a bigger size (or unlimited) starts saving again straight away; Save all now while saving says "Already saving art: n / total"; Settings › Metadata › Scraping › Real media › Save them all on the device restarts a running save with every game's real media in its list. (On the Thor it is saving now: 2,395 / 7,790 when checked, Java heap steady at 48–57 MB.)
- **One cartridge per console:** every cartridge console's games are on its authentic drawn shell by default (by region). Custom pack shapes only when Cartridges only or the custom cartridge source is picked.
- **Labels stretched to the label window** (never cut) on the drawn shells, the template cartridges and the custom pack cartridges. Drawn fronts' cache key `f2`.
- **UMD** drawn 65 : 64. **Switch 2 case** marked sourced (Wikipedia lists 170 × 104 × 10).
- **Audit:** `docs\physical_media\PHYSICAL_MEDIA_AUDIT.md` and `physical_media_verification.json` — 158 entries (every drawn cartridge / card, every case by region, UMD, discs), each with its source and status: 4 verified (Sony UMD, ECMA CD / DVD, Nintendo GameCube 8 cm), 73 approximate (ConsoleMods / Wikipedia agree), 16 disputed (sources disagree — sizes left as they were), 65 unconfirmed (no measurement found). Lists the deprecated duplicates, scraper and fallback rules, labels, regional variants and what still needs measuring.

### Check
- Type-check: 0 errors. No `NON_LOCAL_RETURN` in the compiled classes.
- Every change reread against your PC's copy (diffed).
- The Thor's crash at 09:25 was an OutOfMemoryError (Java heap full at 512 MB; it ran out inside OkHttp's download reader, which is only where it tipped over). **Cause not found:** with the 205 build saving all 7,790 pictures the heap stays at about 50 MB. A watcher on the Thor writes a heap dump if it climbs past 260 MB again (`/data/local/tmp/vc.hprof`).

### What was wrong (root causes, found on the Thor and in Git history)
- **The game window showed another piece than the home screen (update 202).** 202 made "Use its own photo when one is found" decide for the cards, but the game window kept the old rule (drawn shell whenever the 3D finish is on). So a game showed ScreenScraper's cartridge photo on the home screen and Voltcap's drawn shell with the cover under a console band when opened — seen with Pokémon Silver and Army Men (N64).
- **Every Game Boy Color game was a clear see-through cartridge.** The real-shell table gave GBC only the clear Color-only Game Pak; the games marked "(GB Compatible)" came on the black dual-mode one.
- **Drawn pieces wore the cover, not the label.** With the own photo on, a game without a photo got its cover under a console band, even when ScreenScraper had its real printed label.
- **Lists mixing consoles (All games, Favorites, Continue playing…) drew different media.** Case templates, real case shapes and the real cartridge shells were switched off in mixed lists on purpose (from before), so the same game looked custom there.
- **Real spines, backs and labels came late or never.** Every game's scans are saved (2,623 games here), but they were only read when a game's card asked — after it had been on screen 0.4 s. Until then Voltcap's own spine / plain back showed, then the real one popped in; often only on going back to a category.
- **Cases never had a back outside the game window.** The carousels, Case stacks and the other 3D cases had no back handed to them — spinning cases showed plain plastic. Also ScreenScraper's own back scan was never used at all: the back was always cut out of the full box scan.
- **PlayStation backs lost a quarter of their right side (update 204).** 204 capped the cut at the cover template's front shape, which isn't the scan's. Removed; the back and front being the same width is enough (checked on Pokémon Silver's scan: its back now ends 18 px before the spine; the PlayStation back ends 12 px before its spine).
- **Glitches round turned cartridges.** A cartridge's sides were drawn as copies of its whole face, so seen from the side its label showed in stripes; and the cases / cartridges in the packed stacks were 88 % opaque, so each showed the ones behind it.
- **Android / Steam / PC games stood in clear plastic** with Real shell picked — the clear switch from an earlier pick stayed on.
- **Landscape box scans (N64, SNES) were never cut** (their scan is wider than the cut allowed), so no spine or back came from them.

### Now
- **One rule everywhere:** the cards, carousels, Case stacks, grid, tiles, hero, style homes, the launch animation and the game window all pick the same piece: a shell picked for the game or console (Cartridge shell…) wins; else its own photo when "Use its own photo" is on and it has one; else the drawn piece — the real shell for its console and region — **wearing its real label scan** (no console band over it), the cover only when there's no label.
- **Mixed lists:** each game is drawn as in its own console's list (case template, real case shape, real shell). The explicit "Mixed categories" choices (All covers / All CDs / All cartridges…) still apply when you pick them.
- **Game Boy Color:** "(GB Compatible)" games on the black dual-mode shell (with its researched back); Color-only games stay clear.
- **Scans at start:** every saved game's scans are read once at start (no network), so the real spine, back, label and photo are there from the first frame; while a real spine is still loading a neutral strip shows, never Voltcap's spine first. The category you switch to has its pieces' pictures warmed with its covers.
- **Backs:** every 3D case gets its back the first time it turns far enough to show it: its back scan, else the cut from its full box scan, else a printed back. Jewel cases (PlayStation, Saturn, Dreamcast…) have the end flaps of a back insert cut off instead of squeezed on.
- **Solid sides:** a turned cartridge's sides are its outline in its plastic's colour (a photo's colour read off the photo), slices close enough that no gaps show; the pieces shown in the carousels are fully opaque (shade does the depth).
- **Clear plastic** only with Cartridge › Clear plastic.
- **Saving art:** as before, the scans of the games you've shown or that were looked up this run are saved on the device; Save them all (below) saves every game's.

### Real media report (Settings › Metadata › Scraping › Real media)
- While Scrape spines now, Only the missing real covers or Get everything run: "Looking up <console> — 35 / 80 games · <game>", a progress bar, then each kind counted on its own: Box fronts, Backs, Spines, Cartridge / disc photos, Labels, Full box scans, 3D boxes — found / none on ScreenScraper; games ScreenScraper doesn't know (or no sure match); failed look-ups with the reason (no connection, or what ScreenScraper answered, e.g. 429 too many requests, 430 quota). "Finished" when done.
- **Count:** what every game in the library has, kind by kind, and how many of those pictures are saved on the device (no look-ups).
- **Save them all on the device:** every game's real media the looks use (full box scans and 3D boxes only where a cut needs them).
- Settings search: Real media, Scrape progress, Save real media on the device.

### What ScreenScraper supplies (checked in your saved scans)
- Of 2,623 games with saved scans, 2,248 have ScreenScraper's set: Box, Back of the box, Box (3D), Spine (box-2D-side), Box (full scan) — all 2,248; Disc / cartridge photo and Disc label — 2,204. The rest are RetroAchievements' box art and title screen only. So backs and spines were there; they weren't being shown.
- ScreenScraper's cartridge photos are sometimes its own renders (007 The World Is Not Enough's N64 one is a blue render) — that's the photo, not Voltcap's media; turn "Use its own photo when one is found" off to draw every game on its real shell with its label instead.
