### Automatic update check (Settings › Updates & downloads › Check for updates automatically)
- **Why it did nothing:** after the check at start it waited **12 hours**, and coming back to Voltcap didn't check at all. 0.6.1 came out 10 minutes after 0.6.0, so it was never seen (you have 0.6.1 now, the newest on GitHub, so there's nothing to ask about at the moment).
- **Now:** a little after start, every time you come back to Voltcap (from a game or an app, at most every 10 minutes) and every hour while it's on screen. A failed try waits 15 minutes.
- **No GitHub limit trouble:** each check after the first asks "anything new since this?" (ETag); GitHub's "nothing new" answer doesn't count against its 60-an-hour limit.
- **Later:** that version isn't asked about again for 12 hours (or until Voltcap starts again). The automatic check no longer flashes "Checking GitHub…" in Settings.

### Pocket Quest: quick settings
- **Why:** "L1 / R1 switch the console" was on by default, so R1 never opened the quick settings there (only Start did).
- **Now:** off by default (a new setting key, so everyone gets it once): **R1 = quick settings, L1 = shortcuts, L2 / R2 switch the console**. Settings › Home › Layout options › "L1 / R1 switch the console" brings the old way back.
- **Top bar:** a new **Quick settings** button (slider icon) between Sort & filter and Settings — tap it, or reach it with the D-pad.

### Cartridges & discs
- **WWE All Stars (and other Android games) flat:** a "disc / cartridge" picture of another console's release was used as the game's own photo. Android, Steam, PC and arcade games now always go on Voltcap's own cartridge / CD.
- **Games without a cartridge or disc of their own** (arcade, PC, DOS…) get Voltcap's plain cartridge (or the plain CD with their console's name) instead of a flat cover — also in lists mixing consoles with "All CDs" / "All cartridges".
- **Show as (new):** Settings › Game look › Covers, cases & discs › Cartridges & discs › **Show as: Mix / Cartridges / Discs**.
  - **Mix:** every game its own medium (cartridge games their cartridge, disc games their disc); its "Disc games: Their disc / Their case" choice stays.
  - **Cartridges:** every game a cartridge (disc, Android, Steam, PC games on a custom cartridge).
  - **Discs:** every game a disc (cartridge, Android, Steam, PC games on a custom CD).
  - (They're the old Disc games choices underneath, so your current look stays as it was.)
- **R1 › Look:** steps Covers → Cases → **Mix → Cartridges → Discs** → Art; the tile shows which.
- **Only what applies:** looks that don't apply to the layout on screen are left out instead of greyed — in Settings › Game look (a note says why) and on the R1 panel (Look tiles while Pocket Quest shows plain covers, the achievement place there, Background / Background fit while the layout draws its own background).

### Cartridge backs on photos
- **Why the new backs didn't show:** the researched backs were only on drawn shells. Most games show their own cartridge photo ("Use its own photo when one is found"), and a photo turned round showed a plain grey silhouette.
- **Now:** a cartridge photo turned round (carousels, flips, the game window's inspect view, a cartridge beside its case) shows its console's real shell back (by region), at the shell's real thickness and colour. Settings › Game look › Covers, cases & discs › More look options › Cartridge backs › Neutral leaves the maker's text off.

### Case backs (Game Boy, Game Boy Color)
- **Spine strip on the back:** the back is cut out of the game's full box scan (back | spine | front). Game Boy / Color spines have a full-height printed stripe that was taken for the fold, so the spine was found too narrow and its outer part stayed on the back.
- **Now:** the back and front are cut no wider than each other (they're the same width on a real box), never wider than the console's real box front at the scan's height, and a bit further from the fold. (Voltcap's own printed back, `tpl_back_gb` / `tpl_back_gbc`, has no spine in it — checked.)

### Volume mixer: + steps going back
- **Why:** each + tap (pull-down mixer) set the volume from its own thread; an older, slower one finishing last put the volume back a step, and a look at the volumes finishing in between redrew the older value.
- **Now:** every step gets a number when it's tapped; one is set at a time, and a step that's been overtaken by a newer one is skipped. The pull-down keeps showing a tapped step until it's set. The mixer card (◀ ▶ / slider) uses the same.

### Manuals (Settings › Metadata › Scraping)
- **Find manuals:** asks ScreenScraper about every game's manual now (whether the Manuals tick is on or not), with a progress line and Stop.
- **Download all manuals:** does that, then saves every manual found onto the device (offline reading).
- Shows how many manuals are found so far. Also in the settings search (Manuals, Scrape manuals, Find manuals, Download all manuals).

### Category name on every layout
- **Default on:** the layouts that didn't show the category name (TV room, Case stacks, Card binder, Console hub, Resume & discover, Hero tiles, Twin icons, Hero carousel) get the **Category name** part once, at a free spot of each layout. (The others already show it: the Voltcap row / Tile home / Grid category bar, Timeline, Pocket Quest's tabs, Library panel, Spotlight, Cross / Side menu…)
- **Look:** just the name, in the names' style (Settings › Home › Name & logo); with Settings › Categories › On the home screen › Category name › All categories it's the full row of categories.
- **Turn it off:** its ✕ in Edit Home, or Settings › Home › Layout options › Game info on screen › Category name. Move / size it in Edit Home.

### Voltcap row: "Only the first one wide"
- **Why it wouldn't take:** it only works in the plain row with the game you're on at the left; in the carousel nothing changed, and every game unfolded into a wide capsule as you reached it.
- **Now:** picking it (Settings › Game look › Covers › The game you're on) turns the row's carousel off and puts the game you're on at the left. Where the fixed capsule can't be drawn, games stay covers (no more unfolding one by one).

### Overlays over games coming back
- **Why they vanished on going back into a game:** they're brought back when you return to a running game, but only for a game *confirmed* open — and that's filled by a check that runs a moment after Voltcap comes back (and needs usage access or the root service). Going back in before it ran forgot the game for good, so the overlays never returned that session.
- **Now:** any game still in the open list brings its overlays back, keeping the overlay's session clock running.
- **Editing them from the Android drop-down:** not reproduced yet (see the reply) — tell me which control (the notification's buttons, its panel, or the Quick Settings tile) and I'll go after it.

### Check
- **Type-check:** full kotlinc 2.2.10 + Compose type-check of all of `src_copy` against your Gradle cache's jars and android-36: **0 errors**; no `NON_LOCAL_RETURN` in the compiled classes.
- **Reread:** every change line by line against your PC's copies (taken at the start of this update); every caller of `mediaFor` checked for the "never null now" change (game window, case + media, Disc station, launch animation, carousels, grid, tiles, hero, style homes).
- **Reproduced on the Thor (adb):** R1 on the home screen, the WWE All Stars flat cover, the update check (GitHub's newest = v0.6.1 = installed). The overlay service's lifecycle read through (start, reconfigure, restore, stop) — the shade case couldn't be reproduced without a game running.
- **Not tested on a device:** all of it (needs your build). Especially: Pocket Quest's top bar with the extra button on the Retroid Pocket Classic's small screen; the category name's starting spot on each of the 8 layouts (move it in Edit Home if one sits badly); the Game Boy / Color case backs; the pull-down mixer's + / − tapped quickly; cartridge backs on photos in the inspect view.

### Game looks: 4 looks with plain choices
- **The looks:** Covers, Cases, Cartridges & discs and Art replace the ~20 looks and hidden switches. R1 › Look steps through the 4; hold it (or Settings › Game look) for the choices, each with a small preview of the game you're on.
- **Covers:** style (Cover · Wide · Square tile · Spine) and the game you're on (same / wide / only the first one wide).
- **Cases:** your game's real scan (drawn if none) or always drawn; all the same size or real sizes; its disc or cartridge inside only, beside it, or half out.
- **Cartridges & discs:**
  - **Cartridge:** real shell for each console (the drawn ones with their real backs — the default now), your pack's shapes, or clear plastic.
  - **Disc games:** their disc / their case / a cartridge too / every game as a disc.
  - **Your game's own photo:** used when one is found, or switched off.
- **Art:** hero art, screenshots or wide capsules.
- **Migration:** your current look is carried over once. Leftover switches that still do something are under "More look options".

### Two new layouts
- **Green Core (2001):** a dark green machine dashboard. A living sphere of light on the left (rotating grid, pulsing core, rings) and angled menu panels on the right:
  - **Menu:** Games, Systems, Apps, Save Vault, Music, Settings.
  - **Games:** a list or curved carousel.
  - **Systems:** consoles with counts.
  - **Sounds:** made in code.
  - **Its own options:** glow, sphere speed, motion, sounds and hum, reduced motion, browse style, accent colour.
- **Pocket Quest:** a full-screen 32-bit handheld-RPG style menu:
  - **Top bar:** console tabs.
  - **Showcase:** a big showcase of the game with a gold-edged info panel and screenshots.
  - **Collection:** your games along the bottom in your game look.
  - **Screens:** Select a System and a details screen.
  - **Themes:** four themes with pixel-art scenery drawn in code (Island Sky, Sunset Ruins, Deep Lab, Ocean Depths).
  - **Sounds:** optional retro blips.
  - **Its own options:** theme, background, motion, parallax, accent, media, description, screenshots, size, speed, sounds, reduced motion.

### Manuals
- **Recording:** a game's manual (from ScreenScraper) is noted when the game is looked up and downloaded only when you open it.
- **In the case:** when a case opens, the manual lies in the lid as a booklet; tap it to read.
- **Reader:**
  - **Turn pages:** swipe, ◀ ▶ or L1 / R1.
  - **Zoom:** A or a pinch.
  - **Close:** B.
- **Other ways in:** a Manual button in the game window, its options, and the second screen's Details page.

### Updates
- **Update prompt:** when a newer version is on GitHub, Voltcap asks: Update now (downloads, then installs) / Later / Skip this version.
- **When it checks:** at start and every 12 hours (Settings › Updates & downloads › Check for updates automatically).

### Covers, cases and cartridges
- **Covers fill their place:** edge-to-edge with the smallest centred crop. No grey bars, no stretching, no blurred backdrop.
- **Trim:** flat bars baked into a cover image are trimmed (only matching bars on opposite sides, never branding).
- **Android games:** they use Voltcap's Android case and a green Android cartridge inside (not their store art).
- **Console badge:** no longer drawn over a case that already has its console band (no more doubled "Nintendo GameCube").
- **Real spine:** the game window's case uses the game's real spine.
- **Real backs:** cartridges show their researched real backs by default (Cartridges & discs › Real shell).

### Home screen
- **R1 tiles:** each tile shows only where it does something (the header tile only on the Voltcap row with its header on, and so on). Hidden tiles keep their place.
- **Edit Home:** every piece can be moved and sized, including:
  - the news bar;
  - the game row and the game you're on (cover / box / cartridge / disc);
  - the clock, the button legend, the now-playing card and the lyrics line;
  - the art position for every look.

### Fixes
- **Background music:** it no longer plays on with the screen off (it also pauses for the black screensaver, the lid closing and a game on the other screen). New setting: "Keep playing with the screen off" (off).
- **Achievements overlay:**
  - Only the pinned (or next) badge and the progress bar by default. Every part is a toggle in Settings › Overlay and in the in-game panel.
  - Resizing no longer cuts off the bottom.
- **Play time counted twice across devices (e.g. 50 h instead of 25):** each device now keeps its own counter, and syncing merges by the larger value, never by adding. A one-time repair rebuilds totals from the session log.
- **Navigation bar:** it stays hidden inside games (AYN's own hide setting is held while a game from Voltcap runs and put back after). The lower screen of a two-screen handheld picks it up after its next start.

## Update — 14 Oct 2026 (201): power controls that really work, cartridge backs fixed, Lyrics stage without stats

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`.

**Copy `src_copy`** (into `app\src\main\java\com\shelf\launcher\`), changed (14): `src_copy\device\ChargeLimiter.kt`, `src_copy\device\DeviceControls.kt`, `src_copy\device\RootShell.kt`, `src_copy\device\VendorAdapter.kt`, `src_copy\device\tune\GameNotification.kt`, `src_copy\device\tune\TuneHardware.kt`, `src_copy\device\tune\TuneService.kt`, `src_copy\device\tune\Tuner.kt`, `src_copy\ui\CartShells.kt`, `src_copy\ui\LauncherScreen.kt`, `src_copy\ui\LyricsStage.kt`, `src_copy\ui\MediaInspectView.kt`, `src_copy\ui\SecondScreenHome.kt`, `src_copy\ui\TunerContent.kt`.

**Files to delete:** none.

### Power controls (checked live on the Odin 2 Portal and the Thor)
- **The cause:** AYN's root service (the one Voltcap uses for clocks, fan and lights) cuts every command at 255 characters and answers with only the first line. Voltcap's clock writes were one long chain, so only the little CPU cores were ever capped. The big and prime cores, the GPU, the boost switches and the temperature reading were silently dropped. Underclock, the power tiers and AutoTDP therefore did almost nothing, and the tuner page showed one CPU cluster.
- **The fix:** writes are now split into commands that fit, and replies that have several lines are joined into one. All three CPU clusters and the GPU are found and capped, plus the msm_performance limits. AutoTDP now moves every cluster and the GPU.
- **AYN's resets:** the handheld resets its own clocks every 10 seconds; while it keeps doing that, Voltcap checks once a second and writes its limits again. The tuner page and the in-game notification say whether the limits hold.
- **Fan curve and heat guard:** they had no temperature (they read a modem sensor); they now read the chip temperature.
- **Charge limit and lights:**
  - The charge limit now finds every charging switch.
  - The stick lights' "off" is sent in pieces, so both rings really go off.

### Cartridges in the game window
- **Grey plate on the back:** a grey see-through plate the size of the whole piece showed over every cartridge's back (the N64 most visibly). It came from the back's shading spreading over the window; the back is now drawn on a layer of its own.
- **Clear shells:** the mirrored label no longer shows through their backs.
- **Game Boy notch:** drawn as a step cut into the edge.
- **Stick clicks:** the first click after the window opens (or after touching it) now always works.
- **Hint text:** no longer cut off under narrow pieces.

### Lyrics stage
- **Stats panel:** removed.
- **Settings gear:** a gear at the top right opens its settings directly (Settings › Screens › Second screen art & music › Music page layout › Lyrics stage).

### Cases open a step at a time
- **Steps:** a tap (or either stick's click) opens the case: the lid swings, the disc or cartridge still lies in it, and the open case can be turned and looked at. A tap on the disc takes it out beside the case; a tap on it puts it back in the open case; a tap on the case shuts it.
- **Hints:** "Tap the case (or click a stick) to open it", then "Tap the disc to take it out".
- **Finger taps fixed:** the disc, hidden inside the case, sat over the case's right half and took the taps, so a finger on the case didn't open it.
- **Stick click fixed:** the first stick click now always reaches the piece (it took two).
- **"Open cases side by side"** still opens it all the way by itself.
- **Cartridges, loose discs and pieces:** a tap or stick click turns them once round.

### Second screen
- **Highlight:** one ring glides from control to control (it used to jump), follows lists as they scroll, and glides into a newly scrolled row.
- **Pages:** they slide in the direction you go.
- **Folders:** they open with a short scale and fade.

### Lyrics stage — the second screen's new music page (default)
Rebuilt from your lyrics wallpaper:
- **Background:** the cover blurred behind, pulsing with the music.
- **Clock and date** at the top.
- **The cover** with a circle visualizer round it, then the title, progress, and previous / play / next.
- **Synced lyrics** beside it.
- **Effects:** particles, spectrum bars, beat rings, aurora, starfield, bokeh and wave lines.
- **Panels:** a stats panel (CPU, GPU, RAM, drives, network — what Android lets an app read) and a volume control.
- **Status line:** it says when something is missing (e.g. the Microphone permission for the music reaction).

Every toggle from the wallpaper's settings is there: Settings › Screens › Second screen art & music › Music page layout › Lyrics stage (effects, reactions, background, idle and its picture, clock and size, stats panel, lyrics and volume, status line). Full screen, Visualizer and Classic card are still there to pick.

### 3D cartridges: the drawn pieces, with real backs
- **Old 3D models retired:** the pre-rendered models (pictures every 20°, which turned like a slide show) are gone. The 3D cartridges looks now draw the cartridges Voltcap draws itself, turning smoothly at their real thickness:
  - **3D cartridges:** each console's authentic shell.
  - **3D custom cartridges:** your pack's shapes.
  - **3D clear cartridges:** clear plastic.
- **Removed:**
  - the R1 "3D on / off" tile;
  - the old "3D models" settings;
  - the Cartridge shell… menu's "Your 3D pieces" tab. A game set to one of those pieces gets its own console's shell.
- **Backs:** every shell's back is drawn from research of real rear photos: its screws by type (cross, tri-wing, security, slot), moulded text, panels, stickers, seams and connector. The fronts weren't touched.
- **Back setting:** Settings › Game look › Covers, cases & discs › Cartridge backs — the maker's markings on a game's own console's shell (default), always, or plain (same shape, screws and contacts, no branding).
- **Research status:** some backs are still unverified (the research couldn't reach the photos); `CARTRIDGES.md` lists each.
- **GBC back fixed:** the odd logo on the GBC back came from the old models and is gone.

### Folder icons
- **Setting one:** long-press a folder on the second screen's Games page › Change icon… / Reset icon. Settings › Screens › Second screen Games page › Folder icons has a short how-to and every console with Change / Reset.
- **Animated icons:** GIFs and animated WebPs play.
- **Top screen follows the Games page:** the folder you're on shows big on the top screen (its icon or GIF, name and game count); opening it shows its games up there. Switch: "Top screen follows the Games page" (on).

### Fixes
- **Crash on the Odin 2 Portal:** fixed. The cartridge shell choices were made the first time a game was drawn, in the middle of a screen's measuring — "Reading a state that was created after the snapshot was taken".
- **Android games' play time:** a game's splash screen closing a second after the game opened ended the timing, so sessions came out at about a second and were dropped. That is also why nothing synced. Now:
  - the game counts while any of its screens is open;
  - every Android game is tracked from wherever it's started;
  - Continue playing shows Android games and no ordinary apps.
- **Launch animation:** it drew every cover at 2:3, cut to fit. It now uses the card's own shape and art; case and cartridge throws use the case's real shape.
- **Thor RGB timer:** it now switches both light chips off, plus the Thor's combined "1,1" light setting, and puts them back.
- **Underclocking didn't work:** AYN's performance mode keeps its own minimum speeds, and Voltcap kept them as the floor. While a limit is on, the floor is the chip's lowest speed. The tuner page says when a cap didn't hold, and the notification shows the profile that's really running.
- **Animated covers:** they no longer go black for a moment while moving through the games (their first frame stands in while they're decoded again).
- **Covers on cases (other consoles too):** a cover a little off its case's shape, up to about an eighth, is fitted whole instead of cut.

- **Switches:** these work at once, with a short note on the second screen:
  - Play / pause music, Explore, Rediscover;
  - Lights on / off, Overlay (steps Off → Stats → Music → Trophies → All), Endless row, Hide nav bar;
  - Who is playing, Drawn / real discs;
  - Next theme (your starred themes), Battery saver (steps When low → Always → Off);
  - Rescan library, Missing art, Do not disturb.
- **Android panels:** Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Android settings open on the second screen.
- Nothing opens a window on the main screen.
- Hold a shortcut in the dock to move it or take it out, as with apps.

### The cases' opening side
- **Two pieces:** every hinged case's right side now shows the front lid's own edge, a fine seam, and the rear shell's
  lip just behind it.
- **Catches and tabs:**
  - keep and card cases: two small catches;
  - jewel cases: the lid's two tabs;
  - a cartridge clamshell: its one catch in the middle.
- **Where the seam sits:**
  - keep cases: the front cover is about 2 mm, so a slim Switch case shows more of it than a PS2 case;
  - DS, 3DS and Vita: the halves are about even;
  - Mega Drive and Neo Geo clamshells: even;
  - jewel cases: the clear 2.4 mm lid in front of the tray, so a deep PAL PlayStation case shows far more tray than a
    thin one.
- **The thumb grip** is in the rear shell, behind the seam.
- **The top** shows the same join. A cardboard box's top shows its fold at the back and the tuck flap's slit at the
  front; its sides stay closed.
- **Opening:**
  - the halves part at the seam: the lid has its own thickness and its rim shows as it swings;
  - the tray's walls stop where the lid sat.
- **Not done:** rounded corners (the cases are still straight-edged boxes), and the PAL Dreamcast's own multi-part
  case (no measurements found).

### To check on the Thor
- A PS2, PS4, Switch, DS and PS1 (PAL and US) case turned to their right side, closed and opening.
- A dock shortcut of each kind: a page, a switch, Wi-Fi.

## Update — 14 Oct 2026 (192): crash fix — turning a cartridge crashed Voltcap (Thor and Retroid Pocket Classic)

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`.

**Copy `src_copy`** (into `app\src\main\java\com\shelf\launcher\`), changed (1): `src_copy\ui\MediaInspectView.kt`.

**Files to delete:** none.

### The crash
- Since 190, opening a game whose piece is a cartridge (your custom cartridges too) crashed Voltcap on both handhelds
  after a moment.
- Cause: the cartridge's shell colour is read from its own picture, and that picture lives on the graphics chip,
  where Android doesn't allow reading its pixels.
- Now a readable copy is read. If even that fails, the cartridge keeps its plain colour; nothing can crash there any
  more.

## Update — 14 Oct 2026 (191): real game cases per console and region, cardboard boxes that open, Xbox discs on the left, the disc no longer turns into a cartridge

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`.

**Copy `src_copy`** (into `app\src\main\java\com\shelf\launcher\`), new (1): `src_copy\ui\CaseCatalog.kt`. Changed (6):
`src_copy\data\Features.kt`, `src_copy\ui\Case3D.kt`, `src_copy\ui\CaseOpen.kt`, `src_copy\ui\GameWindow.kt`,
`src_copy\ui\MediaInspectView.kt`, `src_copy\ui\SettingsDialog.kt`.

**Project root**, new (1): `CASES.md` (what was found per console and region, and how sure each one is).

**Files to delete:** none.

### Bug: the disc turned into a cartridge
- When a case held a cartridge (Voltcap's own case for an Android game with your cartridge on it), the open case
  showed a disc in it, and a cartridge flew out. Now what lies in the case is what comes out: a cartridge sits in a
  recess, a disc on its hub.

### Real cases, researched console by console (ui/CaseCatalog.kt, CASES.md)
- Each console's packaging was looked up per region:
  - sizes;
  - plastic colour and how see-through it is;
  - where the disc or card sits;
  - memory card and Game Boy Advance slots;
  - cardboard boxes.
- The 3D cases are now drawn from that table, not from one DVD-style case with different art.
- **Region:** from the game's file name — (USA), (Europe), (Japan) and the usual short tags. For names without one:
  Settings › Game look › Covers, cases & discs › Case region. The default is "From the file name, else North
  America"; it can also be Europe or Japan, or one region for all.
- **Sizes and thickness are the real ones.** A PAL PlayStation case is deeper (17.4 mm). A European DS case is clear
  and 20 mm. A Japanese GameCube case is small (149×107) and clear. A Super Famicom box has its own shape. PS3, PS4,
  PS5 and Xbox One cases are Blu-ray height.
- **Plastic:**
  - PS2: black in North America, dark blue in Europe.
  - PS3: clear. PS4 and PS5: see-through blue.
  - Original Xbox: green, near opaque (not black). Xbox 360: see-through lime green. Xbox One / Series: see-through
    green.
  - Wii: white. Wii U: blue. 3DS: white.
  - Switch: clear (the red is the paper). Switch 2: red.
  - Vita: blue. PSP: clear.
  - Mega Drive, Master System and Neo Geo: black clamshells.
  - Sega CD and Saturn (North America): clear longboxes.
  - The edges of see-through cases are deeper in colour, as when you look through the plastic's depth.
- **Jewel cases** (PS1, Dreamcast, Saturn and Mega-CD in Japan, Neo Geo CD, PC Engine CD, 3DO outside North
  America):
  - the booklet sits under the clear lid at its real 120 mm size, the whole cover, nothing cut;
  - the tray's hinge ridge shows beside it: black on PlayStation, clear on a US Dreamcast, white on a Japanese one.
- **Cardboard boxes** (NES, SNES, N64, Game Boy, GBA, Atari, Jaguar, Lynx, ColecoVision, Vectrex, Game Gear,
  WonderSwan, computer big boxes):
  - matte, their top and side in the colours of their print;
  - they open: tap (or click the right stick) and the top's tuck flap swings up and back, the dust flaps fold out,
    the inner tray rises and the cartridge comes up out of it.
- **Inside:**
  - Xbox One / Series: the disc is on the left, inside the front cover.
  - GameCube: an 8 cm disc on its hub.
  - Switch: the card low on the right, with the paper tabs above it.
  - DS: the card at the top and the Game Boy Advance slot under it.
  - PS2 and GameCube: a memory card holder under the manual.
  - Mega Drive and Neo Geo clamshells: the cartridge in its bed.
  - Intellivision: opens like a book, the cartridge in its plastic tray.
  - See-through cases look light inside (the plastic over the paper's white back).
- **Not invented:** Steam, Android, arcade and PICO-8 games never had retail cases, so they keep Voltcap's own case.
- **How sure each one is:** every entry is marked Measured, From a published size, Estimated or Placeholder in
  `CASES.md`.
  - Placeholders draw the nearest known case and are listed there: Famicom, Japanese N64 and GBA boxes, Pokémon
    mini, Master System and 32X sizes, Japanese Mega Drive, PAL Mega-CD, PAL Dreamcast thickness, Game Gear, the
    TurboGrafx-16 case, CD-i.
  - Not drawn yet: Platinum / Greatest Hits colours, obi strips, outer sleeves, early PS1 longboxes, late cardboard
    Mega Drive boxes.

### To check on the Thor
- The case region switch, PAL vs US PS1 depth, an Xbox One / Series disc on the left.
- A box opening (NES, SNES, Game Boy): the flap, the tray rising and the cartridge coming out.
- An Android game with your cartridge: it lies in the case as a cartridge.

### Artwork keeps downloading when Voltcap isn't on screen
- "Getting art" now carries on behind a game, behind another app and with the screen off.
- While it runs, a quiet minimum-priority notification shows the count, and it goes away when the download is done.
- Android freezes a launcher in the background; this notification keeps Voltcap awake only while it downloads.
- It no longer waits for the game to end.
- The "save the rest" pass after a scrape now really runs. It used to stop at once because it saw the scrape still
  running.

  before.

### Cases (checked on the Thor)
- **The stray lines are gone:**
  - the sleeve lip and inner rim on keep cases;
  - the hinge and lid lines on jewel cases;
  - the fold lines on boxes;
  - the white outline round every case;
  - the outlines round each part of an opened case, which made a square round the disc.

  have it on their opening edge, as the real ones do. When closed it's a recess on the edge; when open it's the
  raised strip with the dip for your thumb. Jewel cases and cartridge boxes have none, like the real ones.
- **Inside a keep case:** three curved ridges hold the disc, as moulded in a real tray, instead of a full ring. The
  manual clips sit by the hinge.
- **Out of the way:** an opened case moves aside less far; it went off the screen's left edge.
- **The PlayStation case** keeps its solid black tray ridge.

### Cartridges and cards when turned (the custom Android cartridge and every other one)
- They're solid now. Their sides are their own outline in their own colour (a green shell has a green edge, and a
  notched cartridge's edge follows the notch), drawn slice by slice through their thickness.
- From behind, their outline shows in their shell colour, taken from the picture itself.
- Before, the face only got narrower, with a grey strip floating apart from it.

### Discs
- Nothing shows in the middle any more: the disc's edge and back face showed through the hole as a grey disc with
  a line across it.
- The data side catches the light: two bright and two darker lobes, as a mirror reflects a room, with the rainbow
  bands beside them. Both turn as the disc turns. It looked flat grey before.

### Trailer
- Shot list and script are in the doc "Voltcap trailer: shot list and script".

### Cases open (game window, real cases)
- Tap the case, or click the right stick:
  - it turns to face you and the lid swings open on its hinge;
  - you see inside: the tray with the disc on its hub, or the card in its slot, and the manual in its clips, or the
    booklet in a jewel case's lid;
  - then the case moves aside and the disc or cartridge rises out to the middle, big, tilting gently (a disc spins
    slowly).
- **Drag the disc or cartridge** to turn it round; a disc shows its data side. Tap it, or tap or click again, and it
  goes back in and the case closes.
- **Each kind of case in its real colour:**
  - **Keep cases:** PS2 / GameCube / Xbox black, PS3 smoky, PS4 / Wii U blue, PS5 / Wii white, Switch red,
    Xbox 360 / One green.

  cover as its label.

  better for the others, so Voltcap draws its own cases.

### Disc undersides look like the real ones
The data side follows the disc's actual format, and its light and rainbow move as it turns.
- **CD:** bright mirror silver with fine rainbow diffraction.
- **DVD:** a little darker, with softer rainbows.
- **Dual-layer DVD:** a faint champagne tint and its layer edge.
- **Blu-ray** (PS3 / PS4 / PS5 / Xbox One / Series): cool silver with a blue-violet hint.
- **PlayStation:** deep glossy black.
- **PS2:** cobalt-blue CD-ROM or silver DVD, read from the game's image (cue/bin, ISO size, CHD header, CSO). Over
  4.7 GB it's a dual-layer DVD.
- **Dreamcast GD-ROM:** its two data areas and the darker ring between them.
- **Saturn:** the security ring near the edge.
- **GameCube:** its real 8 cm size.
- **Wii U:** a rounded edge.
- All of them have fine concentric tracks, a clear hub with the stacking ring, and the hole at its real size.

### Second screen: new "Game art" look (Settings › Screens › Second screen art & music › Look; on by default)
- **The art:** the game's art fills the screen, with its logo in the middle (its name when there's no logo) and the
  console and playtime under it.
- **Floating pills at the top:**
  - left: your picture, your points and the page you're on (tap it for the next page);
  - right: notifications, the battery (green while charging) and the time.
- **Floating dock at the bottom:** a home button (back to the first page), your apps as round icons (hold one to move
  or remove it, + adds one), all apps and settings.
- Page dots sit above the dock, and you swipe between pages as before. The other pages show on dark glass over the
  art.
- **Classic** keeps the old tabs and bar.

### Dimmed second screen stays usable
- When it dims, the game's art and logo turn black-and-white and darker; buttons, text and icons keep their
  colours at about half brightness.
- **How dark:** Light, Medium (default) or Strong.
- The backlight goes down less than before.
- The first touch still only lights it up again.

### Stick lights off with the screen
- When the screen goes off (timeout or power button), every stick light now goes off. On the Thor only the right
  one went off before.
- When the screen comes back on, your colour comes back, also during a game.
- Only when Voltcap runs the lights (Settings › Device › Controller lights not set to "System setting").

### "Getting art 1/215": found on the Thor
- **The cause:** the automatic **Details** download and the artwork both ask ScreenScraper, which answers one request
  at a time, so the art waited until every game's details were done. On the Thor it stood at 1/215 while Details went
  134/182; once Details finished, it ran to 211/215 in about two minutes.
- **The fix:** the automatic details now wait while the artwork is being looked up, so the art comes first.

### The carousel stage (the dark area the games stand on)

  run under the panel below). Settings › Home › Layout › Carousel › Game size can grow them further.
- **Spread out:** with only a few games they're spaced wider, Box flow and Spine wall most, so the sides aren't empty.
- **Endless** is on again by default (switched on once for everyone), so a carousel with few games has games on both

- **Bigger:** they fill the screen. Pixel-perfect is now **off** by default; it used to leave the Thor's screens half

- **Wall page:**

  - on the Wall itself, ◀ ▶ go along the slices and A picks.

  - consoles are shown as **Tiles** by default;
  - a row of chips switches between Tiles, Folders, Wide cards and Logos;
  - ▲ ▼ scroll through the grid, and through a console's games, so every one can be reached.
- **↩ back to the layout:** the button on the dashboard now looks like the layout's own buttons. Twin desk and Twin icons
  get a white bar with a round button; the Pocket layouts get a flat white panel with the pixel font and corner
  brackets.

### Art stuck at "Getting art 1/215"
- **Likely cause:** on a two-screen handheld Voltcap can stay "in front" the whole time a game runs on the other screen.
  It then never noticed the game had ended, and scraping (and saving art) waited for good.
- **Fix:** any button or touch on Voltcap's home now ends that game mode, after the first seconds of a launch. Getting
  focus back does the same.
- **Time limits:** every artwork request now has an overall limit (SteamGridDB, ScreenScraper, IGDB, RAWG,
  TheGamesDB, picture downloads), so a slow server can't hold a lookup open for ever.

### Playtime between devices
- **Why it didn't sync:** playtime was matched by the ROM's path under the library folder. With a console's games in
  differently named folders on the two handhelds (psx / PS1, SD card, a subfolder per game), the entries never matched,
  so each handheld kept only its own hours.
- **Now:** playtime and last played are matched by **console + file name**.
- **Your old entries:** folded together once, with the hours added up. The old paths never matched, so nothing is
  counted twice.
- Update both handhelds; the next sync (Settings › Sync) puts each game's total on both.

**Not done yet:** Real cases on the Thor (the scans not showing, the 3D cases cut off) and more case-like 3D case
models. These need a look on the Thor while it's free, and the case models are a separate job in your shape library.

- Changed (27): `src_copy\LauncherViewModel.kt`, `src_copy\data\Features.kt`, `src_copy\data\RomScanner.kt`, and in
  `src_copy\ui\`: `AnimationPreviews.kt`, `AppDrawer.kt`, `Carousel.kt`, `GameCard.kt`, `GameLookPicker.kt`,

  `StyleCaseStacks.kt`, `StyleCustom.kt`, `StyleRecordCrate.kt`.

**Files to delete:** none.

### The freeze on the Thor ("Voltcap isn't responding", 13 Oct 21:16)
- **What it was:** an ANR, not a crash. The app had been open for about 5 hours. In the last 2 minutes, every frame
  took 5–9 seconds to draw, and Android stopped it.
- **Cause:** Android 13's renderer was stuck in its text cache. Text on a part turned in 3D (a case or cartridge
  turning, a spine on a shelf, a card tilting) is never reused: each new angle adds another copy. Over hours, finding
  the right copy took longer than the frame.
- **Fix:** every part that turns in 3D (25 places) is now drawn flat first and only that picture is turned
  (`flatTextFor3d`). This includes the media beside a case in "Case + its media", the Game shelf's resting turn, Case
  stacks' spines, Card binder, Record crate, Grid, inspect view, the launch throw, the custom layouts' turn and flip,
  and more.
- Earlier fixes had already done this for some places. These were the ones left.

### The controller on the second screen
- ▼ past the bottom of the main screen moves the controller onto the second screen: past the games, the round
  buttons and the music player.
- **On the second screen:**
  - The lit control has an accent ring, and a note at the top says the controller is there.
  - ◀ ▶ ▲ ▼ move to the nearest control that way: page arrows, page tabs, dock, round buttons, apps, console folders,
    games in a folder, achievement filters, and the popup menus.
  - A presses the lit control.
  - B, or ▲ at the top, goes back up.
- Picking a game or an app there sends the controller back to the main screen.

### Multi-disc games and duplicates (Settings › Library › ROM folders › Library check)
- **What other frontends do:** ES-DE treats a folder named `Game.m3u` that holds the discs and a `Game.m3u` playlist
  as one game. Voltcap already reads that.
- **Multi-disc games without a playlist:**
  - Each is now one game, started from disc 1.
  - Library check lists them (name · console · how many discs · folder).
  - **Make the .m3u files** writes them all, then scans again.
  - Before, the scan wrote them by itself without saying. That's now a switch, **Make .m3u files by themselves**, off by
    default.
- **Discs in their own folders** (`Game (Disc 1)/…`, `Game (Disc 2)/…`) are grouped in the folder above.
- **Duplicates:**
  - The same game in two formats side by side (`Game.cue` and `Game.chd`, `.iso` and `.zip`) is listed once, in the
    best format (CHD first, archives last). The other copy is named in Library check.
  - One file reached two ways counts once: `/sdcard` and `/storage/emulated/0`, `ROMs/psx` and `ROMs/PSX`, or one ROM
    folder inside another.
  - The same game in two different folders stays listed twice, and both paths are shown so you can tidy up.

### Looks greyed out where they do nothing
- These layouts draw their games their own way: Console hub, Resume, Channel grid, Hero tiles, Twin icons (tiles);
  Live tiles and Twin desk (wide tiles); Game shelf; Disc station; Record crate; Card binder; Arcade cabinets.
- In those layouts:
  - **R1 › Look** is greyed out. Tapping it says why.
  - In **Settings › Game look**, the look, cartridge and case chips are greyed out and can't be picked, with a note.

### Second screen Games page (Settings › Screens › Second screen Games page)
- **Consoles look like:** Folders (as before), Tiles, Wide cards or Logos.
- **Folder pack:**
  - Import a zip, or put the pictures in `Voltcap/Folders` on the handheld.
  - The rule: pictures are named after the console, with the same names as ROM folders (`snes.png`, `psx.png`,
    `gba.webp`, `megadrive.jpg`…).
  - iiSU-style names work too (`snes_list.png`, `snes_title.png`), so packs made for iiSU or ES-DE can be dropped in.
    The packs aren't bundled.
  - `_default.png` is used for every console without its own picture.
- **A picture for one console:** pick one from the handheld for any console. It comes before the pack.
- **Console logo over pictures:** on or off.

### Check after installing
- On the Thor, leave Voltcap open on the Case stacks or Game shelf layout: it should stay smooth.
- ▼▼▼ to the bottom: the ring appears on the lower screen. Move around, press A on a folder, then a game.
- Library check after a scan.
- R1 › Layout › Disc station: the Look tile is greyed out.

## Update — 13 Oct 2026 (176): Custom layouts — make your own animated home screens, import and share them

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`.

**Copy `src_copy`** (into `app\src\main\java\com\shelf\launcher\`):

- New (3): `src_copy\data\CustomLayouts.kt`, `src_copy\ui\StyleCustom.kt`, `src_copy\ui\CustomLayoutSettings.kt`.
- Changed (7): `src_copy\data\AppearanceStore.kt`, `src_copy\data\Features.kt`, `src_copy\ui\OptionIcons.kt`,
  `src_copy\ui\PresetPreview.kt`, `src_copy\ui\PresetsCard.kt`, `src_copy\ui\StyleHomeSettings.kt`,
  `src_copy\ui\StyleHomes.kt`.

**New in the project (not app code):**

- `docs\CUSTOM_LAYOUTS.md`: the tutorial.
- `docs\layouts\neon-drift\layout.json` and `docs\layouts\side-list\layout.json`: two examples.
- `docs\layouts\neon-drift.vclayout` and `docs\layouts\side-list.vclayout`: the same examples, ready to import.

**Files to delete:** none.

### Custom layout (Settings › Home › Layout › Custom layout)
- A new layout that draws a layout file anyone can make. A `.vclayout` is a zip with a `layout.json` and its pictures.
- **Parts:**
  - `games`: the moving games, as a row, a column or an arc, in the card look, covers, square or wide.
  - `art`: the game you're on, as its backdrop, cover, wide art, logo, screenshot or card.
  - Text parts: `title`, `info`, `text` (with `{name}`, `{playtime}`, `{time}`… filled in), `clock` and `category`.
  - `image`: your own picture. **Animated GIF and WebP pictures play.**
  - `shape`: a panel, line or dot, with a colour or gradient and a border.
  - `buttons`: Play / Continue and Details.
- Positions are shares of the screen (0–1), so a layout fits the Classic's 4:3 screen and the Thor's 16:9 screen alike.
- **Motion:**
  - Every part can have a `loop` that keeps going: float, sway, drift, spin, rock, pulse, blink or turn.
  - Every part can also have an `enter` motion, played each time you move to another game: fade, four slides, zoom,
    pop, flip or spin. Delays let parts arrive one after another.
- **Background:** a colour or gradient, the game's art with a shade, and your picture on top (it can have its own
  loop).
- **D-pad:**
  - Row / arc: ◀ ▶ through the games, ▼ to the buttons, ▲ to what lies above.
  - Column: ▲ ▼ through the games, ▶ to the buttons, ◀ back.
  - Tap a game to pick it, and again to open it.
- It starts with the built-in example, **Neon drift**: a curved row along the bottom, the name and buttons on the
  left, the logo floating at the top right.

### Layout options (while Custom layout is picked)
- **Layouts:** pick one, see who made it, and delete the imported ones.
- **Import a file:** a `.vclayout`, a `.zip` or a bare `layout.json`.
- **Import from Voltcap/Layouts:** everything in that folder on the handheld (`.vclayout` files, or folders with a
  `layout.json`). The folder is made if it's missing. Importing again replaces layouts with the same name, so this is
  the quick way to try your edits.
- **Save the example:** saves Neon drift as a `.vclayout` to start from.
- **How to make one:** the step-by-step guide in the app. The full tutorial is `docs\CUSTOM_LAYOUTS.md`.
- A mistake in `layout.json` is reported with what's wrong (for example "part 3: unknown type…"), and the layout isn't
  imported. Missing pictures are named.
- **Safety:** a layout is only a description, nothing in it runs. Only `layout.json` and pictures are taken from the
  zip, flattened into the layout's own folder (nothing is written outside it). The limits are 80 files and 48 MB.

### Check after installing
- R1 › hold Layout › Custom layout: Neon drift with your games.
  - ◀ ▶ slide the arc, and the name, info and logo come in each time.
  - ▼ goes to Play / Details.
- Layout options › Import a file › `side-list.vclayout` (copy it over from `docs\layouts\`): a column of wide pictures
  down the left. ▲ ▼ move, ▶ goes to the buttons.

## Update — 13 Oct 2026 (175): R1 Carousel tile steps through the views, PS3 game folders as one game, faster scraping

`src_copy\ui\QuickSettings.kt`.

**Files to delete:** none.

### R1 › Carousel tile
- A tap now turns the carousel on when it's off, and after that each tap moves to the next view (Tucked behind, Record
  flip, Wheel … Box flow) and round again. It used to turn the carousel off.
- To turn it off: hold the tile › **Carousel off** (new, at the end of the list).
- Picking a 3D-case view by tapping also turns on its glossy floor, the same as picking it from the list.

### PS3 games in folders (seen on the Thor)
- A folder with `PS3_GAME` or `PS3_DISC.SFB` inside is now one game. Its files (EBOOT.BIN, ICON0.PNG, PARAM.SFO, the
  DAT files…) are no longer listed as games, and the folder isn't searched further.
- The name comes from the game's `PARAM.SFO`. Without one, it's the folder's name without ".iso" and its serial
  (`UFC Undisputed 3 BLES01231` → "UFC Undisputed 3").
- On the Thor, both kinds are found: `ROMs/ps3/UFC Undisputed 3 BLES01231/` and the TNA game inside a folder named
  `….iso/` (with "Vimm's Lair.txt" next to it).
- Files that are never games are skipped everywhere: texts, pictures, web pages, checksums, PS3 system files (txt, nfo,
  pdf, png, jpg, sfo, sfb, pup, edat, rap, sprx, md5, sfv…). ".md" stays a Genesis game.
- Launching: aPS3e gets the folder's path in its `game_dir` extra (the way ES-DE starts a folder game). The single-file
  `.iso` games still go as before.

### Faster scraping
- **Artwork:** four games are looked up at once instead of one after another.
- **Details:** three at once, with a short pause in each lane (0.25 s) instead of 0.6 s after every game.
- **Settings › Scraping › Fetch everything:** artwork and details now run together, with one count. Cases, screenshots
  and clips take three games at once, with no half-second wait between games.
- **ScreenScraper:** still never goes over your account's limit. Free accounts stay one request at a time. An account
  allowed more threads (ScreenScraper reports "maxthreads" in every answer) now gets that many at once, up to 4, with the
  1.2 s gap shared between them.

### Check after installing
- On the Thor: the PS3 row shows two games (UFC Undisputed 3, TNA Impact!), and both start in aPS3e.
- R1 › tap Carousel a few times: the views change. Hold › Carousel off turns it off.
- Settings › Scraping › Re-scrape: art arrives in bigger steps.

### What changed
- **Volume mixer on the Pocket Classic** (Spotify playing at 0 %): checked on the Classic with a game and Spotify
  playing. The Classic has the vendor's root service (PServerBinder, like the AYN Thor), the mixer helper starts through
  it and sees every player (Spotify's two with volume handles), and setting a volume works — run once over USB it muted
  Spotify at once. But the background helper that keeps the volumes (the "Volume keeper" in Mixer check) is ended by the
  firmware right after its start, so nothing stayed turned down. Now, once the keeper is seen gone twice, Voltcap
  remembers it and uses the one-shot way instead — the same as the VolumeManager app you found, without Shizuku: each
  time Android reports a player starting or changing (a game starting, Spotify's next track), the helper runs once, puts
  the volumes on every player of the apps you turned down, and ends. A player keeps that volume. Mixer check shows
  "Volume keeper ✓ This firmware ends it, so the volumes are put on each player as it starts". (No pairing or Wireless
  debugging needed after all.)
- **Lists in the Cross menu:** Cross menu options › Lists in the strip — Continue playing, Favourites, Most played, In
  progress, Almost mastered, Mastered, Never played, Not played lately, Emulators, Collections, All games: the ones you
  tick show as icons beside the consoles on the Cross menu only, even when they're hidden in Settings › Categories (their
  order is set there).

  bare 3D case in Box flow, Arc, Spine wall, Turned row (and with the 3D cases switch): now the disc stands half out of
  the case behind it (spinning), or the cartridge / disc leans against its lower right, turning with the case.

## Update — 13 Oct 2026 (162): the carousel as a physical collection, inspecting a game's piece, presets brought up to date

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`.

**Copy `src_copy`** (into `app\src\main\java\com\shelf\launcher\`):
- New (2): `src_copy\ui\MediaInspect.kt`, `src_copy\ui\MediaInspectView.kt`.
- Changed (9): `src_copy\data\LayoutPresets.kt`, and `src_copy\ui\` Carousel, Case3D, GameWindow, HomeExtras, PresetPreview,
  PresetsCard, SettingsDialog, StyleHomeSettings (all `.kt`).

**Files to delete:** none. (161 and 160 come with this block if they aren't installed yet.)

### The carousel (every view; Box flow tuned to the loader videos)
- **Each game as its own piece:** the 3D views box only the case looks; with Cartridges & discs, Cartridges, Discs only
  or 3D models every game stays its real cartridge, card, disc, UMD or model, in its own shape. Turned pieces show
  their thickness (an edge in the shell's colour; discs a thin rim), so a cartridge seen from the side doesn't vanish.
  In mixed-console lists every piece gets about a cover's area, so nothing jumps in size.
- **Box flow:** the middle one facing you a touch higher, a gap the width of its piece, then the stacks a step behind
  on a gentle curve, turned more toward the edges (spines showing more), standing on one floor line; the right stack
  draws each one over the one inside it, so the spines show. Spine wall and Turned row got the same floor and easing.
- **Motion:** the whole carousel runs from one moving position — a smooth spring at your "Moving between games" speed
  that keeps its speed between steps, so holding the D-pad flows instead of stopping at every game; the game leaving
  the middle eases into its stack. No snapping when the list changes. The carousel no longer rebuilds every frame while
  it moves, and the focus pulse runs on the game you're on only.
- **Category change:** the old collection slides on along the carousel and fades while the new one comes in from the
  side you went (off with Lite effects or page animations off).
- **Real case fronts** in the Box art / Real cases looks' 3D cases (Original cases on).
- Settings › Carousel › 3D cases: now says it's for the case looks.

### Opening a game: inspecting its piece
- With a look that draws real things (cases, cartridges, cards, discs, 3D models, or covers drawn as 3D cases), opening
  a game lifts its piece out of the carousel: the others step back and fade, the piece flies forward and grows on one
  side of the window, then turns once — front, side, back — and settles facing you. The game's buttons and info sit
  beside it, never over it.
  - Boxes: the front scan (or cover), the spine, the back cut from the full box scan (else plain plastic, never the
    cover mirrored). Cartridges and cards: the label, a shell-coloured side, a plain rear shell. Discs: the label, a thin
    edge, the silver data side. 3D models: through their own angles.
  - The right stick, or dragging the piece, turns it yourself; let go and it eases back.
- Closing turns it back, shrinks it and flies it back exactly into its place; the same game stays selected.
- Animations off / Lite effects: a short fade instead. Covers and wide capsules open as before.

### Presets (Settings › Home › Layout & presets)

     (a debug build is made for debugging, not speed). The release build (`installRelease`) is compiled and optimised.

  instead of "on this device".

**Copy `project_copy`:** `project_copy\app\src\main\keepRules\rules.keep`, `project_copy\app\build.gradle.kts`,
`project_copy\tools\adb_mcp\server.js` (all changed).

**Files to delete:** none.

### What changed
- **The signed (release) APK crashed at start ("keeps stopping" on the RP Classic).** Found by installing a renamed copy
  of your signed APK on the Odin and reading the crash: R8 (the release build's shrinker) had removed the constructor of
  WorkManager's database, which is created by reflection. `rules.keep` now keeps it and the other classes those
  libraries create by name. Debug builds were never affected.
- **Signing:** `keystore.properties` pointed to the folder `Documenti\Voltcap` instead of the key file in it. The block
  in the chat found the key and fixed the path. `build.gradle.kts` now falls back to the debug key (with a warning) when
  the key file isn't there, instead of stopping the build.
- **Google Drive at the very first start:** the first-start setup's Welcome step now offers "Yes — from Google Drive"
  (signs in to Drive, takes back everything and restarts) next to "Yes — from a backup file…". Settings › Backup has
  "Export to Google Drive" next to Export (the same backup with the parts you ticked, into My Drive › Voltcap ›
  voltcap-backup.json).
- **Trophy count over the cases:** a case, cartridge or disc keeps room at its top for the count when it sits at the
  top (Achievements › Trophy count); every such card the same, so they stay one size.
- **Picture in your own case templates:** it fills the case's window again (the Android case had empty strips at the
  sides); only a picture that would lose more than 15 % (square or wide art) is fitted whole. Same for 3D-model labels.
- **Mastered shimmer:** it froze 30 s after the last button press (the home screen's idle pause). It now has its own
  clock that keeps going (at half the rate) while idle and only stops after 3 minutes.
- **adb tool:** `install_apk`, `push` and `pull`, so Claude can install test builds on a handheld (after a restart of the
  Claude app).

### What changed
- **The Voltcap row slides again (normal view, not carousel).** Recorded on the Odin with the screen recorder (a frame
  every 8 ms): the whole row jumped to its new place in one frame — every card's own spring never ran. The row now glides
  with one shared position, the way the carousel does (Settings › Home › Animations › Moving between games sets the
  speed), and the room the game you're on takes glides along too. In the carousel the name line now starts at the left
  (it was centred and ran under the game's big logo, cutting off the play time).
- **Cases all one height.** A case with its disc (Case + disc) or with its cartridge / disc beside it used to shrink so
  both fitted in its place — smaller than cases with nothing beside them (your Android case). Now every case is as big as
  a case on its own; the disc sticks out to the right, behind the next game. The row leaves room after the game you're on
  so its disc shows whole. "Cases · real sizes" uses the real size for the case itself (the disc no longer shrinks it),
  and 3D-model cases follow real sizes too.
- **Settings is slimmer.** The header is one bar (title, a one-line description, search, ✕), the window is taller, and the
  Close button floating under the settings is gone (✕ and B close). About twice as many rows show on the Odin.
- **One signing key for every build** (app\build.gradle.kts): with `keystore.properties` (your release key), the debug
  builds Android Studio installs are signed with it too, so they, the GitHub releases and the in-app updater install over
  each other. Your RP Classic couldn't install the signed APK because it had the debug-signed Voltcap (a different key).
  `release.ps1` now also updates `project_copy\app\build.gradle.kts`, so a robocopy no longer puts the old version back.
- **Code on GitHub:** `.gitignore` keeps off GitHub: Discord's SDK (`app\libs\discord`, files up to 290 MB and not ours to
  share), `src_copy`, `project_copy`, `Claude outputs`, `screens`, logs. `setup_github.ps1` sets git up once (see below).

**Bug check — every file read (460 files, 132,000 lines), 75 findings, 72 confirmed by a second check and fixed:**
- *Saved art:* the image cache sat in the same folder as your saved art, so a damaged cache journal (a crash, or Voltcap
  killed when a game starts) wiped all saved art. The cache now has its own `cache` folder (moved there once). Finding a
  saved picture no longer touches the disk on the main thread (a list in memory).
- *SteamGridDB:* starting without Wi-Fi said the saved key "stopped working" and switched automatic art off until a
  restart. Now it's kept and checked again a little later; only a real refusal says the key is wrong.
- *Crashes / freezes:* an early exit out of a Column (game header's achievements, RomM browser) that can crash; the
  charge-limit service could crash Voltcap when its notification failed; the RetroAchievements game lists were read and
  indexed on the main thread (the home froze while matching ran).
- *Settings transfer / sync:* this handheld's sync id travelled with "Share settings", so two handhelds wiped each other's
  play from the recaps — each device now keeps its own (made new once; the old one is cleaned off Google Drive). Sleep
  mode's state no longer travels, and Wi-Fi / Bluetooth are checked after waking and switched on another way if needed.
- *Undo after one of your own presets* now puts back the whole home screen, not only about 45 settings.
- *Mixer:* turning Spotify down changed the volume of whatever Spotify Connect device was playing (speaker, PC) — now
  only this handheld; the mixer tile ignores apps that were uninstalled.
- *First setup:* B / a tap outside on any step ended the whole setup — now it goes back a step. The Extra art step shows
  your choice.
- *Home and looks:* console badge drawn over the favourite star / Open tag / game-state mark; Spine wall carousel lost
  every game aside except with 3D cases; hero backdrop showing the previous game blurred; Icon bar name over the big
  tile; Spotlight cards acting on the previous game; Dashboard quick access repeating the menu's shortcuts; corner
  shortcuts' ✕ that did nothing; news card stealing the D-pad; game window text unreadable on a light accent.
- *Other:* crash screen buttons squeezed off on small screens; achievement unlock times shown in UTC; new-unlock stage
  squashing many badges; lyric cloud ignoring Timing; guide reader running Back twice; guide ids colliding; Edit Home
  drag restarting on resize; folded overlay that couldn't be unfolded; RA comments saying "sign in" when offline; RomM
  browser keeping the old console's games; player pages white on light skins; second-screen trackpad dot never moving,
  wall toolbar's Reset / Done squeezed away, apps drawer letting taps through; widget sizes too big; Save Vault PS2 saves
  synced from another device showing 0 B; emulator names ("Genshin" shown as "eden (Optimized)").
- *Text:* every label, hint and note that started with a lower-case letter now starts with a capital ("<1 min" instead
  of "under a minute", "Missable", "Off", "Crisp", "✓ Connected", "Target 60 fps"…).
- *Tidied:* about 300 unused lines in the details window, unused options parameters, the unused MetadataPanel.

## Update — 12 Oct 2026 (140): The cartridge, spine and disc packs rebuilt for dzepdzep/Voltcap

All paths below are on your PC under `C:\Users\User\AndroidStudioProjects\ShelfLauncher\`.

**Copy `project_copy`** (over the project root). No code changed.
- New (152), all in `project_copy\packs\v1\`:
  - `carts_<console>.zip` (64), e.g. `project_copy\packs\v1\carts_snes.zip`;
  - `carts_CREDITS.txt` (the collection's README and its CC0 licence);
  - `spine_<name>.webp` (60), e.g. `project_copy\packs\v1\spine_snes.webp`;
  - `disc_<name>.webp` (27), e.g. `project_copy\packs\v1\disc_playstation.webp`.

**Files to delete:** none.

### What changed
- The cartridge, spine and disc-console packs from 131 were made for `thebigpocket/Voltcap`, which isn't your account, so they were never anywhere the app can reach. They are rebuilt from your originals in Downloads:
  - `Downloads\cartridges\<shape>\<opaque|translucent>\png\<console>.png` → 1,792 pictures, lossless WebP, packed as one zip per console: `<shape>/<o|t>/<console>.webp` (14 shapes × opaque / clear = 28 per zip);

### What changed

**Your 3D shape library as a look** (`ui\Models3D.kt`, Settings › Game look › Covers, cases & discs › **3D models**)
- All 81 models (real cartridges and cards, your custom cartridges, the clear ones, memory cards, the SD card, every case and disc), with their logos as they are.
- Pre-rendered, as you picked: each model from 7 angles (−60° to +60°, every 20°), in a small renderer I wrote for it (same light, gloss and clear tinted plastic for every model). The game's cover goes into the model's art window at whatever angle, lit and tinted like the model (through the clear plastic too). It costs drawing two pictures, so it's light on the handheld.
- **Off / Real / Custom / Clear:**
  - **Real:** each console's real cartridge or card (GB, GBC, GBA, N64, SNES, Super Famicom, Mega Drive / Genesis, Game Gear, WonderSwan, DS, 3DS, Switch), and the real case for disc consoles (PS1 jewel, PS2, PS3, PS4, GameCube, Wii, Wii U as Blu-ray, Xbox, Xbox 360, Dreamcast, Saturn, PSP, Sega CD as the long box…).
  - **Custom:** your custom cartridges (also the PlayStation, PlayStation 2, GameCube, Dreamcast and PSP ones); consoles without a custom one get their real piece.
  - **Clear:** the custom cartridges in tinted clear plastic (the board shows inside).
- Consoles without a piece of their own (PC, Android, Steam, arcade…) keep their usual look. The SD card and the memory cards are for the Save Vault (below).
- **Name on the label** (same place, a toggle, off by default): the game's name on a dark strip along the bottom of the label, drawn into the label so it follows the angle and the light. It costs nothing extra (it's made with the picture, once).
- **Stand:** turned a little with the game you're on facing you (default), all turned, or all straight on.
- Where it shows: the **Cartridges & discs** look (every row and grid, the game window), and the carousels' **3D cases** (Arc, Spine wall, Turned row, or the 3D cases switch): there each game is its model, at the angle nearest its turn.
- The pictures are a download (Extra art packs › **3D models**), like your other packs; until it's there, nothing changes.

**Art drop** (like your Unifideck screenshot; **R1 › Art drop**, and Settings › Game look › Covers, cases & discs)
- How far the cover drops below the top: in the Box art looks, below the case template's top band (up to 15 % of the case); in the 3D models look, below the top of the model's window.
- Each look keeps its own value (Box art one, 3D models another).
- The R1 tile shows only on those looks. Pick it and a slider appears along the bottom of the screen, under the game you're on, without dimming it, so you see the cover move while you change it (◀ ▶ step it). Reset puts it back to 0.

**Save Vault: 3D cards** (Save Vault › Settings › Style › **3D card**)
- Each save is your 3D memory card or SD card, the game's cover on its label and its name on the label's strip; the save you're on faces you, the others are turned a little.
- Pick the card under it: SD card, Black, Blue, Green, Red or Smoke card, and **Clear** for the see-through ones.

- The games beside the middle one at their normal size, side by side with a small gap, no tilt and hardly any shade; only the game you're on pops out a little (a quarter bigger).
- With Games each side › **To the edge** (the default) the row runs past both screen edges; or pick 1–5 each side.

**The wide capsule, fixed in place** (Voltcap row, game you're on = wide capsule, on the left)

**N64 and Atomiswave badges:** the symbol badges were too thin to see. The two pictures have their outlines filled in, and every symbol badge is drawn bigger and bolder in its pill.

**Volume mixer** (Settings › Device › Volume mixer)
- Volumes not changing:
  - On your AYN handhelds the firmware moves a per-app sound effect onto the whole output ("session 0"), so Automatic (sound effect) did nothing per app. Voltcap now checks whether its effects really sit on each app's own session; when they don't, it switches to Player volume for that handheld by itself and says so in Mixer check.
  - Player volume worked once and then hung: starting the helper waited forever for the root service, holding the mixer. It now starts in the background and returns at once, so later changes go through.
- The mixer's own screen (and the R1 quick menu, the overlay controls, the pin-shortcut screen) no longer have a black strip where the navigation bar was.

**Navigation bar hiding** (Settings › Device › Gesture hint › **Force-hide gesture hint**)
- On AYN firmware, the white gesture line comes from the system's second home handle even with the bar hidden. Force-hide now also uses AYN's own "hide navigation bar" setting (it's tried first). Turn it on there to test.

**Visual sweep, every layout and look** (seen on your Odin 2 Portal)
- **Text everywhere:**
  - Words that shrink to fit never get smaller than 10 sp any more (they went down to 6–7 sp, e.g. the TV room's info strip) — 282 places.
  - Two-line names and descriptions keep their line spacing when they shrink (it was fixed and made lines overlap) — 25 files.
  - Hero carousel: the description's spacing.
- **Status bar:** a soft shade along its edge, so the clock, icons and points read over a bright picture.
- **Dashboard:** a dark shade behind the menu and the title down the left (white words vanished over a yellow cover); the subtitle lifted if the accent is dark; Now playing has a shade along its bottom so "Last played" and the button read; the button's text is dark on a light accent; "MASTERED" on the small covers was cut to "MASTE" — narrow covers now show the trophy alone, or "65/65".
- **Side menu:** the menu's buttons get shorter to fit instead of the last one ("Help") showing cut in half.
- **Spotlight (Home menu):** long names under the tile you're on (two lines) didn't show at all; they do now.
- **Live tiles:** no more lower-case labels ("all apps", "search", the category names, "sep 24").
- **Cross menu, Icon bar, Live tiles:** "Last played: Sep 24, 2026" (the date was lower case).
- **Icon bar, Console hub, Resume & discover, Dashboard, Spotlight, Side menu, Game shelf:** a game you've played without recorded time said "Never played" next to its last-played date; it now says "Under a minute".
- **Console hub and Resume & discover:** their own clock and battery showed under the status bar's (two clocks); now they show only when the status bar is off; the achievements sliding behind the Achievements card fade out above its title instead of running through it.
- **Game shelf:** the game you pull out used to cover the spines next to it (most of a short shelf); the games either side now slide apart to make room and close up again.
- **TV room:** the hidden "badges" part left an empty frame; the progress bars were empty (no height).

  - The Voltcap row's, Tiles' and Hero carousel's own carousels keep their flat cards (they only use the Tucked layout).

**Faster spines** (the lag on spine shelves)
- Before, every spine on screen decoded and flattened its own copy of the console's spine picture while the screen was being drawn. A shelf of 40 games did that 40 times.
- Now each console's spine is made once, away from the screen's thread, and kept.
  - That covers the bookcase, Spines look, TV room, the 3D boxes and the new 3D cases.
- The titled spines (your console spine with the game's name) for the 3D boxes and cases are also made in the background and kept (up to about 24 MB).
- For the moment a spine is first being made, a plain dark strip shows in its place.

### What changed

**"Only for this layout"** (Settings › Home, the first card: **Save changes for**)
- Two choices:
  - **All layouts** (as before);
  - **Only <the layout on screen>**: what you change in Settings › Home from then on is kept for that layout alone. Every other layout keeps the shared setting.
- When you switch layouts, the layout you leave gives the shared settings back and the one you go to brings its own.
- A setting a layout has its own value for, changed somewhere else while that layout is on screen (an R1 tile, say), stays that layout's own.
- With All layouts picked, changing a setting that this layout has its own value for makes it follow the shared one again.
- The card says how many settings the layout has of its own. **Use the shared settings here again** drops them all.
- Each time you leave Settings › Home it's back on All layouts, so you never keep saving for one layout by accident.

**Edit Home**
- **Stretchable parts:** every part has two new handles, ↔ in the middle of its right edge (wider) and ↕ in the middle of its bottom edge (taller). What's inside stretches with it.
  - The same is in the part's ✎ Style as **Stretch wider** / **Stretch taller** sliders, 50–250 %, so it works with a controller too (L3 opens Style).
  - X (Reset position) and Y (Reset layout) undo stretches too. So do Settings › Home › Move & resize › Put everything back, and Reset style.
  - The round corner handle still makes the whole part bigger or smaller.
- **Style from the resize handle:** a tap on the round corner handle (without dragging) opens that part's ✎ Style.
- **Less see-through:** the backings behind the parts (layout colours, theme colours, dark glass, and a part's own "Dark glass") now have a dark layer under them.
  - How strong it is: **Backing**, 0–100 %, default 70. 0 is as see-through as they were before.
  - Where: Settings › Home › Layout options › Game info on screen › Backing, and in each part's ✎ Style as **Backing (every part)**.
- **Transparency slider:** in each part's ✎ Style, **See-through (this part)** is a slider now (20 % to Solid) instead of five steps.

### Check
- **Type-check:** 0 errors (a full compile with code generation).
- **Dex marker:** I searched every compiled class for `NON_LOCAL_RETURN`, and none has it.
- **Your PC's copies:** the 6 files, `SUMMARY.md` and `HANDOVER.md` were staged fresh first; all are byte-identical to what 132 delivered. Writes only go through if the file on your PC hasn't changed since.
- **Reread** every change line by line in the diffs.
- **Bug check:**
  - Switching layouts:
    - the layout's own settings are noted before the switch is saved;
    - the shared values come back only where the switch didn't bring another value itself (each layout's parked card size, say);
    - the look settings are read again after the next layout's own ones go in, so the screen shows them at once.
  - Never kept for one layout: the layout itself, the parked looks, device and account settings.
  - Stretch is drawn the same way on moved parts, unmoved parts in the layout, and the layouts' own parts. The touch zones go in this order: ✕, the corner handle, then the stretch handles, then moving.
  - A tap on the corner handle opens Style only when it didn't move.
- **Not tested on a device:**
  - all of it, especially switching back and forth between two layouts with their own settings, and stretching a part with text in it.
- **Note:** Edit Home itself closes Settings. So to keep a moved part for one layout only, move it while that layout is on screen, then open Settings › Home with "Only …" picked and move it again (or change any setting of it there).

**Spotlight: the Home menu look** (built from your blue home-menu screenshot; now Spotlight's default look; Row & menu and Big picture are still there under Settings › Home › Layout options › Spotlight options › Look)
- **Along the very top:**
  - your profile (picture, name, points) on the left;
  - your shortcuts as plain icons spread across the middle;
  - the battery and a big clock on the right.
  
  A thin line runs under them. On an icon (▲), its name shows in capitals in a gap in that line, right under it.
- **The status bar steps aside on this look,** so the menu really sits at the very top. If you want it anyway, turn on Spotlight options › **Status bar**; the menu then leaves out its own battery and clock.
- **The row of big tiles:** the one you're on is bigger and framed, with the game's name in capitals centred under it (two lines at most). Tile shape still comes from Spotlight options › Tiles along the top.
- **Along the bottom: what the buttons do,** with the buttons drawn in your button style (Xbox letters, Nintendo letters or PlayStation shapes):
  - **A** Open (or Play / Continue / Details: whatever A does for you);
  - **X** Favourite / Remove favourite (Close game while the game is still open);
  - **Y** Achievements (only for games with achievements);
  - **Start** Options;
  - **Select** Menu.
  
  Each hint is also a button: tap it, or ▼ then ◀ ▶ and A. They stand in for the legend on this look. Spotlight options › **Button hints along the bottom** turns them off (the legend comes back).
- The other looks' options (big title, cards, category names …) are hidden while Home menu is picked.

**Cross menu: Trophies category**
- A new **Trophies** icon in the Cross menu's strip lists every game with achievements, last played first.
- Under the one you're on: "earned / total achievements · %", a progress bar, and "A: its achievements".
- **A** opens that game's achievements straight away, in the menu's own trophy column (from 127; ▲ ▼ through them, B back). Any other layout doesn't have the category; if you switch layouts while in it, you land on All.
- Settings:
  - on / off: Settings › Home › Layout options › Cross menu options › **Trophies category** (on by default);
  - its place in the strip: Settings › Categories › Category order, where it's listed as "Trophies (Cross menu only)". It starts at the end of the strip.

**The game popup's achievements page** (the game window: Achievements, on every layout except the Cross menu)
- **Order** (the first row; A steps through them, and it stays for every game):
  - Set order;
  - Still to get first;
  - Earned first;
  - Latest earned first;
  - Most points first;
  - Rarest first.
- **A on an achievement** opens it under itself:
  - all of what it asks;
  - when you earned it (and if hardcore);
  - how many players have it, and whether it's missable;
  - the comments people left on its RetroAchievements page (up to 8, newest first).
  
  A again closes it.

- The arrows now follow what's on screen: ▼ from the board → Play (the power switch), ▼ from Play → Settings, ◀ ▶ between Settings and Details, ▲ from Settings / Details → Play, ▲ from Play → back to the board. (▼ from Play used to do nothing, so only ◀ ▶ got you away from it.)

**Blur without blocks**
- Blurred pictures made once and stretched (second screen, Showcase scenes, music screensaver, lyric themes) are now made at a size that suits the blur: a light blur used a 64-px copy stretched 15–20 times, which showed blocks.
- "Whole picture" (Settings › Home › Layout options › Background picture): the soft copy round the picture is now blurred with Lite effects on as well (it was a tiny unblurred copy stretched over the screen).
- Apps with no art: the enlarged icon behind them is blurred into the picture, so it's soft on every Android version and with Lite effects (it was a small icon blown up).
- The Glass showcase's frosted panes are really blurred now (they were a tiny copy stretched ten times).

**Cross menu folders**
- At start-up the icon strip now waits until the consoles have loaded (at most 2.5 s with no consoles), so Last played and Apps no longer show first with the folders popping in after.
- The folders' console logos are decoded ahead, so a folder sliding into the strip has its logo at once.

**Game shelf: no lag going over many games**
- Scrolling the shelf no longer rebuilds every shelf and spine on every frame (only a shelf coming into view is built), the pull-out animation only redraws the game coming out, and each shelf's games are found once instead of searching all games for every shelf on every frame.

**Dashboard:** the middle (Now playing, the row and Quick access) is half way stronger than the side panels. Settings › Home › Layout options › Dashboard options › **Panel strength** still sets both.

**Side menu (and Resume, Dashboard): the first game can be reached**
- ◀ on the first game only goes into the menu on a new press at least about a quarter of a second after you landed on that game. Before, the stick's quick nudges (and a fast second press) went straight past the first game into the menu.
